**Matched-resolution tolerance curves on all three lineage checkpoints, both modes.** Same instrument, same cohort protocol, same ε grid, three seeds per point; each mode normalised by its own clean-to-mean-ablated gap. Recovery at three points on the curve:

| checkpoint | mode | ε = 0.10 | ε = 0.40 | ε = 0.80 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Llama-2-7b (base) | text | +0.993 | **+0.631** | +0.212 |
| Llama-2-7b (base) | protein | +0.910 | **−0.528** | −2.667 |
| ProLLaMA S1 (protein CPT) | text | +0.920 | **+0.208** | −0.257 |
| ProLLaMA S1 (protein CPT) | protein | +0.951 | **+0.362** | −1.049 |
| ProLLaMA S2 (instruction) | text | +0.974 | **+0.491** | −0.185 |
| ProLLaMA S2 (instruction) | protein | +0.929 | **+0.182** | −1.291 |

**The mode gap at ε = 0.40 changes sign twice along the lineage.** The base model favours text by **+1.159**; after protein continued pretraining the ordering **reverses** and protein leads by **0.154**; after instruction tuning it reverses **again** and text leads by **0.309**.

**Each stage trades one mode's robustness for the other's, and each trades in the direction its data would predict.** Protein continued pretraining moves text from +0.631 to +0.208 and protein from −0.528 to +0.362 — it buys protein robustness and pays for it in text. Instruction tuning, which adds **no protein data**, moves text back up to +0.491 and protein down to +0.182. **Neither stage improves both modes, and neither degrades both.**

**Why this is worth more than the standalone panel could say.** These are one architecture, one tokenizer, one parameter count and one weight lineage; the only thing that varies is what was trained and when. A robustness difference between two standalone models could be modality, corpus, tokenizer, scale, or lab. Here it can only be the training stage, and the trade-off is visible as a sign change rather than a magnitude difference.

**It also explains the EXP-R2-159 reading rather than merely confirming it.** That entry recorded, on Stage 1, that the protein mode is the more robust of the two and read it as evidence against a modality account. The lineage now shows this is a *stage-dependent* property of that checkpoint and not a standing fact about the model family: the same architecture reading the same two modalities orders them differently before protein pretraining, after it, and after instruction tuning. **No ordering of the two modes is a property of the model; it is a property of the checkpoint.**

**Bounds, and one that governs the high-ε column.** The protein mode's denominator on these arms is 1.20–1.38 nats against the text mode's 3.81–8.15, so once damage exceeds the gap the protein ratio goes far more negative than the text one for the same absolute damage — the ε = 0.80 column is dominated by that and should not be read as six times more damage. The columns that carry the reading are ε ≤ 0.40, where every cell is inside its own gap. One cohort draw per curve at three seeds per ε; second draws are running. The base model's protein mode is scored on a mode its own qualification calls unmeasurable, so its protein row describes the loss of something that was barely present, and its −0.528 is the least meaningful number in the table.

## 2026-08-11 — EXP-R2-163: the text loss lives in the backbone, not the vocabulary interface, and the protein gain requires both

**The causal dissection.** `Llama-2-7b-hf` and `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` are `LlamaForCausalLM` 32 x 4096 over one unmodified 32,000-piece vocabulary with no added tokens, so their weights are interchangeable tensor-for-tensor. Stage `24_component_swap.py`, snapshot `20260810225544_dc2f11b4b3c0`, component group `vocabulary_interface` (embedding + output head, untied, two tensors moved), estimand and cohorts imported from the qualification stage. Both reference cells report `swap_changed_weights: false` and both chimeras report `true`, so the machinery is an identity where it should be.

| cell | body from | vocabulary interface from | **text** | **protein** |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| reference | base | base | **+5.5240** | +0.0843 |
| chimera | **base** | **stage 1** | **+5.4345** | −0.0777 |
| chimera | **stage 1** | **base** | **+1.5095** | −0.0765 |
| reference | stage 1 | stage 1 | **+0.8336** | +0.5505 |

**On the text mode the answer is the backbone, and it is not close.** The total loss is 4.6904 nats. Installing stage 1's retrained embedding and output head into the base body costs **0.0895 nats — 1.9% of it**. Installing the base's interface into stage 1's body recovers **0.6759 nats — 14.4%**. The vocabulary interface therefore carries somewhere between 2% and 14% of the damage depending on the direction it is measured in, and the transformer body carries the rest.

**This refutes an inference of ours, and the refutation is the point of having run it.** The EXP-R2-152 correction observed that the stage costing 4.69 nats is exactly the stage carrying `modules_to_save="embed_tokens,lm_head"` while the stage costing 0.10 nats is pure LoRA, and concluded that the evidence "points at the input/output vocabulary interface rather than at the transformer body". **That was a correlation across two training stages and it is now contradicted by the swap.** The interface is retrained at that stage, and retraining it is not what breaks the text mode. What breaks it is the LoRA-updated body.

**The two directions do not sum, which is itself a result.** 1.9% forward and 14.4% backward do not add to 100% and are not each other's complement. **The components are co-adapted**: stage 1's body was fitted against an embedding that was moving underneath it, so restoring the base interface to that body recovers seven times more than installing the trained interface into the base body destroys. The loss is therefore not additively decomposable into "interface" and "body" parts, and any statement of the form "X% of the damage is in the embedding" is ill-posed for this lineage.

**On the protein mode the answer is different, and it is joint.** Stage 1's protein capability, +0.5505, survives **neither** swap: both chimeras fall to −0.077, *below* the base model's own +0.0843, which the qualification already calls unmeasurable. **The acquired protein capability is carried jointly by the body and the vocabulary interface, and breaking either half destroys it completely.** So the answer to "interface, backbone, or joint adaptation" is mode-dependent: the text *loss* is overwhelmingly backbone, and the protein *gain* is joint.

**What this decides for the work downstream.** Interpretation should target the **backbone**, not the vocabulary interface — the interface is where the text damage was hypothesised to live and is not where it lives. The protein result additionally says the acquired capability cannot be localised to either component by this method, so a component-level account of the protein mode is not available and a feature-level one is required.

**Bounds.** One cohort draw per cell, and the estimand is context information, so this attributes the loss in *that* quantity and not in every text capability. **Attribution is not causation**: the swap says which component the measured loss travels with, not where it was caused — the two groups were trained together. The protein figures on all cells that draw on the base are bounded by the base's protein mode being unmeasurable, so the two chimeras' −0.077 describes the loss of something that was already absent at one end. Only the `vocabulary_interface` group was run; `embedding` and `lm_head` separately are available on this untied lineage and were not measured.

## 2026-08-11 — EXP-R2-164: the ProGen2 scale ladder made runnable through the tolerance instrument, with its parallel block declared and verified

**What was opened.** `23_perturbation_sensitivity.py` now accepts all four rungs of `src.transfer.arms.PROTEIN_SCALE_LADDER` — `progen2-small` (151.1M, 12 x 1024), `progen2-medium` (764.8M, 27 x 1536), `progen2-large` (2779.4M, 32 x 2560) and `progen2-xlarge` (6443.6M, 32 x 4096). One lineage, one 31-token residue tokenizer, one UniRef90+BFD30 mixture, so a tolerance curve across them isolates **scale**. No campaign was launched; a campaign is running on the cluster and nothing was scheduled there.

**The perturbation target on a parallel residual block, declared and measured.** ProGen2's block is GPT-J-style: `hidden = attn_out + ff_out + residual`, both terms read from one pre-attention `ln_1`, so there is no sequential block output of the kind the GPT-2 arms' interception rests on. The declared target is the **feed-forward output** — the same tensor perturbed on every other arm, before anything is added to it — and the certifying identity is `block output == (attention output + intercepted feed-forward output) + ln_1 input`, reconstructed in the model's own left-associated order. Verified on the live forward pass of the real `progen2-small` at bfloat16 on CPU: **max absolute difference 0.0 across all 12 layers**, while the serial reconstruction `residual + ff` used by the GPT-2 arms **misses by 14.25** on the same pass. The identity is therefore load-bearing rather than decorative, and an architecture with no declaration is refused rather than duck-typed.

**Loader bands measured for the whole ladder, on the frozen self-check inputs, bfloat16, batch 4, CPU** (the same eight Swiss-Prot records every dense protein arm is gated on, rendered `1` + sequence through the arm's declared `n_to_c_control` format):

| arm | parameters | self-check NLL | rendered without its `1` control token | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| progen2-small | 151.1M | **2.3112** | 2.4516 | 0.140 |
| progen2-medium | 764.8M | **1.8452** | 1.9874 | 0.142 |
| progen2-large | 2779.4M | **1.7849** | 1.9884 | 0.204 |
| progen2-xlarge | 6443.6M | **1.2678** | 1.3800 | 0.112 |

`progen2-small` randomly initialised, same convention: **3.6384**, which is 1.33 nats from its own band centre, so L24's shape is caught on this lineage. Device spread measured on the same arm: 2.3112 on CPU against 2.3284 on one L20, **0.0172**, against a half-width of 0.30.

**A limitation the band cannot repair, recorded as data rather than as prose.** Dropping the N-to-C control token costs 0.11–0.20 nats on these four checkpoints — **inside** the 0.30 half-width on every one of them — so the likelihood band does **not** separate a ProGen2 arm rendered without its control token. This is a property of the lineage, not of the band: ProtGPT2's FASTA wrapping is worth 4.38 nats on the same inputs because its BPE merges were learnt over the wrapped byte stream, whereas ProGen2's control token is one token of context in front of an otherwise in-distribution residue run. Narrowing the half-width would not fix it either, since 0.112 on `progen2-xlarge` sits inside any band wide enough to hold the device spread with margin. The same table records that `progen2-medium` and `progen2-large` are only 0.060 nats apart on these inputs, so the band cannot tell those two rungs apart; the declared depth/width check and the weight digest can. Both are declared in `replaceable.UNSEPARATED_DENSE_SELF_CHECK_CORRUPTIONS` and are published beside the gate's own PASS in every artefact.

**`config.vocab_size` is off the path, checked by running rather than by reading.** `progen2-large` declares `vocab_size` 51200 against a 31-token tokenizer and `progen2-xlarge` declares no `vocab_size` at all — only `vocab_size_emb`/`vocab_size_lm_head` — which is the recorded reason both are staged non-members of the panel. Nothing this stage touches reads that key: depth and width come from the declaration and are verified against `n_layer`/`embed_dim`, the alphabet never enters, and symbols-per-token is measured from the tokenizer and the rendering. A unit test runs the whole path on a stub whose config raises on any access to `vocab_size`. The two staged arms additionally declare `capabilities={"pathway"}`, and `budget.arm_power` — the one shared helper that reads the key — now requires the `budget` capability, so a staged checkpoint handed to it is refused with the reason instead of producing a number over a dead alphabet.

**Interface validation, small and on B only.** One real end-to-end run of the stage on `progen2-small`, one L20, bfloat16, 16 Swiss-Prot sequences in the 64–246 band, ε ∈ {0.1, 0.4}, 2 draws, 128 bootstrap replicates. Loader gate PASS (2.3284 inside [2.0112, 2.6112]); estimand identity exact at 0.0 over 12 layers on the live GPU forward; ε = 0 identity gap exactly 0.0; clean 2.0046 → mean-ablated 2.9537, denominator **0.9491** nats/token at 0.994 residues per scored token; recovery **+0.9552** at ε = 0.10 and **+0.4307** at ε = 0.40. **This is an interface check, not a result**: 16 sequences and two draws on one cohort draw, against the 128-sequence protocol the panel's own tolerance curves use. Read only as evidence that the arm runs and its gates fire; the ladder itself has not been measured.

**Every rung's gates were run on its real checkpoint**, through `load_replaceable` at bfloat16 on CPU — the same door the stage uses, including the staged route `arm_spec` → `load_arm_spec` for the upper two:

| arm | implementation | shape | estimand identity | band |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| progen2-small | `ParallelResidualReplaceable` | 12L x 1024d x 16h | **0.0** over 12 layers | 2.3112 in [2.0112, 2.6112] PASS |
| progen2-medium | `ParallelResidualReplaceable` | 27L x 1536d x 16h | **0.0** over 27 layers | 1.8452 in [1.5452, 2.1452] PASS |
| progen2-large | `ParallelResidualReplaceable` | 32L x 2560d x 32h | **0.0** over 32 layers | 1.7849 in [1.4849, 2.0849] PASS |
| progen2-xlarge | `ParallelResidualReplaceable` | 32L x 4096d x 16h | **0.0** over 32 layers | 1.2678 in [0.9678, 1.5678] PASS |

`progen2-xlarge` loads, runs and passes both gates while `config.vocab_size` raises `AttributeError` on it throughout, which is the direct demonstration that the key is off the path.

**Bounds.** Bands for `progen2-medium`, `-large` and `-xlarge` were measured on CPU and have not been re-measured on a GPU; the 0.0172 device spread on `progen2-small` is the only direct evidence that they transport, and it is one arm. Only `progen2-small` has been run through the **whole stage** end to end; the other three have had their loader gates run and nothing else, so no sweep, no cohort and no tolerance number exists for them. The staged rungs remain outside `PANEL` and outside every campaign stage.

## 2026-08-11 — EXP-R2-165 (launched): matched text and protein dictionaries on one joint checkpoint, two seeds each

**The question, and why it is the R2.3 pivot.** F11 says text replacement is far more faithful than protein replacement, and every single-factor explanation offered so far has been excluded — denominator (EXP-R2-156), dictionary budget (EXP-R2-153), error direction (EXP-R2-158), modality of perturbation tolerance (EXP-R2-160). Every one of those comparisons crossed *checkpoints*, so lineage, corpus, tokenizer and architecture all moved with the modality. This run holds the weights fixed: **one** `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` checkpoint, two modes of it, a per-layer transcoder fitted separately to each, matched in everything a dictionary's faithfulness could otherwise be blamed on.

**Matched by construction, and refused at scoring if it drifts.** Architecture PLT, 32 layers x 4096, `d_hidden` 8192, `k` 32, auxk and optimiser at their declared defaults, batch 4, **34,000,000 scored tokens**, 256 evaluation sequences. `src.transfer.transcoders.MatchedTraining` digests exactly those fields plus the backbone digest; both smoke runs produced the identical digest `2e607956a013`, and `15_replacement_faithfulness.py --matched-against` refuses a disagreeing pair rather than reporting it. `--max-tokens` differs between the modes (512 text, 1024 protein) because it is a truncation cap in tokens and the two modes' records are shaped differently; what is held equal is the thing the estimand counts.

**The seed is the replicate axis and is deliberately not a matched field.** Four cells, one card each: text at seeds 20260806 and 20260811, protein at the same two. Both `--seed` and `--corpus-seed` move together within a cell, so a replicate differs in dictionary initialisation *and* in the order the corpus is seen — the honest replicate for "is this a property of the mode or of one run".

**Sizing, from measured throughput rather than assumed.** A 20-step smoke on the real checkpoint at both modes measured **473 scored tokens per record** in text mode at `--max-tokens 512` and **208** in protein mode at 1024. The budget therefore needs about 18.0k steps in text and 41.0k in protein at batch 4; `--steps` is set to 26,000 and 56,000, which is 44% and 37% of headroom, because a budget that outruns `--steps` refuses the run at the end rather than at the start. `--steps` also sets the held-out offset, so the held-out draw stays past everything training reaches: 104,000 records of 396,133 eligible documents in text, 224,000 of 547,305 Swiss-Prot records in protein. At 8192 latents the dictionary sees **129.7 scored tokens per latent**, inside the 108–155 the panel's own arms were trained at, and its active fraction is **0.391%** against the 36 x 1280 arms' 0.417%.

**The trade this sizing makes, stated rather than buried.** A 12x dictionary on this backbone — 49,152 latents — needs 206 GB of optimiser state and does not fit one H200; 8x does not leave room for the frozen backbone. At 2x the absolute reconstruction and recovery numbers here are **not** directly comparable with the panel's 12x cross-model results. The text-versus-protein contrast *within* this checkpoint is exact, and that is the comparison being made.

**What will be read from it**, in the order the pilot was asked for: training stability across the two seeds, held-out reconstruction, the dead-latent count, and then behavioural recovery after sequential layerwise replacement — the last of which is the only one of the four that is a faithfulness result, and the only one that licenses using these features for anything downstream.

Snapshot `20260811004706_579fd22e1771` at commit `2239c05`; four `run_external_baseline_h200.sh` cells staggered four minutes apart on cards 0–3, dispatch records under ignored `logs/external_baseline/`. Smoke runs were written to pod scratch, not to the results tree (Appendix B rule 29). **Launched, not measured**: no number from this run exists yet.

## 2026-08-11 — EXP-R2-166: inside the vocabulary interface it is the output head, and the retrained input embedding is nearly inert

**What was run.** The four separable cells EXP-R2-163 left unmeasured. `24_component_swap.py`, snapshot `20260810225544_dc2f11b4b3c0`, the `Llama-2-7b-hf` ↔ `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` pair, component groups `embedding` and `lm_head` taken one at a time in both directions. The lineage is untied — tying is read from the tensors, not from `config.tie_word_embeddings` — so the two halves of the interface are genuinely separable and all four cells report `INTERCHANGEABLE` over 291 tensors with shapes, dtypes and the full key set compared.

**Text mode.** The total loss is 4.6904 nats (base +5.5240, stage 1 +0.8336).

| cell | body | component moved | text | share of the 4.69 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| forward | base | stage 1 `embedding` | +5.5273 | **−0.1%** (none) |
| forward | base | stage 1 `lm_head` | +5.4316 | **2.0%** |
| forward | base | stage 1 interface (both) | +5.4345 | 1.9% |
| backward | stage 1 | base `embedding` | +0.8854 | **1.1%** |
| backward | stage 1 | base `lm_head` | +1.4790 | **13.8%** |
| backward | stage 1 | base interface (both) | +1.5095 | 14.4% |

**The interface's whole effect is the output head, in both directions.** Installing stage 1's retrained input embedding into the base body changes the text estimand by −0.0033 nats — it is not merely small, it is on the wrong side of zero — while its output head costs 0.0924. Restoring the base output head to stage 1's body recovers 0.6454 nats against the embedding's 0.0518. `modules_to_save="embed_tokens,lm_head"` retrained 262.1M parameters at this stage and **half of them are functionally inert on this estimand**.

**Within the interface the two components are additive; the co-adaptation is between the interface and the body.** Forward, the separate cells sum to 0.0891 against 0.0895 measured together; backward, to 0.6972 against 0.6759. The 1.9%-versus-14.4% asymmetry EXP-R2-163 reported is therefore not an interaction between the embedding and the head — it is the body's co-adaptation to the head.

**Protein mode, where the answer is sharper than "joint".** Stage 1 reads +0.5505. With the base input embedding installed it still reads **+0.5330 and stays `measurable`** — 96.8% of the acquired capability retained through a wholly foreign embedding. With the base output head installed it falls to `unmeasurable_on_this_cohort`, as does the both-components cell. So EXP-R2-163's "the protein gain requires body and interface together" resolves to **body and output head**; the retrained input embedding is not part of what carries it.

**One caveat governs the whole table, and it is structural rather than a bound on this run.** The estimand is a next-token cross-entropy and the output head is the matrix that parameterises that distribution, so a head substitution perturbs the measured quantity more directly than an embedding substitution, whose effect must propagate through 32 layers first. This attributes **the measured loss** to a component; it does not establish that the embedding matters less to the model in general, and a different estimand could order the two differently. The unmeasurable protein cells are reported as destroyed capability, not as the magnitudes −0.076 and −0.061, which their own verdict declines to license.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-167: the fate of every 2026-08-11 dispatch, one recovered set, two diagnosed blockers, and a false success traced to its line

**Why this entry exists.** The pod was found completely idle with four cards at 0 MiB while eleven cells dispatched on 2026-08-11 had left nothing on B. Idle cards are not evidence that work finished. Each cell's fate was established from pod-side artefacts and logs rather than inferred, and the three categories that came back are different in kind.

**Category 1 — completed on GPFS, never pulled (recovered today).** All four EXP-R2-165 dictionary-training cells ran to completion. Their logs carry per-step traces and a terminal `[done] … wrote …` line, and both files exist on GPFS at the declared sizes (8.59 GB `.pt` beside a `.json` each). Text seed 20260806 finished at step 18,113 with held-out NMSE sum **6.5182** over **34,001,412** scored tokens; protein seed 20260806 at step 36,974 with **5.4702** over **34,000,066**. Both report the matched digest `40e6033ecfa5`, so the matched-training contract EXP-R2-165 declared held across the two modes. The four `.json` artefacts are now under `results/transfer/external_baseline/20260811004706_579fd22e1771/<label>/`, pulled through the documented access layer and digest-verified on both sides; the four 8.59 GB `.pt` dictionaries remain on GPFS, where the scoring stage reads them, and were deliberately not transferred. **No behavioural conclusion is recorded from these four cells** — reconstruction is not faithfulness, and the stage that would decide faithfulness is blocked (category 2).

**Category 2 — ran, and raised.** The four `r23_score_*` cells (`15_replacement_faithfulness.py`, ProLLaMA_Stage_1, both modes, both seeds) each loaded the checkpoint, passed the loader self-check, matched the paired dictionary, completed the whole behavioural sweep, and then died in the causal section with `ValueError: prollama:<mode>: no ablation is implemented for component kind 'attention_head'` at `src/transfer/replaceable.py:2049`. The refusal is correct and deliberate — `JointReplaceable.ablated` only implements the block family, because the attention output projection is resolved from the *panel's* per-architecture declaration and a joint checkpoint reached by `--joint-checkpoint` is not a panel arm. The stage nevertheless builds a grid containing attention heads and calls `component_effects` unconditionally at `scripts/transfer/15_replacement_faithfulness.py:1652`, and it writes its artefact only after that section. **So this stage currently cannot score any locally trained transcoder on a joint checkpoint at all, at any setting**: there is no flag that selects the behavioural gate alone, and the behavioural numbers it had already computed are discarded. This is the R2.3 pivot's blocker and it is a code gap, not a measurement outcome.

The behavioural numbers those four runs printed before dying survive only in their pod logs, now copied to ignored `logs/external_baseline/pod_recovered_20260812/`. They are recorded here as **log-derived and not admitted**, because no artefact exists and `vars(args)` provenance is only the dispatch record: text seeds 20260806/20260811 read clean 6.6221 → replacement 10.9062/10.8298 against a fully-ablated 10.4301 (denominator 3.8080, recovery **−0.125** and **−0.105**); protein seeds read clean 4.2082 → 6.1977/5.8777 against 5.5692 (denominator 1.3610, recovery **−0.4617** and **−0.2266**). Both modes fall *through* the mean-ablated floor. Nothing about F11's text-versus-protein separation may be read from this: the dictionary is 2× expansion on a 32×4096 backbone, which EXP-R2-165 already recorded as not comparable with the panel's 12× results, and a negative recovery on the text side is the first thing that would have to be understood before the protein side meant anything.

**Category 3 — died before measuring, on a guard that is working.** `s25_base_to_stage1_protein` (`25_model_diffing_baselines.py`) loaded both 7B checkpoints and raised at `scripts/transfer/25_model_diffing_baselines.py:449`: `214 record(s) appear in both splits`. The guard is correct — the two halves are index-disjoint by construction, so a shared record means the corpus carries duplicates — and its suggested remedy is wrong for this corpus. **Measured on B, CPU only, no model**: over the same `stream_records` path at the 8192+2048 pool this stage draws, Swiss-Prot in this band yields 9,086 distinct sequences out of 10,240 at skip 0, and the cross-split duplicate count is **225 / 227 / 207 / 333 / 194** at skips 0 / 4,096 / 10,240 / 20,480 / 40,960. Sequence duplication is a corpus-wide property of Swiss-Prot, not a local one, so **no skip offset makes this cell runnable** and it was not re-dispatched. The text mode of the same comparison completed normally, which is the asymmetry worth naming: the same-input diffing baseline is attainable on the text control and blocked on the protein side by a property of the protein corpus. Deduplicating the pool is a code change and is not made here.

**The false success, traced to a line.** `logs/r23_pilot/diffing_now.log` records `s25_base_to_stage1_protein controller exited 0` while `logs/r23_pilot/s25_base_to_stage1_protein.controller.log` records `DIED AT DISPATCH` and the sanctioned entry point exited **6**. The sanctioned entry point is not at fault and was not changed: `scripts/transfer/run_external_baseline_h200.sh` detects the death at its liveness check and exits 6 at line 242, and exits 4 and 5 on the two other failure paths. The status was lost in an ad-hoc, git-ignored driver, `logs/r23_pilot/run_diffing_now.sh`, which reads `echo "$(date -Is) ${LABEL} controller exited $?"` — the command substitution runs first and resets `$?`, so the reported status is `date`'s, never the controller's. Reproduced directly: `f(){ return 6; }; f; echo "exited $?"` prints 6, and the same line with `$(date -Is)` in front prints 0. A caller using a bare `$?` would have seen the failure.

**What was added, and what was not.** A permanent regression test now pins the invariant rather than the incident: `tests/test_h200_orchestration.py::ExternalBaselineDispatchTests::test_a_stage_that_dies_at_startup_cannot_be_reported_as_success` runs the real driver against local access-layer stubs with a pod log carrying a traceback, and asserts a non-zero exit, the `DIED AT DISPATCH` line, no `ADMITTED`, and no pulled result directory. It binds: against a copy of the driver with its dispatch-death exit neutralised the test fails. The whole `ExternalBaselineDispatchTests` class passes (10 tests). **No controller, worker or library file was modified.** Two things the entry point still does not do are recorded rather than fixed: its dispatch record carries no terminal outcome, so `logs/external_baseline/*.dispatch` cannot distinguish a dead dispatch from a completed one without reading pod logs; and a stage that dies *after* the liveness window is reported `ABSENT`, which the driver's own comment reserves for "ran and wrote nothing", a measurement outcome rather than a crash.

**Blast radius.** Of 217 recorded dispatches, 17 never produced a result on B under any run id. Four are the recovered dictionaries above; five are the diagnosed failures above; the remaining eight are older and their outcomes were not previously written up. **Five of those eight are confirmed `DIED AT DISPATCH` from their own controller output** — `tc_protgpt2_tokmatched` (2026-08-08), `s15_zymctrl_linear_skip` (2026-08-09), `s15_zymctrl_band64_246_maxtok64` and `…_maxtok128` (2026-08-10), and `s22_progen3_meanablscore` (2026-08-11) — so three more than the two the audit had located. A pod-side check found empty output directories for all of them except `tc_zymctrl_tok85m`, which holds two unpulled files on GPFS and whose consumer `s15_zymctrl_tok85m` did land on B, so that dictionary was used pod-side and only its copy is missing. `reuse_check` has no output directory at all, and the fate of the remaining `20_retrieval_bound.py` `score` dispatch is not established here. **No admitted result was found to be silently missing a cell**; the gap is between dispatch and admission, not inside an admitted campaign.

**Operational note, because it cost two launches today.** Backgrounding a compound `&&` list backgrounds the whole list: three of four cells in the first wave died at argument validation with `H200_POD must be exported by the caller`, because the exports had been swallowed into the first subshell. Nothing was scheduled and no dispatch record was written, so the failure was clean. Separately, the code hash on disk moved from `a322a416b8e9` to `88b29c1d6286` between a freeze and its own launches — another agent added `src/transfer/families.py` — and the driver correctly refused to reuse the stale snapshot. A campaign whose cells are launched over several minutes cannot assume the freeze closure is still.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-168 (launched): the ProGen2 scale ladder measured through the tolerance instrument

**What this answers.** R1.3's model-scale control, the one comparison the architecture and routing line records as not yet run. EXP-R2-160 found perturbation robustness is not ordered by modality, and EXP-R2-161 found the two protein arms sit at opposite ends of the tolerance range; neither can say whether that spread is scale, because the arms differ in lineage, corpus and tokenizer as well. `src.transfer.arms.PROTEIN_SCALE_LADDER` holds modality, tokenisation, rendering, evaluation cohort, architecture and pretraining corpus fixed across 151M → 6.44B, so a tolerance curve across its four rungs isolates scale. EXP-R2-164 made the rungs runnable and explicitly launched no campaign; this is that campaign.

**Verified before launch, on L20, as required.** One real end-to-end run of `23_perturbation_sensitivity.py` on `progen2-xlarge` — the riskiest rung, being the largest and the one that declares no `config.vocab_size` — on one L20 at bfloat16, 8 sequences, ε ∈ {0.1}, 1 draw. Loader self-check PASS, estimand identity gap exactly **0.000e+00**, clean 1.3989 → mean-ablated 3.1119 (denominator 1.7130), artefact written, verdict PASS. Resolved paths were printed first: all four rungs present locally and on GPFS, `PANEL` at 15 arms, `perturbable_arms` admitting all four rungs.

**Configuration.** Snapshots `20260812102519_a322a416b8e9` (xlarge draw 1) and `20260812103809_88b29c1d6286` (all other cells), dispatched through `scripts/transfer/run_external_baseline_h200.sh` one cell per card. Every cell: `--sequences 128 --batch-size 16 --protein-min-len 64 --protein-max-len 246 --draws 3 --bootstrap 1000`, band and draw count matching the panel arms measured on 2026-08-11 so the ladder is commensurable with them. Three conditions per rung, matching the panel's own: the coarse grid `0.05 0.1 0.2 0.4 0.8`; the same grid at `--cohort-skip 4000`, which is the skip-offset sensitivity Appendix B rule 1 requires and not a reseed; and the fine grid `0.5 0.6 0.7 0.9 1.1 1.4`, the condition `s23_gpt2-large_fine` was measured on.

**Status: launched and partly complete; no conclusion is recorded.** Two cells have finished and been read from their pod logs only — `progen2-xlarge` draw 1 (admitted to `results/transfer/external_baseline/20260812102519_a322a416b8e9/s23_ladder_progen2-xlarge_draw1/`, verdict PASS) and `progen2-small` draw 1 (verdict PASS). The remaining cells were still running or in their pull window when this was written. The ladder's coarse curves are not quoted here: a scale ordering read from two rungs of four, on one cohort draw, before the skip-offset condition has returned, is exactly the shape of claim this programme has retracted before. The reading belongs in a later entry once all four rungs have both draws.

**Two blockers recorded so the ladder is not over-read.** The perturbation target on this lineage is the feed-forward output of a parallel GPT-J-style block, not the sequential block output the GPT-2 arms use; EXP-R2-164 certified the identity exactly, and the artefact carries `perturbation_target`, but a curve across arms of different block layouts is a comparison of two declared targets and must be stated as such. ## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-169: the family-disjoint split protocol, and the CATH labels are not where the inventory said they were

**What this is.** The data-side prerequisite D3.b/R3.1, R3.2 and R3.4 share: one component that decides what "family-disjoint" means, refuses when the property does not hold, and measures rather than asserts it. CPU only, no GPU, no model. `src/transfer/families.py` and `tests/test_family_splits.py`; the split mask itself is `relational.homology_disjoint_split`, which stays this package's one implementation of "a mask that never divides a group".

**`/Data/public/datasets/cath-s40` cannot supply a superfamily-disjoint split, and the resource inventory that motivated this work said it could.** Verified directly: the dump holds a 34,653-line list of CATH **domain identifiers**, the matching ATOM FASTA at CATH 4.4.0, and the coordinate tarball. A domain identifier (`12asA00`) is a PDB code, a chain and a domain index and **does not encode the C.A.T.H superfamily**; no `CathDomainList` is staged beside it, and the dump carries no UniProt accession, so it does not join to Swiss-Prot, AlphaFold, Pfam, PhosphoSite or ProteinGym. What it does carry is a guarantee no grouping is needed for — its records are pairwise below 40% identity — and that is the only thing it can currently be used for.

**The route that does exist was already on disk.** InterPro's `protein2ipr.dat.gz` carries `G3DSA:` Gene3D signatures, which *are* CATH superfamily codes, keyed on UniProt accession — the identifier every corpus in this programme joins on. One pass by `families.extract_cath_superfamilies`: **1,175,529,272 rows read in 1088.9 s**, 146,340,822 of them G3DSA, restricted to the 574,627 Swiss-Prot accessions, giving **372,181 accessions (64.8%) over 2,608 distinct superfamilies** and a 9.7 MB table at `data/interpro/cath_superfamily.tsv`. Source digest `f4bc8fe0a11e…` is recorded in the report. Spot-checked against known folds: `P31946` (14-3-3 beta) → 1.20.190.20, `P05102` (M.HhaI) → 3.40.50.150.

**Measured on a real cohort, three skip offsets and three seeds each** (Appendix B rule 1 in both halves: a seeded permutation of the whole eligible set, and a skip-offset sensitivity). 400 Swiss-Prot proteins drawn from the 213,034 records in the qualifying 64–246 band with canonical residues only:

| source | labelled of 400 | units | groups | largest group | singletons | achieved train fraction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pfam | 375–376 | 375–376 | 269–284 | 5–7 (1.3–1.9%) | 202–219 | 0.500–0.504 |
| CATH superfamily | 246–261 | 246–261 | 132–140 | 11–23 (4.5–8.8%) | 80–93 | 0.500–0.510 |

Both sources partition at the requested half on every offset and seed, with 58–151 family groups per side against a floor of two. The two disagree in exactly the direction that makes running both worth the cost: CATH annotates a third fewer proteins and merges them into half as many, larger groups, which is what a structural superfamily is.

**One statistic in the leakage audit turned out to be source-dependent, and it is recorded rather than tuned.** The audit compares cross-boundary k-mer Jaccard against same-group pairs, the "as similar as two agreed relatives" scale. On the same cohort the same-group median is **0.061–0.073 under Pfam and 0.026–0.034 under CATH**, because superfamily members are remote homologues with little sequence similarity left — the property that makes CATH the stricter split. The derived count of cross-boundary pairs above that median therefore reads **0–31 of ~35,000 under Pfam and 917–3,335 of ~15,000 under CATH**, and the second number measures how low the reference sits, not how leaky the split is. `cross_max` moved over the identical range under both (**0.072–0.218**) and is the statistic that carries the alarm. The module docstring now says so with these numbers; the count is not deleted, it is scoped to sequence-family groupings.

**What a split from this module controls, stated because the distinction decides what may be claimed from it.** It closes leakage between our own fitting and evaluation sides. It does **not** close leakage into the *model's* pretraining corpus, and nothing built from public protein data would: Swiss-Prot lies inside UniRef50 by construction, so every evaluation protein reachable here is a candidate training member whatever family it belongs to. That question keeps its own instruments — `homology` for the identity stratification, `profiles` for the retrieval bound — and a family-disjoint split neither replaces nor weakens them.

**Refusals are the interface.** Unlabelled units are refused by default, because reading "unannotated" as "unrelated to everything" is the assertion this component exists to stop; `unlabelled='drop'` is available and records the count and the annotation bias it introduces. A cohort collapsed by a hub domain, a side carrying one family, and an achieved fraction outside tolerance each raise with their own numbers rather than returning a split. Group-count is checked before achieved fraction on purpose: told about the fraction, an operator widens the tolerance and gets a two-against-one split; told about the group count, they go and find more families.

**Test evidence.** `tests/test_family_splits.py`, 29 tests, all passing, written against the ways this could report a false family-disjoint result rather than against its lines: the invariant over twelve seeds and uneven family sizes, the shared-second-domain leak a dominant-family rule cannot see, hub-domain chaining being refused rather than split, every refusal path, seed determinism, the three-way split by composition being pairwise family-disjoint, the label table's header and column count, the extraction keeping only G3DSA and raising on a moved format, and a planted cross-boundary homologue the audit has to detect. `tests/test_transfer_audit_invariants.py` and `tests/test_transfer_stage_contract.py` pass unchanged; 235 tests in total.

**Not built.** No lens stage, no method code, no concept basis in the tree. The pre-declaration numbers for that basis were computed here and are quoted in the design, not committed: over the 20 letters, Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy against formal charge reads r = −0.064 and against side-chain volume r = −0.080, while charge against volume reads **+0.331** (frequency-weighted +0.362) and volume against log residue frequency reads **−0.364**, so volume is the one declared property materially confounded with the unigram prior. The 64–246 band's residue marginal carries 4.1566 bits over 33,456,395 residues, against 0.99 / 1.58 / 1.99 / 2.28 bits under equal-mass K-way partitions at K = 2…5 — the scale of what any coarsening buys before a model is consulted.

Three verification measurements taken on the B workstation to reproduce three defects and confirm their repairs. `conda activate ct`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1`, `TRANSFER_MODEL_BASE_DIR=/Data/public/models_R2`. No H200 work.
