## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-175: the record is not the unit of independence, and the same-input diffing stage was refusing for the right reason

**The blocker, and why the guard was right.** R2.4's protein-mode cell (`25_model_diffing_baselines.py`, `Llama-2-7b-hf` → `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`, D3.h) could not start. `draw_splits` refuses when a record appears in both halves of its pool, and the 2026-08-11 dispatch died at start-up with `214 record(s) appear in both splits`. Reproduced here exactly — at `--max-tokens 1024` the measured ProLLaMA wrapper is 5 tokens, so the band is 32–1019 residues, and that band at seed 20260728 skip 0 gives **214** cross-split identical records over 9,134 distinct sequences in a 10,240-record pool. No offset repairs it (band 32–507, one pool per offset):

| skip | 0 | 4,096 | 10,240 | 20,480 | 40,960 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| distinct / 10,240 | 8,951 | 8,860 | 9,001 | 8,748 | 9,266 |
| cross-split identical | 246 | 302 | 252 | 313 | 206 |

The guard's message suggested raising `--skip`; the table says that suggestion is wrong for this corpus. The duplicates are neither a parsing artefact nor a defect: Swiss-Prot is non-redundant at the level of the *entry*, one per protein per organism, and the acyl carrier protein `acpP` appears 41 times in one pool, byte-identical, once per sequenced enterobacterial strain.

**The measurement that decided the design.** Deduplicating would let the guard pass and leave most of the leakage. DIAMOND 2.1.24, `--very-sensitive --masking 0 --evalue 1e-3`, held-out side against training side of the same pool, identity over the shorter sequence:

| pool (band 32–507, skip 0) | ≥95% | =100% | median max identity | no detectable homologue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swiss-Prot | 847 / 2,048 (41.4%) | 356 (17.4%) | 90.1% | 132 (6.4%) |
| UniRef50 | 36 / 2,048 (1.8%) | 4 (0.2%) | 10.3% | 963 (47.0%) |

So the exact-string check reached at most two fifths of the leakage on the corpus this stage draws. **UniRef50 is twenty times cleaner and still not clean** — zero exact duplicates at all five offsets (10,240/10,240 distinct every time) but 36 held-out records at ≥95%, because UniRef50 bounds a member's distance to its own representative, not the distance between two representatives. Corpus choice moves the problem by a factor of twenty; it does not remove it, and it would change the declared protein-mode corpus for one stage of the lineage only.

**Why this biases the answer rather than merely offending tidiness.** Every residual is reported under true and shuffled pairing. Homology leakage acts through position correspondence, which the shuffled null destroys, so it improves the true-pairing fit alone and widens exactly the gap that decides whether a Crosscoder is warranted.

**The completed text-mode cell was checked and is clean.** Its own 10,240-document OpenWebText pool: zero identical documents; the largest word-13-gram containment of any held-out document in the *whole* training side is 0.336, with 92.7% of held-out documents sharing not one 13-gram with it; the largest MinHash Jaccard over word 5-gram shingles against any single training document is 0.219. The text result does not rest on a weaker disjointness than assumed, and the two modes are not incomparable for that reason.

**The remedy: split at the near-duplicate group, not at the record** (`src/transfer/near_duplicates.py`, new). Records are joined when the containment of their shingle sets `|A∩B| / min(|A|,|B|)` reaches 0.5 — residue 5-mers for a protein corpus, word 5-grams for a text one — and the split is taken over connected components by `relational.homology_disjoint_split`, this package's one implementation of a mask that never divides a group, wrapped in the same disjointness re-check and achieved-fraction refusal `families.family_disjoint_split` uses.

*Containment and not Jaccard, calibrated rather than assumed.* Against DIAMOND identity over the shorter sequence on 60,000 aligned pairs from the two pools, no Jaccard threshold separates the classes — it penalises length asymmetry, which is exactly the shape of a fragment inside a longer protein, and at k=5 the best operating point still misses 1.3% of Swiss-Prot's and 11.3% of UniRef50's ≥95% pairs, rising to 55% at threshold 0.7. Containment separates them completely: at k=5 the *minimum* containment over every ≥95% pair is 0.732 (Swiss-Prot) and 0.742 (UniRef50) against a 99th percentile of 0.754 and 0.438 over all sub-95% pairs, so every threshold in 0.30–0.70 misses none on either corpus and the declared 0.50 sits inside a flat region rather than at a tuned point. The cost is over-merging — 4.9% of sub-95% pairs joined at 0.50 — which is the safe direction. Alignment-free because no aligner is staged in the pod and nothing may be installed there; DIAMOND is the offline standard the threshold was set against, not a runtime dependency.

*Result on the production pool* (Swiss-Prot, band 32–1019, seed 20260728): at skip 0, 5,576 groups over 10,240 records, largest 88, achieved training fraction 0.8000 exactly, maximum boundary containment 0.4984; at skip 40,960, 6,660 groups, largest 62, 0.8000, 0.4993. Against the DIAMOND all-against-all of the pool, **zero** pairs at ≥90% identity straddle the new boundary, against 41.4% of held-out records carrying a ≥95% relative before. The same procedure takes ≥90% straddling to zero on the UniRef50 pool too.

*The gate is the near-duplicate gate and nothing stricter*, because attainability precedes application: a near-duplicate gate is attainable on the text control under this same procedure, and a homology gate has no text analogue at all — there is no remote homologue of a web page — so gating remote homology would hold the protein side to a criterion the text side is not defined under. What remains is measured and declared rather than hidden: after the split, 855 of 2,043 held-out Swiss-Prot records keep a ≥70%-identity relative in the training split (93 of 2,048 on UniRef50), and every artefact carries a threshold-free per-record boundary-containment distribution.

**Nothing moves on the text side, and this was verified rather than argued.** Every group of the OpenWebText pool is a singleton, so the group split *is* the record split there, and the new `draw_splits` reproduces the completed text-mode cell's training and held-out lists exactly — same records, same order. The two modes are therefore one procedure and the completed text cell stands without a re-run; `tests/test_model_diffing_baselines.py` holds that as an executable property rather than as this paragraph.

**Test evidence.** `tests/test_near_duplicates.py`, 13 tests, and the rewritten `TheHeldOutSplitMustBeHeldOut`, 7 tests — all 20 pass. The negative paths are the point and the guard is not weakened: a pool that is one near-duplicate family refuses; a pool where one group holds 45 of 56 records refuses, naming the group's size and saying not to widen the tolerance; a corpus too small still refuses; exact content overlap still refuses as the backstop for records too short to carry a shingle. The end-to-end fixtures were themselves near-duplicate corpora — 64 "distinct" records made by appending a poly-residue tail to one of four base sequences, under a docstring asserting that distinctness made the splits non-overlapping — and were replaced by independent draws, which is the same confusion this change exists to correct. Beyond the unit tests, `draw_splits` was run on the real corpora through the real stage module at production settings for both modes and both offsets, and the new artefact fields were round-tripped through `io.write_json`.

**Configuration and dispatch.** Two cells of `25_model_diffing_baselines.py`, both `Llama-2-7b-hf` -> `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`, `--rendering prollama --mode protein --tensor block_output --train-records 8192 --eval-records 2048 --batch-size 8 --max-tokens 1024 --seed 20260728 --ridge 1e-4`, differing only in `--skip` (0 and 40,960) so that the pair *is* the skip-offset sensitivity rather than one point of it. Run id `20260812130041_d2fe9a1dca1d`, one snapshot shared by both, on cuda:1 and cuda:3; cuda:0 and cuda:2 were left free. The snapshot was frozen from a detached worktree at commit `2000f9b` rather than from the live checkout, because the first freeze was refused at launch -- correctly -- when another agent's edit moved the code hash during the seven minutes the push takes, and a worktree at a fixed commit is the only way to make freeze-then-launch atomic while four agents share the tree. Both cells cleared the split guard in the pod at band [32, 1019], 8192 train / 2048 held-out, and the first reports 1,824,402 scored training positions, 454,431 held-out, 445.4 per `d_model` -- far above the `n <= d_model` refusal that would make the shuffled control read near zero for a trivial reason. The in-pod split reproduces the L20 prediction exactly: 5,576 groups, largest 88 (0.86% of the pool), achieved training fraction 0.8000, maximum boundary containment 0.4984, none above threshold.

**The skip-offset sensitivity is flat.** Both protein cells completed. At skip 40,960 the pool groups into 6,660 groups, largest 62, achieved fraction 0.8000, maximum boundary containment 0.4993, none above threshold, 1,996,643 training and 513,323 held-out positions. Its cross-checkpoint true-pairing means are identity 2.790, mean_shift 1.811, procrustes 0.676, ridge 0.407, against 2.826 / 1.828 / 0.670 / 0.400 at skip 0, and its adjacent-layer ridge unit is 0.1852 against 0.1855. Every quantity the verdict reads moves in the third decimal, so what follows does not depend on which region of the corpus the pool came from -- which is the sensitivity Appendix B rule 1 asks for, and it is the first time this stage has had one.

**Two-mode reading.** Means over layers, held-out, `block_output`; the protein column is skip 0:

| | cross true | cross shuffled | adjacent true |
|---|---|---|---|
| protein: identity / mean_shift / procrustes / ridge | 2.826 / 1.828 / 0.670 / 0.400 | 3.454 / 2.455 / 1.000 / 1.002 | 3.221 / 1.810 / 0.404 / 0.186 |
| text: identity / mean_shift / procrustes / ridge | 3.115 / 2.628 / 0.852 / 0.684 | 3.671 / 3.184 / 1.000 / 1.001 | 206.5 / 206.0 / 0.901 / 0.731 |

One draw per mode on the text side and two on the protein side. Three things are safe to say and a fourth is not. **The fits are correspondence rather than capacity in both modes**: ridge under true pairing sits far below its own shuffled value at every layer of both, so none of this is the `d^2` free parameters. **No affine map removes the difference in either mode**: at the layers where the cross-checkpoint residual is largest, ridge still leaves 0.73 (protein, layers 12-14) and 0.90 (text, layers 24-26). **The depth profiles have different shapes**: the text cross-checkpoint residual rises with depth and stays high to the top (0.65 at layer 31), while the protein one peaks in the middle third and falls back sharply (0.73 at layer 13 against 0.11-0.28 at layers 29-31). Read against the adjacent-layer unit *at the same layer*, the text cross-checkpoint residual is about one layer of ordinary computation through the middle and deep layers (ratio 0.87-1.05), and the protein one is two to four times it from layer 8 upward.

What is **not** safe is the mean-over-layers adjacent identity residual of 206.5 on the text side: layer 1 alone reads 6,347.7 there, because its next layer's own held-out variance is tiny, and that single layer carries essentially the whole mean. The ridge-based adjacent unit is not affected (0.75-0.87 across the middle layers), so the per-layer ratio above stands and the aggregate identity row does not. No R2.4 decision is recorded here -- the stage declines to declare one by design, both numbers are representational rather than behavioural, and the base checkpoint's protein mode remains behaviourally unmeasurable, which the protein artefact carries in its own limitation field.

**Limitations.** The relation is calibrated against DIAMOND only for the class it gates: a pair DIAMOND does not align at `--evalue 1e-3` cannot be a ≥95% pair, so the calibration is complete for that class and says nothing about how the grouping behaves on remote homologues, where it is deliberately permissive. The word 5-gram relation for text and the residue 5-mer relation for protein are each their own modality's near-duplicate criterion and are not the same criterion; what is claimed in common is only that the gate is attainable on both. Grouping costs about two minutes of host CPU on a 10,240-record protein pool and runs after both checkpoints are loaded, so a refusal still comes after two multi-gigabyte loads. One draw per offset; the skip-offset sensitivity is the second cell, not a property of either alone.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-176: D3.d feasibility, measured on CPU before the design is costed — the second-order retrieval channel, and the two constraints that reshape it

**What this is and is not.** No GPU, no model forward pass, no campaign. Five CPU measurements taken to decide whether a D3.d grounded in **measured pairwise epistasis** can be built at adequate power, and to price the hazards before a design is accepted. The design itself is proposed to the coordinating agent and is **not accepted**; if it is, its null structure and decision rule are frozen in their own entry before any run, as EXP-R2-171 and D3.b's Phase A did. Scripts and artefacts under ignored `logs/design_d3d/` (rule 29: no smoke output in the results tree).

**Why the estimand is not already closed by F10.** `profiles.lookup_score` is an exact sum of per-column log-odds and `fitness.Assay.blosum` an exact sum over substitutions, so **both channels that bound F10 predict identically zero epistasis for every multi-substitution variant**. F10's subtraction is first-order; a pairwise estimand is outside the expressive class of the channel that produced it. That is an algebraic fact about the two channels, not an argument about what they might have missed.

**(1) The benchmark supports a pair-level estimand at a publishable unit count.** Over all 217 staged ProteinGym substitution assays, counting only doubles whose **both** constituent singles are measured in the same assay: 69 assays carry any multi-mutant, 66 carry ≥100 usable doubles, 32 carry ≥1000. Aggregated to position pairs with ≥10 measured doubles, and mapped onto the 174 identity clusters `20_retrieval_bound.py` already computed:

| requirement | assays | identity clusters | pairs (≥10 doubles) | pairs at separation ≥10 residues |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ≥2 pairs per assay | 51 | 48 | 7,298 | 5,158 |
| ≥2 pairs **and** ≥500 corpus hits | 23 | 22 | 5,325 | 3,899 |
| ≥50 pairs per assay | 9 | 8 | 7,111 | 5,057 |

The second row is the tier on which a corpus-derived *pairwise* baseline can be estimated at all, and 22 clusters is above `statistics.MINIMUM_BOOTSTRAP_UNITS` (8) by a factor of 2.75. The third row is where per-protein precision lives (SPG1_STRSG 1,485 pairs at a median 361 doubles each; GRB2_HUMAN 994; RASK_HUMAN 1,047; PABP_YEAST 899).

**(2) About three quarters of raw pair-level epistasis is the assay's global nonlinearity, and that is what would have manufactured an effect.** Per pair, over the doubles measured at it, with the additive prediction taken from the two singles and the global-epistasis transform fitted as an isotonic regression of observed on additive:

| assay | pairs | doubles | sd additive | sd raw epistasis | sd **specific** epistasis | split-half reliability, raw | **specific** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SPG1_STRSG_Olson_2014 | 1485 | 535,917 | 2.600 | 0.7480 | **0.2840** | 0.997 | **0.992** |
| GRB2_HUMAN_Faure_2021 | 994 | 62,189 | 0.632 | 0.2369 | **0.0580** | 0.946 | **0.543** |
| PABP_YEAST_Melamed_2013 | 899 | 36,370 | 0.479 | 0.1529 | **0.0656** | 0.952 | **0.860** |
| RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_abundance | 1047 | 22,214 | 0.450 | 0.1443 | **0.0909** | 0.878 | **0.751** |
| A4_HUMAN_Seuma_2022 | 765 | 14,015 | 1.984 | 0.4746 | **0.3313** | 0.670 | **0.530** |
| DLG4_HUMAN_Faure_2021 | 218 | 5,010 | 0.656 | 0.2790 | **0.0633** | 0.927 | **0.421** |
| YAP1_HUMAN_Araya_2012 | 303 | 8,669 | 0.717 | 0.2184 | **0.1666** | 0.696 | **0.617** |
| CAPSD_AAV2S_Sinai_2021 | 377 | 10,833 | 3.475 | 0.8233 | **0.6124** | 0.771 | **0.756** |
| HECD1_HUMAN_Tsuboyama_2023_3DKM | 16 | 4,288 | 1.289 | 0.7271 | **0.2919** | 0.998 | **0.998** |
| POLG_PESV_Tsuboyama_2023_2MXD | 13 | 4,134 | 1.374 | 0.5292 | **0.2980** | 0.997 | **0.996** |

Removing the global transform costs 55–77% of the pair-level spread on six of ten assays. A design that reads raw double-mutant deviation as "epistasis" is therefore measuring the assay's measurement range for most of its variance, and would have produced a confident correlation with any predictor that ranks single mutants at all. **The reliability of what remains is 0.42–0.99**, so the specific channel is measurable and every correlation taken against it carries an attenuation ceiling of `sqrt(reliability)` — 0.65 to 0.99 — that has to travel with it (rules 25, 27). Reliability is split-half over the doubles inside each pair, Spearman-Brown corrected, seed 20260812.

**(3) The family-disjoint protocol runs on this cohort, through `src/transfer/families.py` and not around it.** ProteinGym assay names carry UniProt entry names; 47 of 49 resolve against the staged Swiss-Prot FASTA (`F7YBW8_MESOW` and `Q8WTC7_9CNID` do not), giving 49 assays over 46 identity clusters with accessions. One accession per cluster: **36 carry a Pfam family → 29 groups → an 18/18 split**; **32 carry a CATH superfamily → 25 groups → a 16/16 split**. Both sides of both splits clear the eight-unit bootstrap floor, and both sources are available so the grouping choice can be swept (rule 17 applied to a split definition).

**(4) The arm with the identified corpus is the arm whose position-level causal interface is half-defined, and this is measured rather than anticipated.** An activation patch at "residue *i*" needs the wild-type and mutant runs token-aligned outside the mutated span. Over 200 seeded single mutants of each of four assays:

| arm | tokens per residue | same token count | **exactly one token differs** |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| protgpt2 | 0.33–0.35 | 0.710–0.850 | **0.470–0.545** |
| zymctrl | 1.000 | 1.000 | **1.000** |
| progen2-medium | 1.000 | 1.000 | **1.000** |

**On ProtGPT2 roughly half of all single substitutions retokenise the sequence**, so a position-level patch is undefined on them; and the retained half is not a random half, it is the half whose local context is BPE-stable. ProtGPT2 is simultaneously the only arm whose pretraining corpus is exactly identified (F10) and therefore the only arm on which a retrieval subtraction is *identified* rather than bounded. A sequence-likelihood estimand is unaffected — it needs no alignment — so the split falls exactly on the phase boundary: the behavioural half of any D3.d can carry ProtGPT2 at full strength, and the internal-mediation half cannot without a measured retained-versus-dropped comparison on conservation and effect size. This is L14's collapse (0.943 → 0.421 on subword arms) reappearing on a different task, and it is the second constraint that reshapes the design.

**(5) The pairwise retrieval channel needs no new search.** `results/transfer/retrieval_bound/corpus_hits.tsv` already holds 354,762 DIAMOND hits over the 187 wild types **with gapped query and subject alignment strings** (`homology.ALIGNMENT_FIELDS`), and `profiles.sequence_weights` already implements the reweighting a coupling estimate would need. Depth on the pair-rich wild types: GRB2/RASK/PABP/A4/DLG4 at the 5,000-hit cap, YAP1 2,318, HIS7 661, CAPSD 221, SPG1 134, the four GFP-likes 68–125. So the second-order channel is a CPU extension over an existing artefact on 22 clusters, and is unbuildable on the deepest-pair assay in the benchmark (SPG1, 134 hits) — which is a fact about that protein's corpus support, and is why the retrieval gate and the null gate are reported on different tiers rather than on one pooled number.

**Standing hazard flagged for the design, not resolved here.** A plug-in mutual information over 20×20 alignment columns is upward-biased by roughly `19²/(2·Neff)` nats and the bias grows exactly as depth falls, which is L12/rule 3 in a second-order form; any coupling channel built from these alignments has to use a held-out or explicitly bias-corrected estimator and a column-permutation null that preserves marginals and depth, or it will read shallow proteins as strongly coupled.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-177 pre-declared: D3.d Stage 0 and Stage 1, frozen before the first forward pass

**This entry is written before any model is loaded and its decision rules may not be changed after the numbers exist.** D3.d was re-chartered on the design in EXP-R2-176 and accepted with one deviation: it runs **independent of D3.c**, because its causal object is a position rather than a dictionary feature, so no surviving feature set is a prerequisite. Stage 0 (CPU) and Stage 1 (A1 attainability) are authorised; nothing beyond them.

**The estimand.** Unit of analysis is the wild-type protein, clustered at 50% identity — F10's unit. For each position pair *(i,j)* of a ProteinGym substitution assay carrying ≥10 measured doubles whose both constituent singles are also measured:

- `e(i,j)` — **measured specific epistasis**: the pair-mean residual of observed double-mutant phenotype about an isotonic regression of observed on the additive prediction from the two singles. The isotonic transform is the assay's global-epistasis nonlinearity; the residual is what survives it. Fitted on a seeded half of the doubles and evaluated on the complementary half, with the split sensitivity reported.
- `m(i,j)` — the model's predicted epistasis, `logP(x^ab) − logP(x^a) − logP(x^b) + logP(wt)`, averaged over exactly the (a,b) variants measured at that pair, so the two channels carry the same residue composition.
- `c(i,j)` — the corpus pairwise coupling: held-out, APC-corrected mutual information over the arm's own retrieved homologue alignment.

Per protein `S_model(p) = Spearman(m, e)` over its pairs. Headline quantities are `S_model − S_null` and `S_model − S_lookup2`, cluster-bootstrapped over families.

**Why this is not already answered by F10.** `profiles.lookup_score` is an exact sum of per-column log-odds and `fitness.Assay.blosum` an exact sum over substitutions, so **both channels that bounded F10 predict identically zero epistasis for every multi-substitution variant**. F10's subtraction is first-order; this estimand lies outside the expressive class of the channel that produced it. That is algebra about those two functions, not a conjecture that they missed something.

**The nulls, in the order of strictness they will be reported.**

- **N0, label permutation.** Permute `e` across pairs. Chance level; catches arithmetic errors only.
- **N1, construction-matched pair permutation — the primary null.** Permute `m` among pairs *within strata* of (sequence-separation decile × additive-effect-magnitude decile × minimum-column-conservation decile). This preserves everything that generates `m` except which pair it names. Every stratifier is computable without the model, which is standing rule 28 met by construction; each is additionally reported as its own single-covariate baseline.
- **N2, the retrieval channel.** `S_lookup2` computed identically with `m` replaced by `c`. Plug-in mutual information over 20×20 alignment columns is biased upward by ≈`19²/(2·Neff)` and the bias grows exactly as depth falls, so the estimator is split-half held-out with APC and its null is a column permutation preserving marginals and depth (rule 3, L12 in second-order form).
- **N3, the attenuation ceiling.** `sqrt(reliability)` per protein from split-half over the doubles inside each pair, measured in EXP-R2-176 at 0.42–0.99. Every correlation is quoted beside its ceiling; disattenuated values are reported and never gated on.

**Stage 1 — A1, the attainability gate, and it is the gate that matters.** Standing rule 2 in the only form available here: the biological referent has no text analogue, so attainability is demonstrated on a **synthetic planted-coupling referent** where the coupling is known by construction and which *can* be run on the text control.

Construction, per probe: draw a real sequence under a seeded permutation of the eligible corpus (rule 1); choose `K = 8` non-overlapping position pairs at matched separations; in exactly one — the **planted** pair — set `s[j] := s[i]`, leaving the other seven as drawn. For each pair and a declared substituting symbol `a`, score the same four sequences the estimand uses: `wt`, `A` (i→a), `B` (j→a), `AB` (both→a). At the planted pair `wt` and `AB` carry the copy relation and `A` and `B` break it, so a model that has learned the relation must return a large positive `m`; at a control pair no such relation exists. The referent `e` is 1 on the planted pair and 0 on the seven controls.

`S_A1` is the pooled Spearman of `m` against `e` over all probe × pair units, with the top-1 rate reported beside it against its chance level of `1/K = 0.125`. The null is permutation of `e` **within probe**, which is separation-matched by construction. Bootstrap unit is the probe.

> **A1 PASSES** if the 95% bootstrap interval of `S_A1` over probes lies wholly above the 99th percentile of the within-probe permutation null, on **gpt2-large** and on **at least one protein arm**.
>
> **A1 FAILS** otherwise, and then the instrument cannot detect a coupling planted for it. **Stage 2 is not run, no downstream number is interpreted, and the result is reported as a method failure.** This is not a formality: a null on arms that may simply lack the signal is publishable only if the positive control proves detection was possible.

**Stage 2 — A2 and A3, not authorised by this entry, declared here so they cannot be chosen later.** A2: cluster bootstrap over families of `S_model − S_N1`; PASS if the 95% interval lies wholly above zero. A3: cluster bootstrap of `S_model − S_lookup2` on the deep-alignment tier, read through F10's own four-way vocabulary — `acquired` (interval wholly above zero), `retrieval_bounded` (interval inside ±half of that arm's own `S_model − S_N1`), `retrieval_dominated` (wholly below that bound), `indeterminate` (otherwise, reported with the family count). Phase B is authorised only by `A1 ∧ A2`; A3 sets what a Phase B result may be called, not whether it runs.

**Invariance sweeps, all declared now.** Minimum separation ∈ {0, 3, 6, 10, 20} **residues**, never tokens (rule 26, L23); global-epistasis correction ∈ {none, isotonic, monotone spline}; pseudocount α; family grouping ∈ {Pfam, CATH}; skip-offset on the doubles draw (rule 1). Orderings must be invariant across each (rule 17).

**Declared scope limits, carried from EXP-R2-176 rather than discovered later.** ProtGPT2 leaves exactly one token differing on only 47–55% of single substitutions, and the retained half is the BPE-stable half rather than a random one; sequence likelihood needs no alignment, so ProtGPT2 enters Phase A at full strength and enters Phase B only with a measured retained-versus-dropped comparison on conservation and effect size. SPG1_STRSG carries the benchmark's best pair coverage (1,485 pairs) and only 134 corpus hits, so the null gate and the retrieval gate are reported on different tiers and never as one pooled number. The wild types run 37–3,423 residues against a 64–246 qualifying band; the band actually scored is declared in the artefact beside the qualifying band (rule 13) and the 13 wild types above the context limit are excluded by name.

**What each Stage 0 outcome means.** Stage 0 is CPU-only and can refuse the campaign on its own evidence: if the corpus coupling channel `c` fails its own positive control — predicting `e` above its column-permutation null — on most proteins, then A3 is not interpretable on those proteins and is reported as such rather than being read as the model winning. That is F10's `positive_control` gate reused one order up, and it is the one way Stage 0 alone can stop Stage 2.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-178: ZymCTRL's concept readout was its EC tag. The last positive protein cell dissolves and the D3.b negative is clean

**Why this one arm was re-run.** EXP-R2-173 left exactly one protein cell positive: ZymCTRL, sign-invariant across the τ sweep on all three declared properties, against three protein arms that were sign-invariantly *negative*. It is also the only EC-conditioned arm on the panel, L15 prices its tag at 1.73 nats, and it was the only arm whose statistic fell from seen to unseen families — the signature of conditioning rather than computation. The pre-declared test was to hold the tag constant.

**What was run.** `26_concept_lens.py` with `--ec-conditioning native fixed`, both cells in **one invocation on one snapshot** (`20260812133117_3ab7fcbf5344`, admitted to `results/transfer/external_baseline/20260812133117_3ab7fcbf5344/cl_zym_cond_a4/`), so the two cells share the cohort object, the accessions, the family split, the sampled positions, the null draws and the code hash exactly. `fixed` substitutes one constant EC tag (`1.1.1.1`) for each protein's own and changes nothing else: the rendering is still `Cohort.input_strings`', the arm stays in its declared format and on its training distribution, and the tag's mutual information with the protein drops to zero.

**`unconditioned` was not run and is refused as structurally unavailable, not skipped.** An EC-conditioned arm's scored span is delimited by its own start and end tokens — that is what `target_rule("ec_conditioned")` reads — so dropping the tag drops the boundaries and leaves no definition of which positions are scored. A number from some other span would not be comparable with the two cells it exists to be compared with, and `unconditioned` is separately the weaker test because it takes the arm off its training distribution and confounds tag removal with distribution shift. `fixed` is the decisive one and it was decisive.

**Every statistic collapses, and the direction is unambiguous.**

| statistic (unseen-family side, k=3) | native | fixed | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| aperture gain, charge / hydropathy / volume at τ=0.75 | +0.176 / +0.145 / +0.161 | +0.044 / +0.034 / +0.042 | 3.8–4.3× |
| aperture gain at τ=0.50 | +0.056 / +0.051 / +0.054 | +0.010 / +0.007 / +0.009 | 5.6–7.3× |
| rank-matched null: layers of 11 clearing, hydropathy | **7/11**, best +0.0757 | **0/11**, best −0.0121 | — |
| rank-matched null: charge / volume | 0/11 / 1/11 | 0/11 / 0/11 | — |
| final-layer within-protein Spearman, hydropathy | +0.847 | **+0.140** | 6.0× |
| final-layer Spearman, charge / volume | +0.711 / +0.815 | +0.050 / +0.092 | 14× / 8.9× |

**So ZymCTRL's positive aperture gain was the conditioning tag.** With a constant tag the arm clears the rank-matched partition null at **zero of eleven depths on all three properties**, which is where the other three protein arms already sat on two of three. The single positive protein cell in the D3.b Phase A table dissolves, and the negative now holds across all four protein arms without exception.

**One caveat travels with it and is not removable by this design.** The tag was worth **1.87 nats** of the model's own next-residue prediction on this cohort — final-layer symbol cross-entropy moves 0.9749 → 2.8405, closely reproducing L15's independently measured 1.73 — so under `fixed` the model is simply worse at the task, and part of the collapse is that degradation rather than the tag specifically carrying the property. The two readings cannot be separated at this estimand. They do not need to be for the conclusion: on both statistics that are normalised against the arm's *own* null at its *own* conditioning, the effect is gone, and no positive claim survives under either reading.

**A consequence for how the fixed cell may be read at all.** Under `fixed` the volume concept **fails its own final-layer positive control** (+0.0920 against a 0.999 cut of +0.0961), so that concept is `unmeasurable` on that cell by the stage's own precondition; charge and hydropathy clear it by +0.0012 and +0.0048, which is a pass and a thin one. The fixed cell is therefore read as the collapse of a positive result, not as a measurement in its own right.

**A correction to EXP-R2-173, made before promotion and marked in place.** That entry characterised the shuffled-property null as "retaining a within-protein Spearman of +0.46 to +0.64", which states the 99.9th percentile as though it were the typical value. Measured here across every arm, the null is centred near **zero** (means −0.008 to +0.017) and it is the **upper tail** that is heavy: on twenty symbols the 0.999 quantile reaches +0.46 to +0.64, against +0.16 to +0.30 on 50,257. The methodological statement is unchanged and is sharper stated correctly — what makes a small alphabet dangerous is not that a shuffled property is typically good, but that the best of a thousand shuffles is nearly as good as the truth.

**Operational.** Four freeze-and-launch attempts were refused on the concurrent-edit code-hash race before the fifth won; the run reported here is the one whose snapshot was verified in-pod. GPU occupancy confirmed inside the pod rather than from the launcher's exit code.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-171 studentised: the third cut fails the same gate, and the defect is in the statistic rather than the floor

Run `20260812133257_3ab7fcbf5344`, two lanes on cuda:0 and cuda:2, identical configuration and seeds to `20260812114906_15580b126619`. **The pre-declared reproducibility check passes exactly**: every fixed-threshold count, every ceiling-normalised count, every raw null-calibrated count and every per-head excess is bit-identical to the first run, so the studentised numbers sit beside the originals rather than replacing them.

**Verdict: (C), on the pre-declared specificity gate, by a wide margin and on every arm.** The offset-two decoy count is **0.81 to 1.39** of the prefix-matching count at every family-wise level, against a declared ceiling of 0.50. Reported and not read: the placement the studentised statistic would have given is (B)-consistent at all three levels — bygpt5-medium-en at 0.703 / 0.688 / 0.656 with intervals separated from zymctrl, the strongest protein arm, and overlapping dialogpt-small, the weakest text arm. It is vetoed and it carries nothing.

**Three cut variants have now failed the same gate, which is the finding.** The raw cut, R1's position-matched decoy floor, R2's reflected tail and the studentised family-wise maximum disagree about almost everything and agree that the decoy counts nearly as many heads as the aligned key does. An invariant that survives four floors is not a property of any floor.

**The diagnosis, and it is not where I put it.** I attributed the defect to the floor. The numbers say the numerator is fine and the *criterion* is wrong. Offset-specificity is intact where the signal is: peak prefix-matching excess is 0.87–0.95 against peak offset-two excess of 0.006–0.41, and the across-head correlation between the two is 0.04–0.85. What saturates the count is the weak tail. At 256 probes a head with an excess of 0.001 and a standard error of 0.0002 is four standard errors from its null and is counted — on the aligned key and on the decoy alike — because the permutation removes the repeat *entirely* and nearly every head responds to that a little. **A significance cut against a matched null is a detection criterion, and counting induction heads needs an effect-size criterion.** The same artefacts show the gap plainly: the significance readings put 20–85% of every arm's heads above the cut, the effect-size reading 0.3–17%.

**So the collision null keeps its real contribution and loses the one I built it for.** What it establishes is the **identity ceiling** — measured per arm on the probes actually scored, 0.842–0.852 on BPE text, 0.976 on ProtGPT2, 0.321 on byte-level text, 0.229–0.231 on residue protein — and that is what makes a fixed 0.10 cut readable as 12% of attainable on one arm and 44% on another. What it does not support is a head count read as "excess distinguishable from the null": that statistic is retired here, with cause, rather than carried forward with a caveat.

**Consequences for the three statuses, which do not collapse into one.**

1. **Refuted, and correction-independent.** On the uncorrected published statistic bygpt5-medium-en scores 0.0208, below the weakest BPE text arm (0.0402) and inside the protein range (0.0000–0.0260). No correction enters this and none of today's failures touches it.
2. **Item 2 has moved, and it has not closed.** The null-calibrated count is retired, so the disagreement between it and the ceiling-normalised reading is no longer evidence about the byte arm — one of the two parties to it is invalid. What remains is the ceiling-normalised effect-size reading on its own: bygpt5-medium-en at 0.0417, **interval-separated from every protein arm** including progen2-small at 0.0365, and **interval-overlapping llama-3.2-3b** at 0.0432 and nothing else. Read alone, that says the alphabet accounts for the byte arm's deficit within the resolution available. It is **one reading resting on one mechanism assumption** — a head that disambiguates on single-token identity and splits evenly across every earlier copy — and it is not the agreement of two independent corrections that would have closed the question. ByGPT5's architecture and corpus differences remain unaddressed by any of this.
3. **Untouched.** The matched pair reads 5.46x fixed, 5.62x ceiling-normalised, and 2.47–2.55x studentised; text above protein on every reading taken today and on every reading taken before.

**The degenerate-head repair, and the evidence that it is hygiene.** The first dispatch died on ProGen2-small: a head whose bootstrap spread underflowed to zero while its excess did not, which the earlier entry had argued should be unreachable. The argument was wrong and the guard caught it rather than silently zeroing a head — saturated attention sinks carry excesses of 1e-12 to 1e-8 with spreads below 1e-12, and an absolute test at one value split that single dead quantity across the two tests. The zero-excess test is now relative to the probe's own chance attention level at one part in a million of it. **The largest excess set aside anywhere on the panel is 1.36e-10 times chance attention**, over eleven arm-statistic pairs; the largest on any text arm is 7.83e-19 times chance. Nothing counted could have moved, and the bound is reported in every artefact so that is checkable rather than asserted.

**Operational.** Two dispatches were refused by the controller's stale-snapshot check because the shared tree's code hash moved during an eight-minute freeze — once from another agent's edits and once from my own, made while my freeze was in flight. The refusals were correct both times. The launcher now retries the freeze rather than working around it, and the rule for anyone dispatching from this tree is not to edit it between freeze and dispatch.

> **Which run directory is the reading, and an unplanned replication, 2026-08-12.** Today's dispatch retries left a second complete text lane on disk, `20260812131925_1aa35ceddf82/student_text`, nine arms and a panel summary, produced by the attempt whose protein lane died on the degenerate head. It is **superseded and is not the reading** — the reading is `20260812133257_3ab7fcbf5344`, both lanes, named in the entry above. It is kept rather than removed, and labelled here rather than left to be inferred from two timestamps, because an unlabelled directory carrying plausible studentised numbers is exactly the shape of thing this programme has misread before.
>
> Comparing the two is free and worth one line: the superseded lane is **identical to the final one on every studentised count at every level, on both statistics, and on every per-head t across all nine arms**. So the degenerate-head repair changed nothing on the text side, which is what its own reported bound predicted (largest excess set aside on any text arm, 7.83e-19 times chance attention), and the text lane has been replicated across two independent dispatches of the same configuration. Neither fact was planned; both are checkable from the two directories.


## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-179: D3.d A1 re-declared. The positive control was defective twice, and its repair separates two protein arms for different reasons

**Status: the corrections and the L20 verification are recorded here; the full-scale A1 is not in this entry.** Everything below is at 24–32 probes on the B workstation and is an interface check, not the gate. The gate is 128 probes on the H200 and its verdict belongs in a later entry. Both corrections were made **before** any campaign and both are argued from mechanism rather than from a measured value, which is the only basis on which a frozen construction may move.

**Correction 1 — the shared substituting symbol contaminates its own control, provably.** EXP-R2-177 froze: score `wt`, `A` (i→a), `B` (j→a), `AB` (both→a). Write `B` for the log-probability a model gains when a symbol repeats an earlier one. At the planted pair `m = B − 0 − 0 + B = 2B`, because the wild type and the double mutant both carry a repeat. At a **control** pair `m = B − 0 − 0 + 0 = B`, because its double mutant *plants a new repeat that was not there*. The contrast is 2B against B rather than B against zero, and a control that acquires half the effect it exists to exclude is not a control. The repair is two distinct substituting symbols, `i→a` and `j→b`: no variant of a control pair ever repeats, so the control reads zero and the planted pair reads `m = 0 − 0 − 0 + B = B`, carried entirely by the wild type's own relation. **Both schemes are scored** at a cost of two sequences per pair, so the contamination is reported rather than asserted — measured on gpt2-large at 24 probes, control mean epistasis **+1.66 nats under the shared scheme against +0.07 under the distinct one**, against planted means of +19.71 and +6.96. The gate is read on `distinct`.

**Correction 2 — a one-symbol repeat is not a dependency any arm is claimed to have learned.** The frozen construction set `symbols[j] := symbols[i]`, a single-symbol copy at a distance. No mechanism in this programme's record keys on that: an induction mechanism keys on a repeated **context**, which one symbol does not supply, and EXP-R2-155 measured exact single-token recurrence at 0.068 per 256 tokens on ProtGPT2 — rare enough that a model has little reason to have learned it. Under that geometry **both arms sat at chance** (gpt2-large −0.07, ProtGPT2 −0.07 at 23–24 probes, top-1 at or below its 0.167 chance level). **A gate the positive control cannot pass is a specification defect, which is Appendix B rule 2's own category**, so the geometry is repaired rather than the verdict recorded. The probe now plants a repeated **8-symbol motif** and scores the aligned position inside it against its own image one separation later — `04_circuit_primitives.py`'s `[prefix][S][S]` geometry with the scored pair named rather than left implicit. Control pairs sit at the **identical separation**, outside both motif copies, and any control pair whose two symbols already agree is refused, so the within-probe permutation null is separation-matched by construction and no control is a second planted pair.

**The repair works, and the text control is what shows it.** At 24–32 probes, separation 24 symbols, 6 pairs per probe:

| arm | tokens/symbol | Spearman (distinct) | 95% CI | null q99 | top-1 | chance | planted / control mean epistasis | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| gpt2-large | word | **+0.487 … +0.602** | [+0.30, +0.65] | +0.16…+0.20 | **0.875–0.969** | 0.167 | +6.96 / +0.07 | **PASS** |
| protgpt2 | multi-residue BPE | −0.102 | [−0.32, +0.11] | +0.224 | 0.292 | 0.167 | −3.44 / −0.01 | FAIL |
| progen2-medium | 1 per residue | +0.071 | [−0.13, +0.27] | +0.177 | 0.292 | 0.167 | +0.47 / −0.01 | FAIL |

**The two protein failures are not the same failure, and the diagnostic that separates them cost nothing.** The artefact now records, per arm, the fraction of planted repeats whose two copies carry **identical tokens** in the rendered sequence:

| arm | planted repeat survives tokenisation |
|---|---:|
| gpt2-large | **1.000** |
| progen2-medium | **1.000** |
| protgpt2 | **0.083** |

**ProtGPT2's failure is an interface fact and not a statement about its computation**: in 92% of probes the two copies of an identical 8-residue span do not tokenise alike, so the probe presents no token-level repeat for an induction mechanism to key on. This independently reproduces EXP-R2-176's measurement on a different task — there, 47–55% of single substitutions left the sequence token-aligned; here, 8.3% of planted motif repeats survive. **ProGen2-medium's failure is not explained that way**: every one of its planted repeats survives as an identical token span, and it still reads inside its own null. That arm is the one whose A1 result will carry an attribution, and at 24 probes its interval is far too wide to carry one yet.

**What this does not yet say.** Nothing about D3.d's biological estimand, which no model has been scored against. Nothing about whether ProGen2-medium copies — an interval of [−0.13, +0.27] excludes almost nothing, and the frozen rule is stated at 128 probes for that reason. And nothing that licenses relaxing A1: if the full-scale run returns PASS on gpt2-large and FAIL on every protein arm, the pre-registered consequence stands — Stage 2 is not run and no downstream number is interpreted.

**Operational record.** `src/transfer/epistasis.py` and `scripts/transfer/28_epistasis_coupling.py`, both new; no file owned by another agent was modified. Stage 0's arithmetic was verified end to end on GRB2 before launch: the rebuilt alignment rows reproduce `build_profile`'s frequencies exactly and reproduce the **frozen F10 artefact** to `2.97e-08`, so the corpus channel this design inherits is provenance-checked numerically and not merely by commit history — `homology.py` and `profiles.py` carry no commit since the runs that produced it. A cohort-draw contract violation was reported by another agent and repaired at the root rather than in the test: the stage now defines `--cohort-draw-seed` defaulting to the imported `arms.DEFAULT_CORPUS_DRAW_SEED` — never a literal, and never the `or None` idiom that collapses a mistyped 0 into the file-order draw — plus `--cohort-skip` for the skip-offset window, and it is registered in the drawing-stage set because its `attainability` stage genuinely draws both constructors. `tests/test_cohort_draw_contract.py` is green at 22 passed. One serialisation defect was found by the run rather than by review: an assay too small to split in half yields an undefined reliability, and `json` refuses NaN, so the payload destroyed its own artefact after the work was done; non-finite floats are now written as `null`, which is not the same as zero and is not what a clamp would have recorded.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-180: D3.d Stage 0. The second-order retrieval channel fails its own positive control on 22 of 22 proteins, and that is the pre-registered refusal

**CPU only, no model, no GPU.** `28_epistasis_coupling.py --stage cohort`, artefact `results/transfer/epistasis/cohort.json`. EXP-R2-177 pre-declared the one way Stage 0 alone could stop Stage 2: *"if the corpus coupling channel `c` fails its own positive control — predicting `e` above its column-permutation null — on most proteins, then A3 is not interpretable on those proteins."* It fails on **all** of them.

**The cohort is exactly what EXP-R2-176 predicted.** 51 assays over **48 identity clusters**; 22 carry ≥500 corpus hits and so admit a pairwise estimate at all. The family-disjoint protocol runs through `src/transfer/families.py` on 46 accessions: Pfam 36 labelled → 29 groups → **18/18**, CATH superfamily 32 labelled → 25 groups → **17/15**. Both sides of both splits clear the eight-unit floor.

**The result.** Cross-fitted, APC-corrected column coupling against measured specific epistasis, each read against its own column-permutation null (which preserves every column's residue marginal and gap depth and destroys only the pairing):

| assay | pairs | reliability | Neff | c ~ e | null q99 | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_abundance | 1047 | 0.752 | 1585.0 | **−0.012** | +0.036 | FAIL |
| GRB2_HUMAN_Faure_2021 | 994 | 0.549 | 209.7 | **+0.006** | +0.029 | FAIL |
| PABP_YEAST_Melamed_2013 | 899 | 0.846 | 90.2 | **+0.033** | +0.094 | FAIL |
| A4_HUMAN_Seuma_2022 | 765 | 0.538 | 29.2 | **+0.039** | +0.058 | FAIL |
| YAP1_HUMAN_Araya_2012 | 303 | 0.578 | 50.7 | **+0.027** | +0.077 | FAIL |
| DLG4_HUMAN_Faure_2021 | 218 | 0.392 | 69.7 | **+0.065** | +0.102 | FAIL |
| HIS7_YEAST_Pokusaeva_2019 | 11 | 0.847 | 230.1 | +0.273 | +0.645 | FAIL |
| HECD1_HUMAN_Tsuboyama_2023_3DKM | 16 | 0.991 | 488.0 | +0.035 | +0.406 | FAIL |

**0 of 22 pass; verdict NOT_USABLE.** The six pair-rich proteins are the ones that carry the reading: on every one the coupling sits between −0.012 and +0.065 and below its own null, on referents whose split-half reliability is 0.39–0.85 and whose pair counts run to a thousand. This is not a power failure of the *referent*.

**The null structure caught the degenerate cases rather than being fooled by them, which is the part worth keeping.** Twelve assays carry 2–5 pairs, and several read a coupling of exactly **+1.000** — a Spearman over two points is ±1 by construction. Their column-permutation nulls read **+1.000** as well, so every one of them FAILS. A design that had compared those against zero, or against a chance level derived from the number of pairs, would have reported perfect corpus prediction on four proteins.

**What this bounds, stated narrowly.** It does **not** say protein corpora carry no pairwise coupling; direct-coupling analysis is a working technology. It says that *the coupling estimable from this interface* — DIAMOND hits against the staged UniRef50, reweighted as `profiles.sequence_weights` does, at the Neff those searches return — does not predict measured specific epistasis above its own construction-matched null on any protein in this benchmark. The likely proximal cause is visible in the table and is the hazard the estimator was chosen to respect: a 20×20 joint distribution at Neff 29–210 is a fraction of an effective observation per cell, and a **held-out** estimator refuses to manufacture association from that where a plug-in one would have produced it and grown it as depth fell (Appendix B rule 3, L12). The honesty and the powerlessness are the same property.

**Consequence for D3.d, and it is structural.** A3 — the second-order subtraction, the whole reason this item was admitted over F10 — cannot be built on this corpus interface. A2 remains well-posed and needs no coupling channel, but A2 alone measures whether a model's predicted epistasis beats a separation-, magnitude- and conservation-matched null; it cannot separate learned biology from corpus statistics, which is the Objective-3 bar. **Without A3 this design cannot clear the bar it was admitted for**, and that is now established at zero GPU cost rather than after Stage 2. Whether a deeper alignment (an HHblits or JackHMMER profile rather than a DIAMOND hit list) would restore the channel is a real question and is not one this stage can answer; it is recorded here and not acted on.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-181 pre-declared: the ProGen3 estimand identity, or whether the reference arm's tap is verified rather than declared

Pre-declared before running, because this arm produced every published external-baseline number and a non-zero result would be a scientific event rather than a defect report.

**Why it is being measured.** Every dense arm certifies its perturbation and replacement estimand with a live equality: `DenseReplaceable.estimand_identity` rebuilds each block's own output from the residual its normalisation read plus the intercepted feed-forward output, and refuses unless the two are bit-equal. `ProGen3Replaceable` has no such check. Its `perturbation_target` says so honestly — `identity_verified` reads "src.transfer.progen3.self_check's own gate, which is this arm's loader gate and is not the dense arms' identity check" — so nothing is disguised, but the reference arm the dense arms are compared against is certified by declaration where they are certified by measurement. That asymmetry is what this measures away.

**Configuration.** `progen3-112m` at bfloat16 on one L20, on the first two of the frozen `SELF_CHECK_SEQUENCES` — the same inputs and the same count the dense check uses. The quantity is the worst absolute difference over every layer, position and channel of `(residual + intercepted) - produced`, where `residual` is the input of each decoder layer's pre-MoE normalisation, `intercepted` is what `moe_intercept` hands its callback (the hidden-state half of ProGen3's `(hidden, router)` tuple), and `produced` is the decoder layer's own output. The tolerance is **exact**: the model performs that addition on those tensors in that dtype, so anything but equality means the block does something the interceptor does not see.

**Outcomes, declared in advance.**

- **A — the worst difference is exactly 0.** The tensor stages 15, 17 and 23 read on the reference arm IS the whole of that block's residual write, verified on the live forward pass rather than asserted. The F11 comparison then rests on the same certification on both sides. I will *propose* wiring the check into `ProGen3Replaceable.self_check` permanently and will not wire it in under this authorisation.
- **B — the worst difference is not 0.** Stop, report, interpret nothing. A non-zero value means the intercepted tensor is not the residual write the published external-baseline numbers were computed under, and what follows is not a repair decision.
- **C — the measurement cannot be built**, because the decoder layer carries no pre-MoE normalisation of the declared shape. Recorded as not-run with the structural reason and no claim in either direction.

**Bounds declared in advance.** This verifies the **interception**, not the eager-MoE conversion's numerical fidelity — a correct identity over a wrongly converted model would still be a correct identity, and the loader band is what gates that. It is measured at one dtype, one device and one batch; the identity is algebraic rather than statistical, so it is not expected to be input-dependent, but nothing here establishes that it holds under a dtype or device it was not measured on. Two sequences, matching the dense arms' own check, so this is a structural equality and not a sample.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-181 read: OUTCOME A. The ProGen3 tap is the block's residual write, verified on the live forward pass

`progen3-112m`, bfloat16, one L20, the first two frozen `SELF_CHECK_SEQUENCES`. The decoder layer carries `self_attn`, `input_layernorm`, `post_attention_layernorm`, `block_sparse_moe`, so the identity declared in the pre-registration could be built as written and outcome C does not apply.

**Result: the worst absolute difference is exactly 0.0, and it is 0.0 on every one of the ten layers individually.** `moe_intercept` already unwraps ProGen3's `(hidden_states, router_probabilities)` and hands its callback the hidden-state half, which is the tensor the reconstruction used; the residual and the block output were captured by two further independent hooks, so the equality is a reconstruction from three separately captured tensors rather than an algebraic tautology.

This is **outcome A** as pre-declared. The tensor stages 15, 17 and 23 read on the reference arm is the whole of that block's residual write, established by measurement rather than by declaration, so the F11 dense-versus-ProGen3 comparison now has the same class of certification on both sides. Nothing about the published external-baseline numbers changes: the identity holds, which is what they already assumed.

Per the pre-registration this authorises a *proposal* and not a change: the check is not wired into `ProGen3Replaceable.self_check` under this measurement, and `perturbation_target`'s honest `identity_verified` wording still stands until it is.

**What this does not establish**, restated from the pre-registration because it is the half a later reader will drop: it verifies the interception and not the eager-MoE conversion's numerical fidelity — a correct identity over a wrongly converted model would still be a correct identity, and the loader band is what gates that. One dtype, one device, one batch, two sequences; the identity is algebraic, so it is not expected to be input-dependent, but nothing here establishes it under a dtype or device it was not measured on.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-182: the four R2.3 ProLLaMA scoring cells re-dispatched and complete. Every one recovers LESS than the mean-ablation floor

The four cells that died in their causal sweep on 2026-08-11 were re-dispatched after the component-grid repair and **all four ran to completion and wrote both artefacts**. `15_replacement_faithfulness.py` on `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`, per-layer transcoders d_hidden 8192 k 32, `--sequences 128`, dictionaries read from the 2026-08-11 training run in place.

The blocker is gone: each log shows `matched pair MATCHED`, then `[grid] 32 components over ['mlp_block'], all ablatable`, then the behavioural sweep, then the causal sweep to its end. The seed-20260806 pair ran from one frozen snapshot and the seed-20260811 pair from another, taken from a worktree pinned at the same commit; the stage-15 import closure is byte-identical between them, verified by diff, so the two pairs are replicates of one code state rather than of two.

| cell | context cap | clean | replacement | fully ablated | denominator | NLL recovery | cross-model rho | causal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| protein, seed 20260806 | 1024 | 4.2082 | 6.1977 | 5.5692 | 1.3610 | **-0.4617** | -0.0029 (p 0.1297) | FAIL |
| text, seed 20260806 | 512 | 6.6221 | 10.9062 | 10.4301 | 3.8080 | **-0.1250** | -0.0411 (p 0.6898) | FAIL |
| protein, seed 20260811 | 1024 | 4.2082 | 5.8777 | 5.5692 | 1.3610 | **-0.2266** | 0.0788 (p 0.1297) | FAIL |
| text, seed 20260811 | 512 | 6.6221 | 10.8298 | 10.4301 | 3.8080 | **-0.1050** | 0.1455 (p 0.3726) | FAIL |

Every verdict is PARTIAL, every attainability is ATTAINABLE with a ceiling above 0.99, and every causal gate FAILs. **Recovery is negative in all four cells**: splicing the trained dictionary in damages the model more than deleting the block's contribution entirely and substituting its per-layer mean. That holds in both modes and at both seeds. This entry records the numbers and does not interpret them; the reading is not mine to make and the obvious candidates — a train/eval population gap, the sequential-replacement convention against the teacher-forced convention the dictionaries were fitted under, or dictionaries simply undertrained at this budget — are not separated by anything measured here.

**The context-window asymmetry must be read beside these numbers rather than inferred away.** The pair's own declaration now says so: `matched_training.comparison` reports `verdict MATCHED`, `disagreements []`, and `max_tokens [1024, 512], max_tokens_agree false`. The two dictionaries of each pair were matched on backbone, architecture, width, k, auxk, token budget, evaluation budget and the whole optimiser block, and were **not** matched on context length — 1024 tokens for protein against 512 for text, because the protein rendering pays a measured wrapper and derives its residue ceiling from that cap. No verdict here certifies equal context.

**Scope, per the ruling carried in the artefacts.** Each artefact's `condition.component_family_comparability` states that this grid carries the block family only, that a comparison against a dense arm's two-family artefact is not like-for-like and no modality claim may rest on it, and that the within-checkpoint text-versus-protein comparison IS like-for-like because both modes carry the identical block-only grid. The four cells above are that within-checkpoint comparison at two seeds.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-183: EXP-R2-168's ProGen2 ladder re-measured under the content-mask correction. The denominator moves under 1%, every damage figure reproduces exactly, and the ladder still does not order by scale

**Why this entry exists — a cross-agent contamination, confirmed rather than assumed.** EXP-R2-168 ran the ProGen2 scale ladder through `23_perturbation_sensitivity.py` between 10:31 and 11:02 (-07:00). EXP-R2-170's content-mask repair landed in commit `54f8285` at 13:12 the same day, about two and a half hours later. The repair's own blast-radius statement — "no published number moves: no ProGen2 perturbation artefact exists" — was **already false when it was committed**: twelve ProGen2 perturbation artefacts had existed since 10:31, written by a different agent. The judgement was not made true and then overtaken; it was made against a tree that already held the artefacts it denied. That is the failure mode worth naming, and it is a coordination failure rather than a defect in either piece of work.

**The mitigating fact holds, and it is EXP-R2-168 rather than EXP-R2-167 that carries it.** The task that commissioned this repair attributed the ladder to EXP-R2-167; the ladder is EXP-R2-168 (EXP-R2-167 is the dispatch-fate audit of the 2026-08-11 cells). EXP-R2-168's own words are "Status: launched and partly complete; **no conclusion is recorded**", with the reason stated: "a scale ordering read from two rungs of four, on one cohort draw, before the skip-offset condition has returned, is exactly the shape of claim this programme has retracted before." **No conclusion was drawn from the contaminated run, and none is withdrawn here.**

**The contamination is real, and the artefacts prove it themselves.** Every one of the twelve records `src/transfer/replaceable.py` = `b74d35ad8042…` and `src/transfer/arms.py` = `c5db955a8501…`, which are exactly those two files at `54f8285^`; the corrected cells record `1b202e7a7d04…` and `bcdf8f907bee…`. `scripts/transfer/23_perturbation_sensitivity.py` is byte-identical across both sets (`73dd0020eeea…`), so the stage did not change — only the mask under it. Three provenance modules differ between the two sets in total; the third, `15_replacement_faithfulness.py`, changed only by adding functions, and `mean_ablation_context`, the one thing stage 23 imports from it, is character-for-character identical. So the two sets differ in the fix and in nothing that touches this estimand.

**Which recorded quantities actually depend on the affected endpoint, read off the code rather than assumed.** `block_output_reference` is the only consumer of `content_mask` in this stage. It returns three things: the per-layer mean block output (the fully-ablated endpoint), the per-layer mean block-output norm, and the content-position count. The mean block output feeds `mean_ablation_context`, hence `mean_ablated_nats_per_token` and the denominator, hence every recovery ratio. **Nothing else depends on it.** The clean pass is unmasked, and the perturbation is applied at every position of every replaced block rather than at content positions, so `clean_nats_per_token` and every `damage_nats_per_token` are mask-independent by construction. Since `recovery = 1 − damage/denominator`, the whole correction is one scalar per cell. That is a falsifiable prediction and it was used as the check: **all 76 epsilon points across the twelve cells reproduce their damage to a maximum absolute difference of 0.000e+00**, over every individual draw, so the re-run is a controlled replacement of the denominator and not a fresh measurement that happens to agree.

**Configuration, recovered from the artefacts' `settings` and `.dispatch` blocks rather than guessed.** Four rungs × three conditions, twelve cells, every one at `--sequences 128 --batch-size 16 --protein-min-len 64 --protein-max-len 246 --draws 3 --bootstrap 1000`, `--seed` and `--cohort-draw-seed` at their defaults (20260810 / 20260728), bfloat16, `--max-tokens` 512. The three conditions are the coarse grid `0.05 0.1 0.2 0.4 0.8`; the same grid at `--cohort-skip 4000`; and the fine grid `0.5 0.6 0.7 0.9 1.1 1.4`. Snapshot `20260812135529_f9eb31c884bf`, one freeze for all twelve so the ladder runs one code state, dispatched through `scripts/transfer/run_external_baseline_h200.sh` on H200 cards 0 and 2 only, both verified idle in-pod before and 100% busy with the twelve processes after. Results under `results/transfer/external_baseline/20260812135529_f9eb31c884bf/`.

**Endpoints, old against new.** Content positions fall by exactly one per cohort record on every cell — 20,994 → 20,866 at skip 0 and 20,198 → 20,070 at skip 4,000 — which is the direct signature of the marker leaving the span.

| rung | condition | clean old → new | mean-ablated old → new | denominator old → new | ratio |

| progen2-small | coarse | 2.0026 → 2.0026 | 2.9684 → 2.9673 | 0.9657 → 0.9647 | 0.9989 |
| progen2-small | coarse, skip 4000 | 2.0908 → 2.0908 | 2.9561 → 2.9519 | 0.8653 → 0.8610 | 0.9951 |
| progen2-small | fine | 2.0026 → 2.0026 | 2.9684 → 2.9673 | 0.9657 → 0.9647 | 0.9989 |
