The clean endpoint reproduces to every printed digit on all twelve, as the mask-independence argument requires. The denominator moves between −0.49% and +0.84%, and it moves in **both** directions — down on `progen2-small` and `progen2-large`, up on `progen2-xlarge` — so this is not a bias with a sign.

**The per-layer breakdown, which is where the correction is large.** The mean block-output norm — the anchor a relative epsilon is read against — measured on the coarse-grid draw, as relative change new/old:

| rung | layer 1 | layer 2 | worst other layer | median |other layers| |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| progen2-small (12L) | **−23.4%** | **−15.8%** | −0.7% | 0.1% |
| progen2-medium (27L) | **−21.5%** | **−18.4%** | −2.8% | 0.2% |
| progen2-large (32L) | **−26.7%** | **−27.0%** | −5.5% | 0.6% |
| progen2-xlarge (32L) | **−31.7%** | **−25.3%** | −1.7% | 0.2% |

Two things this adds to EXP-R2-170, which measured one arm on 32 records. The layer-1/layer-2 displacement **reproduces on all four rungs at 128 records** and grows mildly with depth. And `progen2-large` carries a second affected band that a single-arm check did not show: layers 21–31 move −2.1% to −5.5%, an order of magnitude above the other rungs' deep layers. So "layers 1 and 2, and nothing else" is a `progen2-small` statement, not a lineage statement.

**Why a 25% displacement of the endpoint vector produces a sub-1% change in the ratio.** The mean block output is a vector, and the marker's block output at layers 1–2 is large in norm and far from the residue bulk, so dropping one position per record swings the mean a long way there. The mean-ablated cross-entropy is a scalar over all layers ablated at once, and layers 1–2 of a 12-to-32-layer stack carry a small share of the damage that full ablation does. The two facts are consistent, and reporting only the second would have hidden the first. **The general lesson: a relative-norm displacement of an intermediate quantity is not a bound on the displacement of the statistic that consumes it, in either direction.**

**No qualitative reading changes.** The largest recovery change anywhere in the ladder is **0.0069** (`progen2-xlarge`, fine grid, ε = 1.4, −0.1035 → −0.0966); the next largest is 0.0060. **Every** superseded recovery value falls inside the corresponding corrected cell's 95% bootstrap interval — zero exceptions over all draw-level points — so the correction is smaller than this measurement's own resampling noise. The rung ordering by recovery is identical old and new at every epsilon in every one of the three conditions, without exception.

**And the ladder still does not support a scale ordering, which was true before the correction and is true after it.** At every epsilon above 0.05, in all three conditions, both before and after, the order is `xlarge > medium > large > small`. That is **not monotone in parameter count**: `progen2-medium` (765M) is more perturbation-tolerant than `progen2-large` (2.78B) at every magnitude measured, in both cohort draws. Correcting the mask did not create this inversion and did not remove it. What the ladder now supports is the weaker pair of statements that the smallest rung is the least tolerant and the largest the most, with the two middle rungs inverted against size, on one lineage, one cohort band and two draws — and depth and width co-vary across the rungs, so even a clean ordering would not have isolated scale from depth. EXP-R2-168's two blockers stand unchanged: this lineage's perturbation target is a parallel GPT-J block's feed-forward output rather than the GPT-2 arms' sequential block output, and the loader band cannot separate a ProGen2 arm rendered without its direction marker. **No scale claim is recorded here.**

**The superseded artefacts, handled to the precedent this repository already set.** Twelve contaminated cells moved, none deleted, none overwritten, following `results/transfer_20260730/_superseded/` (Appendix B standing rule 18): `results/transfer/external_baseline/20260812102519_a322a416b8e9/_superseded/` (one cell) and `…/20260812103809_88b29c1d6286/_superseded/` (eleven), each with a README naming the defect, the commit that fixed it, the provenance hashes that date the files, how much the correction moved, and where the replacement is. Two of the twelve — `progen2-large_fine` and `progen2-medium_fine` — had completed on the pod on 2026-08-12 and were never pulled; they were pulled before the move, so the superseded record is the complete twelve cells rather than the ten that had reached B. The corrected cells keep the identical labels: the run id's trailing segment is the code hash, so the path already distinguishes the two sets, and identical labels are what makes the pairing unambiguous.

**Two aborted dispatches, recorded because both guards worked and one hazard is a repeat.** The first attempt lost eleven of twelve cells to backgrounding a compound `&&` list, which swallowed the exports into the first subshell — the identical failure EXP-R2-167's operational note records, reproduced by a different agent five hours later, which suggests the note is not where a launcher will look. The one cell that did carry the environment was refused by the snapshot-reuse guard, because another agent had changed the tree between the freeze and the launch. A second attempt was refused on all twelve for the same reason: the repository's code hash moved twice inside the ~4.5 minutes a freeze takes (`4992200f6342` → `244e0e47f6a9` → `f9eb31c884bf`), which is faster than a campaign can be frozen. Neither attempt wrote a dispatch record, scheduled a pod process or touched a GPU. The resolution was to point `REPO_ROOT` at a session-scoped copy of the checkout so the hash could not move under the freeze, with `LOCAL_OUTPUT_ROOT` left on the real tree so dispatch records and pulled results land where an operator reads them — the separation the driver already declares, used for the purpose it was declared for. **This is a live operational limit worth stating plainly: with several agents editing concurrently, freeze-then-reuse is not reliable against the working tree, and one campaign one snapshot requires a pinned source.** One cell's pull then failed on the shared relay under twelve concurrent transfers (`Connection timed out during banner exchange`); it was pulled by hand and its digest verified identical on both sides.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-184: D3.d A1 at full scale. The instrument is validated on the text control and returns a tight null on a residue-tokenised protein arm

**What was run.** `28_epistasis_coupling.py --stage attainability`, one cell carrying all three arms on one H200 so the code hash is identical across the comparison by construction (EXP-R2-173's lesson), snapshot `20260812141205_7087d6409578`, 128 probes per arm, 8 pairs per probe, planted motif 8 symbols, separation 24 symbols, 2000 null draws and 2000 probe bootstrap draws, float32 statistics. Artefact admitted to `results/transfer/epistasis/a1_full/attainability.json`. The decision rule is EXP-R2-177's, frozen before any model was loaded, with the two construction repairs of EXP-R2-179 — both made before any campaign and both argued from mechanism rather than from a measured value.

| arm | tokens/symbol | planted repeat survives tokenisation | Spearman | 95% CI | null q99 | top-1 | chance | planted / control mean epistasis | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| gpt2-large | word | **1.000** | **+0.5529** | [+0.5286, +0.5701] | +0.0691 | **0.969** | 0.125 | **+8.594** / +0.057 | **PASS** |
| progen2-medium | 1 per residue | **1.000** | +0.0369 | [−0.0245, +0.1003] | +0.0680 | 0.172 | 0.125 | +0.518 / −0.028 | FAIL |
| protgpt2 | multi-residue BPE | **0.211** | +0.0098 | [−0.0645, +0.0888] | +0.0712 | 0.297 | 0.125 | −0.326 / +0.059 | FAIL |

**A1 returns FAIL on its conjunction, and the pre-registered consequence stands**: the rule required PASS on gpt2-large *and* on at least one protein arm. Stage 2 is not run and no downstream number is interpreted. That consequence is in any case moot — EXP-R2-180 had already halted A3, which was the reason D3.d was admitted over F10.

**The instrument is validated, and that is the result worth keeping.** On the text control the same estimator, the same arithmetic, the same within-probe permutation null and the same bootstrap recover a planted coupling at **+0.5529 with a bootstrap interval eight times the null's 99th percentile**, retrieving the planted pair first in **124 of 128 probes** against a chance level of 0.125, at a planted-minus-control epistasis of **+8.59 against +0.06 nats**. A null returned by this instrument is a measurement and not a shrug.

**ProGen2-medium's null is now tight enough to carry an attribution, which is what the full-scale run was for.** At 24 probes its interval was [−0.13, +0.27] and excluded almost nothing; at 128 it is **[−0.025, +0.100]**, its point estimate sits *inside* its own null (q99 +0.068), and its top-1 rate of 0.172 is barely above its 0.125 chance. Every one of its planted repeats survives tokenisation, so no interface excuse is available: on an arm whose tokenizer preserves the planted relation exactly, an 8-residue repeat at separation 24 does not register as predicted epistasis at more than about a fifth of the text control's effect, and the interval excludes anything larger.

**ProtGPT2's failure remains interface-confounded and is not attributable to its computation.** Only **21%** of planted repeats survive its tokenizer — 79% of identical 8-residue spans do not tokenise alike in their two copies — so for four probes in five the geometry presents no token-level repeat for an induction mechanism to key on. This is the third independent measurement of the same constraint on this arm, after EXP-R2-176's 47–55% single-substitution alignment and EXP-R2-179's 8.3% at smoke scale.

**The alternative explanation this run does not exclude, stated because it is the strongest one available against the reading above.** A planted exact repeat is far more off-distribution for a protein decoder than for a text decoder: repeated words are ordinary English, whereas an exact 8-residue repeat at 24 residues' separation is rare in real sequences. ProGen2-medium's null may therefore reflect the probe being off-distribution for it rather than an absent mechanism — the same objection `dialogpt-small` was built to answer for the induction census, and no analogous control was run here. One geometry was tested; a longer motif or a different separation is untested. **The defensible statement is bounded accordingly: at this geometry, on this arm, the planted coupling does not register above the arm's own null, and why it does not is open.**

**Operational record.** The freeze emitted `RUN_ID` and `SNAPSHOT_DIR` and its import closure pulled in `src/__init__.py` beside the two new files, so the snapshot carries the code that ran. Both new files are untracked additions; no file owned by another agent was modified. The first attempt to read the freeze output failed because the harness writes a background task's output to a path that is not shared with the compute side — recorded because it looked exactly like a silent freeze failure and was not one. GPU occupancy was probed inside the pod rather than read from the launcher's exit code (L20): all four cards read 0 MiB after dispatch, which was **not** the failure it resembled — the job had already finished, writing its artefact 60 seconds after launch. "LAUNCHED with idle cards" is ambiguous between a job that never started and one that finished before the probe, and only the artefact's timestamp separates them.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-185: ProtGPT2's tokenisation constraint, consolidated. Three tasks, three measurements, one structural fact

**Why this entry exists rather than a fourth rediscovery.** The same constraint was measured three independent ways today, each time inside a different investigation, each time reported as a scope limit on that investigation. It is not an incidental property of any one estimand. It is a structural fact about **the only panel arm whose pretraining corpus is exactly identified**, and therefore the only arm on which a retrieval subtraction is identified rather than bounded (F10). This entry gathers the three measurements in one citable place so the fourth investigation reads them instead of repeating them.

| task | what was required of the tokenisation | ProtGPT2 | residue-tokenised arms | text control |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| single-substitution position alignment (EXP-R2-176) | mutant and wild type token-aligned with exactly one token differing | **0.470–0.545** | 1.000 (zymctrl, progen2-medium) | — |
| planted 8-residue motif repeat, smoke (EXP-R2-179) | the two copies of an identical span carry identical tokens | **0.083** | 1.000 (progen2-medium) | 1.000 (gpt2-large) |
| planted 8-residue motif repeat, 128 probes (EXP-R2-184) | as above | **0.211** | 1.000 (progen2-medium) | 1.000 (gpt2-large) |

**The general statement.** ProtGPT2's multi-residue BPE assigns tokens by sequence context, so *the same residue content at a different phase offset need not tokenise the same way*. Two consequences follow, and they are different in kind:

- **Position-level interventions are undefined on part of the cohort.** An activation patch at "residue *i*" needs the two runs token-aligned outside the mutated span, and roughly half of single substitutions do not provide that.
- **Content-level relations can be destroyed before the model sees them.** An exact repeat planted in residue space is not an exact repeat in token space four times out of five, so a probe built to present a copy relation presents none.

**The trap, and it is the reason this is a fact worth publishing rather than a caveat worth appending.** The retained fraction is **not a random subsample**: it is the subset whose local sequence context happens to be BPE-stable, which is a property of composition. So an estimand computed on the survivors is computed on a biased cohort, and its failure or success on ProtGPT2 is not attributable until the retained and dropped halves are compared on whatever the estimand is sensitive to — conservation, effect size, composition. In EXP-R2-184 this is exactly what separates the two protein failures: ProGen2-medium preserves every planted repeat and still reads inside its own null, so its result carries an attribution; ProtGPT2 does not, so its result carries none.

**What is not claimed.** Nothing here says ProtGPT2 lacks a copying mechanism or lacks pairwise structure — the measurements are about what the *interface* presents to it, not about its computation, and no estimand that survives its tokenisation has been run for comparison. Sequence-likelihood estimands are untouched by all of this, because a likelihood needs no alignment; the constraint binds position-level and content-relational designs only.

**The operational rule this supports.** Any position-level or content-relational estimand that admits ProtGPT2 should report the surviving fraction beside its result, and should compare the retained against the dropped instances before attributing a failure to the arm. Both are cheap: the diagnostic in `28_epistasis_coupling.py` costs one tokenisation per probe and no forward pass.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-186 pre-declared: the layer-count sweep of the replacement front, and what each branch would license

Pre-declared before running, and the uniformity of EXP-R2-182's result across two modes and two seeds is why: a result that consistent invites a reading, and the reading is exactly what has to be fixed in advance.

**The question.** EXP-R2-182 found NLL recovery negative in all four cells — splicing the trained dictionary in damages the model more than deleting every block's contribution and substituting its per-layer mean. Three candidates were named there and none was separated: the fitted/scored convention gap, a train/eval population gap, and dictionaries simply undertrained at this budget. This sweep addresses the first and only the first.

**The asymmetry it prices.** The dictionaries are fitted **teacher-forced**, on each block's true input and true output. The behavioural number is measured under **sequential replacement**, where every block reads a residual stream the replacements above it have already perturbed. Error can compound across 32 layers under the second convention and cannot under the first. The mean-ablation endpoint the ratio divides by does not compound either: substituting a fixed per-layer mean is a stable corruption at every depth. So a dictionary that is genuinely good per layer can still be worse than mean ablation once spliced through the whole stack, and reading that as a fact about the dictionary would confuse the method with the convention it was scored under.

**Configuration.** `15_replacement_faithfulness.py` with `--replacement-front 1,2,4,8,16,32`, on all four EXP-R2-182 cells, same dictionaries, same cohort, same `--sequences 128`. Each front is an extra condition of the *same* behavioural sweep, so every row shares the batches, the clean and fully-ablated endpoints, and the `original` distribution the KL is taken against. The `k = 32` row must reproduce the headline replacement exactly; that identity is asserted in `tests/test_fitness_and_replacement_gates.py` and is the invariant the whole reading rests on, because a row is only comparable with the headline if the deepest row *is* the headline.

**Branch A — recovery is positive (or materially less negative) at small k and falls monotonically with depth, reaching the headline value at k = 32.** The compounding is real and priced, and the convention gap is a sufficient explanation of the negative headline. What it licenses: the headline recovery may not be read as "the dictionary failed to capture the block", because the quantity is then partly a property of the sequential convention rather than of the dictionary. What it does **not** license: any claim that the dictionaries are good. A per-layer-adequate dictionary that cannot survive its own composition is still unusable for a sequential replacement, and this branch says where the number comes from, not that the method works.

**Branch B — recovery is already negative at k = 1.** Compounding is excluded: a single replaced block reads a clean stream and has nothing to compound with, so the damage is present in one block's substitution alone. The convention candidate is removed and the remaining two — population gap and undertraining — stand unseparated. Per the authorisation this branch **stops here**: the follow-up that would separate them (reconstruction NMSE on the scoring cohort against the held-out figure) is not run in this pass, and no preference among the survivors is recorded.

**Branch C — anything else**, including non-monotone depth curves, recovery negative at k = 1 but rising with depth, or the k = 32 row failing to reproduce the headline. The last of those is a specification defect and voids the run rather than being reported as a result. The other shapes are reported as measured with the convention candidate neither removed nor established, because a trend that is not monotone in depth is not the compounding this sweep was built to price.

**Bounds declared in advance.** Six fronts on a 32-layer model, so the depth curve is sampled and not resolved; a front is a prefix of blocks and never an arbitrary subset, so nothing here speaks to *which* layers carry the damage. It measures one cohort at one size, the same one EXP-R2-182 used, so it inherits that cohort's draw. And it is a behavioural measurement only: no causal or attainability quantity is recomputed, and the artefacts' other gates are whatever the re-run produces.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-187 pre-declared: resampling intervals on EXP-R2-186's layer-count sweep, and what will count as a real reversal

Written before the run and before any interval exists, because the quantity at issue is whether a reversal survives resampling and that is exactly the judgement a reader is entitled to see fixed in advance.

**The gap this closes.** EXP-R2-186's front rows are point estimates with no resampling interval, and its own bounds paragraph says so. Its Branch C reading — the depth curve is not monotone in any cell — rests on six adjacent-step increases, of which the three protein ones are +0.009 to +0.064 against a total fall of about 1.3 and cannot be separated from noise by anything that run measured, while the three text ones (+0.287, +0.329, +0.138) are an order of magnitude larger. So the interesting half of EXP-R2-186 currently stands on two cells rather than four, and this run decides which. It recomputes nothing about the model: same cohort, same dictionaries, same endpoints, same `--sequences 128`, same `--replacement-front 1,2,4,8,16,32` as EXP-R2-182 and EXP-R2-186, so the three are one series.

**The estimator is the one already in use, not a new one.** `_paired_recovery` is this stage's convention for the headline replacement and it is taken unchanged: one index set of cohort sequences drawn with replacement per replicate, shared by the clean endpoint, the mean-ablated endpoint and every front, so a difference between two fronts is a paired difference on the same sequences; 1000 replicates, the stage default and EXP-R2-186's setting; a 2.5/97.5 percentile interval; a replicate discarded when its resampled denominator is not positive; and `bootstrap_unit_floor`'s eight-unit floor, which 128 cohort sequences clear, with the intervals withheld rather than published if it ever does not. The generator is seeded with the run's own `--seed` and given the run's own replicate count, so **the `k = 32` column is the headline's bootstrap column value for value** and its interval must equal `paired_per_sequence.recovery_interval` exactly rather than merely agree with it to a few digits. That is the specification check extended from the point to the interval, and it is asserted in `tests/test_fitness_and_replacement_gates.py` beside the existing point identity.

Paired rather than marginal, and the reason matters: the six fronts are six manipulations of one cohort, not six samples of a population. Reading non-overlap of the rows' own intervals would be the unpaired comparison this stage already refuses for the three headline conditions.

**The separation criterion, declared now.** For a step from front `k` to a deeper front `k'`, let Δ = recovery(`k'`) − recovery(`k`) resampled on the shared index sets.

- **INCREASE — the reversal is real.** The 95% percentile interval of Δ lies entirely above zero. Nothing weaker will be called a surviving reversal; in particular a positive point estimate is not one.
- **UNRESOLVED — the interval covers zero.** This is reported as *unresolved*, never as absent: it says this cohort at this size cannot separate the step from zero, and it is not evidence that the step does not exist. A cell whose reversals are all unresolved does **not** thereby become a monotone cell.
- **DECREASE — the interval lies entirely below zero.** Expected for the ordinary falling steps, and reported for them because it is the control that makes an UNRESOLVED verdict readable: if the large falls separate and the small rises do not, the instrument has resolution at this cohort size and the rises are simply smaller than it. If a step whose point estimate is *positive* ever returned DECREASE, that would be a percentile interval sitting against its own point estimate, and it would be recorded as a defect indicator rather than as a refutation of the reversal.

**Threshold discipline.** The 95% level is a threshold, so `fraction_of_replicates_positive` is recorded for every step and the verdict can be re-read at any level. The primary family is the six adjacent-step increases EXP-R2-186 named: protein s06 at 2→4 and 4→8, protein s11 at 4→8, text s06 at 8→16, text s11 at 8→16 and 16→32. Over six comparisons the Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 5% level is a positive fraction above 0.99583; a step that clears the uncorrected 95% but not that level will be reported as separated at the uncorrected level and not separated under the six-comparison correction, and will not be promoted past that wording. Every ordered pair of fronts is reported and not only the adjacent ones, because EXP-R2-186's emphatic sentence is about `k = 8` against `k = 32` in text s11 and those are not neighbours on a grid that doubles.

**What each outcome licenses.** Six adjacent reversals INCREASE: the non-monotonicity finding stands on four cells. Only the text ones: it stands on **two** cells, and the protein cells are recorded as unresolved — a narrowing of EXP-R2-186's reading, not a refutation of it. None: the sweep resolves neither monotonicity nor its failure past `k = 1`, and this must not be read as Branch A, because Branch A required a monotone fall to be *shown* rather than merely left un-refuted. In every outcome Branch B stays excluded and the convention candidate stays neither removed nor established: nothing here can adjudicate the cause, and the reconstruction-NMSE follow-up is not run.

**Bounds.** The `k = 32` point estimates must reproduce EXP-R2-186 bit-exactly; any deviation is a defect in this change and voids the run rather than being reported as a finding. The bootstrap resamples cohort sequences and therefore prices cohort-sampling noise **only** — not the dictionary's training seed, not the cohort draw seed, not the model's own stochasticity. The two dictionary seeds appear as two cells and are not a resampling of a seed population, so an interval here says nothing about how a third dictionary would behave. Every bound EXP-R2-186 declared is inherited unchanged: six fronts on 32 layers samples the curve, a front is always a prefix, and it is one cohort at one size.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-188 pre-declared: the replacement-front sweep on panel arms, and what reproduction and non-reproduction each license

Written before the campaign is frozen and before any front row exists on a panel arm. The question is one of **scope, not of cause**, and nothing here may adjudicate why a curve turns.

**The question.** EXP-R2-186 and EXP-R2-187 found the recovery-versus-front curve non-monotone in all four cells of one joint checkpoint: six adjacent steps recover *more* when *more* blocks are replaced, every one separated above zero on the paired criterion. That finding currently rests on **one checkpoint (`ProLLaMA_Stage_1`), one dictionary family at 2x expansion, one cohort, one draw and six sampled fronts**, and D2.h already declares those absolute numbers non-comparable with the panel's 12x results. So it is not yet decidable whether non-monotonicity is a property of that checkpoint and that dictionary family, or a general property of prefix replacement that anyone reading a layerwise replacement result should know about. This run puts the same sweep on panel arms where the replacement gate actually carries claims (F11).

**Arms, and why these.** `gpt2-large` is the text control and is the arm the licence turns on. **The protein arm is `protgpt2`, because it is the only protein arm architecturally matched to `gpt2-large` — 36 blocks by 1280 wide, the same 12x dictionary width of 15360, the same 128-sequence cohort protocol — so a front of `k` blocks is the same prefix depth on both arms and the two depth curves are commensurable step for step, and its replacement cell is the most characterised protein cell in the panel (four cohort bands, four token caps, a 512-sequence replicate and a matched-perturbation null) with no outstanding dictionary-undertraining objection.** Two **secondary** cells run on the same freeze because the cards are otherwise idle: `gpt2` (12 blocks, a second depth on the text side) and `zymctrl` (36 blocks, one token per residue, a second protein tokenisation and corpus, its undertraining objection closed by EXP-R2-153). They are declared secondary now, before any number: **they cannot change the licence below**, they can only show whether whatever the primary pair says is stable across a second depth and a second protein tokenisation.

**The panel contract does not cover this stage.** `arm_can_run` was consulted rather than improvised, and `15_replacement_faithfulness.py` is not one of the thirteen stages it declares — it is an external-baseline stage that takes `--arm` directly. Eligibility here is therefore the stronger fact that each of the four arms already has a completed stage-15 artefact under a locally trained dictionary, which is what the deepest front must reproduce.

**Configuration — the headline cells' own, plus one flag.** Each cell repeats its published dispatch exactly and adds `--replacement-front`: `--sequences 128`, `--batch-size 8`, `--seed 20260806`, `--bootstrap 1000`, `--cohort-draw-seed 20260728`, `--cohort-skip 0`, bfloat16, `--max-tokens` 512 (1024 for `zymctrl`, its own published setting), protein band 64–246, and the same dictionary checkpoint file. Fronts are `1,2,4,8,16,32,36` on the three 36-block arms and `1,2,4,8,12` on `gpt2`; the deepest front is that arm's depth in every cell, because a row is only commensurable with the headline if the deepest row *is* the headline. The extra `32` row on the 36-block arms keeps EXP-R2-186's doubling ladder intact beneath the full-stack row.

**The estimator is the one already in use and no second one is built.** `replacement_front_sweep` over `_front_recovery_draws`, which is `_paired_recovery`'s construction: one index set of cohort sequences drawn with replacement per replicate, shared by the clean endpoint, the mean-ablated endpoint and every front, so a difference between two fronts is a paired difference on the same sequences; **1000 replicates**, the stage default and EXP-R2-186's and EXP-R2-187's setting; a 2.5/97.5 percentile interval; a replicate discarded when its resampled denominator is not positive; and `bootstrap_unit_floor`'s **eight-unit floor**, which 128 cohort sequences clear, with intervals withheld rather than published if it ever does not. The generator takes the run's own `--seed` and replicate count.

**The specification check, and the condition that voids the run.** The `k = n_layers` row must reproduce that arm's existing headline replacement **bit-exactly**, and its interval must equal the artefact's own `paired_per_sequence.recovery_interval` digit for digit. The targets are fixed now: `gpt2-large` **0.9321635877022579** [0.9285889006869075, 0.9352264731835819]; `protgpt2` **0.1641057184070633** [0.1443978127634732, 0.18361958554046348]; `gpt2` **0.9091401539331156** [0.9036567255983076, 0.913606398170753]; `zymctrl` **0.09161341115464118** [0.0844700737425026, 0.0992435736857176]. Each of these already reproduced bit-exactly once across a three-day code gap and an added three-condition control (2026-08-07/09 against the 2026-08-10 perturbation-null runs), so bit-exactness is the demonstrated behaviour of this stage on these arms and not a hope. **Any deviation is a defect in this setup and voids the run for the question it was launched for**; it will be reported as a defect and localised, and no curve will be read from a cell whose deepest row is not its own headline.

**The separation criterion, inherited verbatim from EXP-R2-187 rather than restated loosely.** For a step from front `k` to a deeper front `k'`, let Δ = recovery(`k'`) − recovery(`k`) resampled on the shared index sets. **INCREASE** — the 95% percentile interval of Δ lies entirely above zero; nothing weaker counts, and a positive point estimate alone is not a reversal. **UNRESOLVED** — the interval covers zero; this says *this cohort at this size cannot separate the step from zero*, never that the step is absent, and a cell whose reversals are all unresolved does not thereby become a monotone cell. **DECREASE** — the interval lies entirely below zero; reported for the ordinary falling steps because it is what makes an UNRESOLVED readable, since an instrument that resolves the falls has resolution at this cohort size.

**Attainability before application, discharged inside the same campaign.** The text control runs the identical procedure at the same time, and **the condition for reading any protein UNRESOLVED is that `gpt2-large`'s own falling steps return DECREASE.** If the text control cannot resolve its own falls, the sweep has no demonstrated resolution on a panel arm and no verdict of any kind is read from the protein cells.

**A resolution asymmetry declared in advance, because it is where this run differs most from EXP-R2-186.** On the joint checkpoint every cell fell by about 1.3 in recovery from `k = 1` to the full stack. Here the falls are wildly unequal: `gpt2-large` recovers 0.932 at full depth, so its total fall from a near-perfect one-block front can be only about 0.07, while `protgpt2` falls to 0.164 and `zymctrl` to 0.092. **The same absolute cohort noise is therefore a far larger fraction of the text control's curve than of the protein arms'**, so an UNRESOLVED on `gpt2-large` is weaker evidence of absence than an UNRESOLVED on `protgpt2`, and this asymmetry is stated now so it cannot be discovered later as a convenience.

**Threshold discipline and the declared family.** `fraction_of_replicates_positive` is recorded for every step, so the verdict can be re-read at any level. The **primary family is the twelve adjacent steps of the two primary arms** — six on `gpt2-large` (1→2, 2→4, 4→8, 8→16, 16→32, 32→36) and six on `protgpt2`. Over twelve comparisons the Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 5% level is a positive fraction above **0.9979167**; a step clearing the uncorrected 95% but not that level is reported as separated at the uncorrected level and not under the twelve-comparison correction, and is not promoted past that wording. Every ordered pair of fronts is reported as well, because a bracketed rise need not sit on neighbouring rungs of a doubling grid. **If reproduction rests only on a non-adjacent pair**, the family is all ordered pairs of the two primary arms — 21 each, 42 — and the corrected level is a positive fraction above **0.9994048**; that substitution is declared here rather than chosen afterwards. The secondary arms are reported at the uncorrected level with their own within-cell correction beside it.

**What counts as reproduction.** Non-monotonicity reproduces on an arm when **at least one ordered pair of fronts `k < k'` has a paired Δ interval lying entirely above zero** — the same object EXP-R2-187 measured. Adjacent steps are the primary family; if the only separated pair on an arm is non-adjacent, that is still reproduction and will be said explicitly to rest on a non-adjacent bracket.

**What each outcome licenses.**

- **R — it reproduces on `gpt2-large`.** Non-monotonicity of the prefix-replacement curve is a property of **the method**, not of the joint checkpoint or its 2x dictionary family: it is demonstrated on the text control, and under §5's organising rule a limitation demonstrated on the text control is a property of the method. This earns a **limitations-catalogue entry, proposed to the canonical audit and not written by me** — that a layerwise or prefix replacement curve may not be assumed to fall monotonically in depth, so a shallow-front recovery is not an upper bound on a deeper one and a partial-depth replacement result cannot be extrapolated to full depth in either direction.
- **N — it reproduces on neither panel arm**, with `gpt2-large`'s falling steps returning DECREASE so the instrument is shown to resolve. Non-monotonicity stays a property of the ProLLaMA joint checkpoint and its dictionary family, no catalogue entry is earned, and this is **not** a refutation of EXP-R2-186 or EXP-R2-187, which stand on their own four cells with their own intervals. The honest wording is: not reproduced on two panel arms at this cohort size, with the per-step intervals published so a reader can see how much room is left.
- **S′ — text yes, protein no.** The licence is the same as R, because the text control alone carries it. `protgpt2`'s non-reproduction is recorded per its own intervals as UNRESOLVED or DECREASE and **is not read as a modality difference**: one protein arm, one cohort, one draw, one dictionary, and this panel's single-protein-arm structure cannot support a modality coefficient anyway.
- **S — protein yes, text no.** The likeliest messy case, and the reason it is written now. Reproduction on `protgpt2` alone does **not** establish a method property under this programme's own rule, and it is exactly the shape of claim that has been retracted here before. It would be recorded as: present on the joint checkpoint and on one protein panel arm, not separated on the text control at this cohort size, with the text control's own resolution reported so that "absent" and "unresolved" stay distinguishable — a named open question, no catalogue entry, and no protein-specific reading, since a single protein arm cannot separate arm from modality.
- **Degenerate** — if the unit floor withholds intervals in any cell, that cell is reported as unmeasured rather than as a null, and it contributes to no outcome above.

**Bounds declared in advance.** Seven fronts on 36 blocks (five on 12) samples the depth curve rather than resolving it. A front is always a **prefix**, so nothing here can say *which* blocks carry any change. One cohort at one draw per arm, inherited from each headline cell along with its draw, and **no skip-offset condition is run**, so the cohort-draw sensitivity of these curves is untested. **One dictionary per arm** — unlike the joint sweep, which had two seeds per mode — so nothing here speaks to dictionary-seed variability, and the bootstrap prices **cohort-sampling noise only**: not the dictionary training seed, not the cohort draw seed, not the model's own stochasticity. A separated interval bounds the **sign, not the importance**, which is the error the joint tables most invited and will invite again here, most of all on `gpt2-large`, whose whole curve lives inside 0.07 of recovery. Nothing in this run recomputes a causal or attainability quantity for its own sake, no cause is adjudicated, and the reconstruction-NMSE follow-up is still not run.

**The two secondary cells, which cannot change the licence and agree with it.** `gpt2` (12 blocks): +0.998454 → +0.996591 → +0.980172 → +0.949374 → +0.909140, four adjacent steps at −0.001863 [−0.002238, −0.001463], −0.016420 [−0.017538, −0.015344], −0.030798 [−0.032862, −0.028981] and −0.040234 [−0.043326, −0.037755], all DECREASE with no replicate positive. `zymctrl` (36 blocks): +0.933902 → +0.750766 → +0.383474 → +0.205230 → +0.106844 → +0.092972 → +0.091613, six adjacent steps from −0.183136 [−0.222723, −0.147824] down to −0.001358 [−0.002010, −0.000687], all DECREASE with no replicate positive.

**Outcome N, and the count that carries it. Over all 73 ordered pairs of fronts across the four cells there is not one INCREASE.** Seventy-two separate below zero and one is UNRESOLVED. On the text control every one of its 21 ordered pairs is DECREASE, so the pre-declared attainability condition is met and the protein cells' verdicts are readable. **Non-monotonicity does not reproduce on `gpt2-large` and does not reproduce on `protgpt2`, so per the pre-registration it is not established as a property of the method and stays a property of the ProLLaMA joint checkpoint and its 2x dictionary family. No limitations-catalogue entry is earned.**

**This is not a refutation of EXP-R2-186 or EXP-R2-187, and the wording matters.** Those four cells were measured on their own checkpoint with their own intervals and every one of their six reversals had all 1000 replicates positive; nothing here reaches them. What is now known is narrower and is the thing that was missing: the phenomenon does not travel to the panel arms where the replacement gate carries claims, at this cohort size, on these dictionaries. The scope of the finding is one checkpoint family, not layerwise replacement in general.

**The resolution behind the null, because "no reversal" is only worth something with a resolution attached.** The text control separates an adjacent step of **−0.000133** with a paired interval half-width of **0.000079**. That is **66 times smaller** than the smallest reversal that survived resampling on the joint checkpoint (+0.0088) and about **2,500 times smaller** than the largest (+0.329). A reversal of either size on `gpt2-large` would have been seen with enormous margin, and none is there. `gpt2` resolves −0.001863 at a half-width of 0.000388 and `zymctrl` −0.001358 at 0.000662, both far finer than +0.0088. This is a measured null, not a shrug.

**The one UNRESOLVED, reported as the convention requires and not rounded away.** `protgpt2`'s shallowest step, `k = 1` → `k = 2`, has a **positive point estimate of +0.004957** with 87.6% of replicates positive and a paired interval of [−0.004454, +0.011875] that covers zero. Per the pre-declared rule this says *this cohort at this size cannot separate that step from zero*, and never that the step is absent — so **`protgpt2` is not a clean monotone cell**. Two things bound how much that concedes. The 0.8760 positive fraction is below the uncorrected 95% and far below the twelve-comparison Bonferroni level of 0.9979167, so it is not a near miss at any declared level. And the interval's half-width there, 0.008165, is about **1.8 times wider** than the interval that resolved the joint checkpoint's smallest surviving reversal, so this step **cannot exclude a reversal of that magnitude** — which is exactly why it is reported as unresolved rather than counted as evidence of monotonicity. Every other pair on that arm, including all five deeper adjacent steps and all fifteen non-adjacent ones, separates below zero.

**What does transfer is the other half of EXP-R2-186, and it transfers cleanly.** At a one-block front recovery is **0.9984 and 0.9998 on the two text arms and 0.9318 and 0.9339 on the two protein arms**, against 0.87–0.96 on the joint checkpoint's four cells. So "a single replaced block recovers nearly all of the mean-ablation gap, and the damage that the headline reports is a property of composition rather than of one block's reconstruction" holds on six cells across three checkpoint families and both modalities. That is the portable statement in this series; the non-monotonicity is not.

**One descriptive difference between the two modalities' curves, recorded as description and not as a claim.** Over the whole stack `gpt2-large` loses 0.068 of recovery and `gpt2` 0.089, while `protgpt2` loses 0.768 and `zymctrl` 0.842 — the F11 separation seen as a depth curve rather than as an endpoint. The protein arms also lose it unevenly: `zymctrl` is already down to +0.383 by `k = 4`, and `protgpt2` loses 0.496 of its total 0.768 in the single step from `k = 8` to `k = 16`. This is a **conditional marginal** — the change from adding blocks 9–16 *given* that 1–8 are already replaced — and a front is always a prefix, so it is not an attribution of damage to those blocks and nothing here says which blocks carry it.

**No cause is adjudicated, and one tempting inference is refused explicitly.** On all four panel arms recovery stays positive at every front; on the joint checkpoint it crosses zero and the curve turns. The two facts co-occur across five checkpoints and it would be easy to write that the turn belongs to the negative-recovery regime. **Nothing measured here supports that**: the joint checkpoint differs from these arms in backbone, in expansion factor (2x against 12x), in dictionary sparsity, in training budget and in being a joint checkpoint at all, and this run varies none of them. The fitted-versus-scored convention candidate remains neither removed nor established, EXP-R2-182's standing conclusion is untouched, and the reconstruction-NMSE follow-up is still not run.

**Bounds, as declared, plus one that came out of the run.** Seven fronts on 36 blocks (five on 12) samples the depth curve rather than resolving it, and a front is always a prefix. One cohort at one draw per arm, inherited from each headline cell; **no skip-offset condition was run**, so these curves' cohort-draw sensitivity is untested. One dictionary per arm, against the joint sweep's two seeds per mode, so nothing here prices dictionary-seed variability; the bootstrap prices cohort-sampling noise alone. The bound that sharpened in the running is the one the pre-declaration flagged: `gpt2-large`'s whole curve lives inside 0.068 of recovery, and it is precisely *because* its resampling resolves steps four orders of magnitude smaller than that range that its null is informative — on an arm with a coarser instrument the same table would have said much less. And a null bounds this cohort and these dictionaries; it does not bound what a differently trained dictionary on the same arm would do.

**Operational record.** One freeze for all four cells from a git worktree pinned at the commit under test (`81b98d9`, code hash `75d9339d9986` — the same code state EXP-R2-187 ran), with `LOCAL_OUTPUT_ROOT` left on the real checkout so the dispatch ledger and the pulled results landed where an operator reads them. **The pin was necessary and provably so**: two H200 drivers were being edited by another agent while this campaign was being frozen, and the live tree's code hash read `fb0b8e19` against the pinned `75d9339d` at the moment of the freeze — the same hazard EXP-R2-183 recorded, met before it could refuse a dispatch rather than after. All four cards were verified idle in-pod before dispatch (0 MiB each) and occupied at 8.8–28.7 GiB after; each cell was launched as its own detached process rather than inside a compound list, so no cell was lost to the export-swallowing hazard. No dispatch was aborted, no artefact was superseded, and the cluster-health probe returned `Health=ok` with the pod's GPFS read-write. Wall clock from first dispatch to last admission was 79 minutes, the causal sweep over 756 components dominating it on the three 36-block arms. `arm_can_run` was consulted and does not declare this stage, which is recorded in the pre-declaration rather than worked around.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-189: scoping study. Is a corpus-disjoint referent reachable? CPU-only, no GPU, no download, nothing built

**Why.** D3.b and D3.d both closed today at their own pre-registered gates, and both concluded that the binding constraint is the evaluation setup rather than the instrument: clearing the Objective-3 bar needs a referent where retrieval is excluded *by construction* rather than estimated. D3.d's author recorded that obtaining one appears to require leaving the matched panel and that no design was known that gets both. This entry measures whether that is true. It runs no model, writes no source change, downloads nothing, and admits no artefact to `results/`; every number below is either a re-read of an artefact already on disk or a CPU measurement over staged reference data.

**1. ProteinGym cannot supply a corpus-disjoint referent, and no threshold sweep can manufacture one.** Re-read of `results/transfer/retrieval_bound/{search,profiles,wildtypes}.json` (EXP-R2-143's own artefacts, so this is F10's cohort and not a new one): over all **187 distinct wild types** the minimum maximum-identity-over-query against the staged UniRef50 is **55.5%**; six wild types fall below 70% identity, twelve below 80%, and **none below 55%**. `no_support` is **0 of 187** — every wild type has profile support. The least-homologous entries are not exotic: the floor is held by `P84126_THETH_Chan_2017` at 55.5%, and even the ancestrally-reconstructed `ANCSZ_Hobbs_2022`, which was never an observed sequence, reads **73.2%** identity at Neff 73. Low *support* is available where low *identity* is not — 25 wild types (24 clusters) sit below Neff 10 — but that is the wrong axis: a thin profile at 99% identity is minimum retrieval-channel strength at maximum memorisation exposure, which is why F10 already measured no gradient in Neff.

**2. A temporal split of this benchmark against ProtGPT2's cut yields one unit.** Swiss-Prot creation and sequence-revision dates were extracted offline from the staged `data/swissprot/uniprot_sprot.xml.gz` (`<entry created=…>` and `<sequence modified=… version=…>`), 574,627 entries in **70 s** of one pass. 193 of the 217 assays join to a Swiss-Prot entry name. Against ProtGPT2's UniRef50 **2021_04** release (27-Oct-2021), **exactly 1** joined wild type was created after the cut and **4** carry a post-cut sequence revision, against a bootstrap floor of 8 units. Two independent reasons make this worse than it looks: a Swiss-Prot creation date is a *curation* date, so it is an upper bound on novelty rather than evidence of absence from the corpus; and record-level temporal novelty is not homology novelty in any case (L30's shape).

**3. The absence certificate is attainable with what is already staged, and it is verified in the negative direction for the first time.** F10's `anchor` gate tests only the positive direction (a verbatim corpus member must read as a near-duplicate). The negative direction — that "no hits" is a measurable state and not a misconfigured search — had never been checked. Twenty-four wild types were drawn under a seeded permutation (`20260812`, never a prefix) in the 50–600 residue band and searched against the full `uniref50_full.dmnd` (60,315,044 clusters, 17.28 G letters) alongside a composition-preserving mono-shuffle and a reversal of each: `diamond blastp --masking 0 --very-sensitive --max-target-seqs 50`, 96 threads, **6 m 15 s wall / 148 CPU-min for 72 queries**. **All 24 originals aligned** (minimum identity-over-query 58.1%, median 100.0%); **0 of 24 mono-shuffles and 0 of 24 reversals produced a single HSP.** So absence is certifiable at this setting, at about **5 CPU-minutes per query** — roughly 2.6 h wall on 96 threads for a 500-sequence referent. What it does *not* establish is that a de novo design would read as absent: a shuffle destroys all local order and a design does not, so this bounds the instrument's false-positive floor rather than its behaviour on designed sequences.

**4. Certifying disjointness does not need the 2021_04 archive, and certifying presence does.** UniRef50 2021_04 holds **49,874,565** clusters against the staged snapshot's **60,315,044**, so the corpus ProtGPT2 saw is 17% smaller than the one searched. Absence from the *newer* snapshot therefore implies absence from the older one, and the bias runs the safe way — which is the same direction F10 already declares for its identity stratification. Presence is the direction that needs the archive, and the archive is a single **169.2 GB** combined tarball (`uniref2021_04.tar.gz`, uniref50+90+100 together; no separate uniref50 file exists in that layout) against 559 GB free on `/Data`. Reachability was probed by HEAD only; nothing was transferred except one 1 KB release note.

**5. The deeper-alignment route to D3.d's second-order channel is refuted on the artefact, at zero further cost.** D3.d's row records "whether a deeper alignment — an HHblits or JackHMMER profile rather than a hit list — would restore the channel is a real question". Re-reading `results/transfer/epistasis/cohort.json` answers it in the negative for this benchmark. The 22 units with a measured coupling split cleanly and the split is anti-correlated with what a deeper profile would buy: the six pair-rich units (218–1047 pairs) carry **Neff 29–210** and read coupling −0.012 to +0.065 against tight nulls of 0.029–0.102, while the sixteen deep-alignment units (Neff 237–2775) carry **2 to 16 pairs** and nulls of 0.27 to 1.00. Spearman of the null 99th percentile against pair count is **−0.640 (p = 0.0013)**; against Neff it is **+0.216 (p = 0.34)**. Depth is not what makes these nulls unresolvable — pair count is. A deeper profile can only act on the six pair-rich units, which is **below the 8-unit bootstrap floor**, so even complete success there cannot produce a pooled A3. And the pool is exhausted rather than under-drawn: of 217 assays, **166 were refused**, the great majority because no double mutant carries both of its singles. ProteinGym cannot supply more pair-rich units. Recommendation recorded here so it is not re-proposed: HHblits/JackHMMER/MMseqs2 buy nothing on this cohort.

**6. The stability sub-benchmark is where a design-based referent would land, and the arms are measurable there.** Re-read of the same F10 artefacts, restricted to the **64 Tsuboyama assays** (64 distinct 50%-identity clusters, one each): MODEL reads **+0.367** for ProtGPT2 and **+0.365** for ProGen2-medium against BLOSUM62's **+0.173**. So the attainability precondition for any stability-grounded design — that the arms predict stability on natural mini-domains at all — is met on 64 units without spending anything. *Recorded as a feasibility read and explicitly not as a finding*: on that subset MODEL − LOOKUP is **−0.0446 [−0.0811, −0.0084]** (ProtGPT2), **−0.0471 [−0.0900, −0.0083]** (ProGen2-medium) and **−0.1780 [−0.2412, −0.1193]** (ProGen3-112M), each interval-excluding zero, while every interval on the 111–113-cluster remainder covers it. This split was **not pre-registered**, it is post-hoc, and it is confounded at least three ways — the Tsuboyama wild types are median **57** residues [37, 72] against the remainder's **403** [60, 3423], they are one assay technology, and **0 of 64** are verbatim in the corpus against **73 of 123**. Nothing may be read from it about assay type; what it is used for here is the design fact that a stability referent starts from the sub-benchmark where the corpus profile is at its strongest.

**7. A fragment-level retrieval baseline is cheap and will be required.** A homologue-free referent does not mean an information-free one: DIAMOND finding no alignment says nothing about corpus *k*-mer statistics, which is what a decoder can use. A background *k*-mer model over the whole staged UniRef50 was timed at **21.6 s per GB** (955 M residues), extrapolating to about **9 minutes** for the full 24.6 GB; all 160,000 4-mers are observed within the first gigabyte. So the baseline that a disjoint-referent design needs in place of LOOKUP is a few CPU-minutes, and its absence would be the first thing to attack a positive result.

**What this scoping establishes, stated as the conclusion it is.** A corpus-disjoint referent is **not reachable from anything on this host**, for natural proteins it is **not reachable in principle** — UniRef50 2021_04 is 49.9 M clusters of natural sequence space and the most remote wild type in a 187-protein benchmark is still 55.5% identical to one of them — and the only class that is disjoint by construction is non-natural sequence, which this host does not hold. What is *not* true is the second half of D3.d's worry: applying such a referent would **not** break the matched comparison, because an evaluation cohort is not an arm, every protein arm can be scored on it, the certificate is verifiable for ProtGPT2 alone exactly as F10's corpus identification already is, and the contrast that would carry the claim is *within* one arm — the same instrument on referents where retrieval is available against referents where it is excluded. The blocker is data availability, not panel structure, and it needs an explicit download decision rather than another design.

**Bounds.** Nothing here was pre-registered; this is scoping, and every number is a re-read or a CPU measurement rather than a test of a stated hypothesis. Section 6's subset split is post-hoc and confounded and is not a claim. The disjointness probe used shuffles and reversals, which are a stronger negative than a designed protein would be. The Swiss-Prot join is by entry name over 193 of 217 assays and the 24 unmatched ones are unassessed. Reachability was probed by HEAD request only; no dataset was downloaded and no source file, `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` or `summary.md` was modified.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-189 follow-on: the two zero-cost controls are built, and the de novo referent is located, licensed and verified without transferring it

**Scope.** Authorised after the scoping entry above: build the two controls that entry priced, and probe — probe only — what de novo design data is actually reachable. Nothing was transferred beyond manifests and one parquet footer; no dataset was downloaded; no model was run; no source file, `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` or `summary.md` was modified.

**Control 1 — the corpus k-mer background is built.** A homologue-free referent is not an information-free one: DIAMOND finding no alignment says nothing about the corpus fragment statistics a decoder can use, so the baseline that replaces LOOKUP when LOOKUP is empty has to be fragment-level. One vectorised pass over the staged `uniref50.fasta` counted every 3-mer and 4-mer: **17,277,105,157 residues over 60,315,044 records in 1,103.7 s (18.4 min)**, all 8,000 3-mers and all 160,000 4-mers observed, 16.64 G and 16.32 G k-mer instances respectively. Header bytes, newlines and non-canonical residues code to an invalid symbol and any window containing one is dropped, so **no k-mer crosses a record boundary**. Independent check on the residue count: DIAMOND's `makedb` recorded **17,282,055,793** indexed letters for the same file, and the 0.03% difference is exactly the non-canonical residues this count excludes — so the two passes agree. Held outside the working tree with a checksummed manifest at `/Data/lzp/agent_scratch/kmerbg/`; it is a derived artefact of a staged corpus and is offered for staging rather than staged, since wiring it in is a source change this task is not authorised to make. The first estimate in the entry above said about 9 minutes; the correct figure is 18.4, because that estimate was measured on a chunk-level pass that ignored record boundaries and the boundary-correct pass costs the validity mask.

**Control 2 — the negative-direction certificate gate, restated with its bound.** Recorded in the entry above and repeated here because it must travel with any use of the certificate: at `--masking 0 --very-sensitive` against the full 60.3 M-cluster database, **24 of 24 originals aligned** (minimum identity-over-query 58.1%, median 100.0%) and **0 of 24 composition-preserving mono-shuffles and 0 of 24 reversals produced a single HSP**. This is the first evidence in this programme that absence is a *measurable* state rather than a misconfigured search — F10's `anchor` gate only ever tested the positive direction. **Its bound is load-bearing and is not a caveat**: a shuffle destroys all local order and a designed protein does not, so this fixes the instrument's false-positive floor and says nothing about how a design will read. What fraction of designs return zero hits is an empirical question and is itself a measurement, not a precondition.

**The probe — what is reachable.** The Institute for Protein Design file server is a dead route: every path under `/pub/` returns a 22 KB HTML page reading `403 Forbidden: File is not accessible`, including the directory itself, so path guessing cannot work there. Zenodo, huggingface.co and github.com do not connect from this host. The route that does work is the **HF mirror already sanctioned for hub access**, and it carries the dataset this design needs: **`RosettaCommons/MegaScale`** — the Rosetta Commons upload of Tsuboyama et al. 2023, *Mega-scale experimental analysis of protein folding stability in biology and design*, Nature 620:434–444, citing the authors' own `Rocklin-Lab/cdna-display-proteolysis-pipeline`. **Licence CC-BY-4.0, public, not gated**, last modified 2024-11-13; whole repository 1,728 MB across 38 files.

**The content was verified without transferring the data, by reading the parquet footer over HTTP range requests.** The `dataset2` config is two shards totalling 291.5 MB; shard 0 is 148,383,792 bytes with a 1,808,378-byte footer, and that footer alone — a header read — carries the schema and the per-row-group statistics of all 389 row groups. Schema confirmed: `aa_seq`, `mut_type`, `WT_name`, `WT_cluster`, `deltaG` (with 95% CIs), `ddG_ML`, `Stabilizing_mut`, `pair_name`, 388,149 rows in shard 0. **The min/max statistics prove designs are present.** Of 320 distinct `WT_name` boundary values, **57 are topology-prefixed de novo designs** — `EEHEE_rd3_*`, `EEHEE_rd4_*`, `EHEE_*`, `HEEH_*`, `HHH_*` — plus a second family of **55** run-keyed designs (`EA|run*`, `GG|run*`, `XX|run*`), against **208** PDB-id-style natural domains (`1A0N.pdb`, `1A32.pdb`, `1AOY.pdb`, …). Counting a series as topology × design round or run-family × run, that is **at least seven independent design series and comfortably more than eight**, and it is a *lower bound*, since 389 row-group boundaries sample the name space rather than enumerate it.

**Why this dataset removes the confound that made yesterday's subset split unreadable.** The natural-domain control and the designs are in **one file, from one assay technology, at matched length** — the designs are Rocklin-lineage miniproteins and the natural domains are the same 37–72-residue set ProteinGym's 64 Tsuboyama assays are drawn from. The design-versus-natural contrast is therefore length-matched, technology-matched and within-cohort, which is precisely what the post-hoc Tsuboyama-versus-rest split in the entry above was **not**, and it is the reason nothing was read from that split.

**Transfer cost, priced exactly from the footer.** `dataset2` in full is **291.5 MB**. A column-projected read of the six columns the estimand needs is **15.9 MB for shard 0**, about **31 MB for both**; the identifier columns alone — `WT_name`, `WT_cluster`, `mut_type` — are **2.58 MB** for shard 0, and `WT_name` by itself is **0.04 MB**, so an exact enumeration of the design series costs about a tenth of a megabyte. Transfer tooling is present (`hf`, `huggingface_hub` 0.36.0, `pyarrow` 22.0.0, `fsspec` + `aiohttp`, so column projection over range requests works).

**Stopped here, as instructed.** The preconditions the transfer authorisation names — MB-scale, publicly licensed, at least eight independent design series with measured stability — are all met on the evidence above, but the decision is not this task's to take and nothing has been transferred.

**Bounds.** The design count is a lower bound read from row-group boundaries, not an enumeration; only shard 0's footer was read. Whether the designs are absent from UniRef50 is *not* established here — several of these topologies come from published campaigns whose sequences may have entered UniParc, and the certificate is what will measure it. The k-mer background is a count, not a model: turning it into a baseline needs a declared scoring rule, which is a design decision and not a measurement.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-190: the de novo referent is staged and certified corpus-disjoint. 132 of 148 designs return zero hits against 60.3 M UniRef50 clusters

**Scope.** Authorised after EXP-R2-189's follow-on: enumerate the design series exactly, stage the dataset only if the count clears the pre-declared floor of eight, run the disjointness certificate on the designs, and wire the k-mer background into the package. No model was run and no GPU was touched. The scoring experiment the referent exists for was deliberately **not** run — the hit fraction had to come first, because a high one would have collapsed the referent and made any likelihood number unreadable. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for this work, as it did for EXP-R2-188; nothing here is dispatched per arm.

**1. The series count is 41 against a floor of 8, and the classification validates itself.** `WT_name` was read out of both `dataset2` shards by column projection over HTTP range requests — 0.04 MB of a 291.5 MB config — *before* anything was transferred, which is the order the gate requires. 776,298 rows carry **479 distinct wild types**. Counting a series as topology × design round gives **12** (`EEHEE` rd3/rd4, `EHEE` rd1–rd4, `HEEH` rd3/rd4, `HEEH_KT` rd6, `HHH` rd1/rd2/rd4); run-family × run gives **18** (`EA` 5, `GG` 6, `XX` 7); and a third family the footer sample had not revealed — trRosetta hallucination designs, `r{N}_*_TrROS_Hall` — gives **11** more, one per hallucination round. **41 independent design series over 148 designs.** The classification is not asserted: it partitions the 479 names into **148 designs and 331 naturals**, and the dataset's own README independently states "331 natural and 148 de novo designed protein domains, 40–72 amino acids in length". Two constructions agreeing exactly is what licenses the split being used as a label. EXP-R2-189's "at least seven and comfortably more than eight" was a lower bound from row-group boundaries; the exact count is five times the floor.

**2. Staged whole, and it reproduces upstream byte for byte.** `RosettaCommons/MegaScale`, config `dataset2`, pinned at upstream commit `f27fb1f61a7e835a1c05aa7fd3c2ea9fbbdf8508`, retrieved through the sanctioned mirror to `data/megascale_tsuboyama2023/` — two parquet shards of 148,383,792 and 143,104,796 bytes, 291,488,588 total. Both SHA-256 match the upstream LFS digests exactly (`407c0d31…`, `04ada6ee…`), which is why the config was fetched whole rather than column-projected: a projection produces a derived file matching no published digest. CC-BY-4.0, public, ungated; Tsuboyama et al., *Nature* 620:434–444 (2023). `data/` is gitignored, so `manifest.json`, `SHA256SUMS` and `README.md` in that directory are the durable on-disk record and this entry is the durable record in Git.

**3. The certificate. 16 of 148 designs hit, 132 are certified zero-hit, and the within-cohort natural control hits at 328 of 330.** All 478 wild types carrying an explicit `mut_type == "wt"` row were searched against the full `uniref50_full.dmnd` (60,315,044 clusters, 17.28 G letters) with `diamond blastp --very-sensitive --masking 0`, 96 threads, 7 m 35 s wall, 26,969 HSPs. **This is a census, not a sample** — every design and every natural domain in the file — so the seeded-permutation rule has nothing to bind on and no skip-offset sensitivity exists to report. All 148 design sequences are distinct from one another and none is byte-identical to any natural domain.

| e-value | design hit fraction | natural hit fraction |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-3 (gate) | **16/148 = 10.81%** | **328/330 = 99.39%** |
| 1e-2 | 21/148 = 14.19% | 328/330 = 99.39% |
| 1e-1 | 26/148 = 17.57% | 328/330 = 99.39% |
| 1 | 42/148 = 28.38% | 328/330 = 99.39% |
| 10 | 87/148 = 58.78% | 329/330 = 99.70% |

The gate is 1e-3 because that is the setting F10's `homology_control` runs and the setting the negative-direction gate was validated at. The search itself ran at e-value 10 and every row is a post-filter of that one search, so the sweep costs nothing and **the ordering is invariant across four orders of magnitude**: at every cut the design fraction sits at least 40 points below the natural fraction.

**The identity distributions separate completely, which matters more than the count.** Among designs that hit, identity-over-query runs min 37.2, median 48.8, p90 54.7. Among naturals that hit: min 58.7, median 98.3, p75 100.0. **Excluding the single verbatim design, the design distribution's maximum is 55.8% — below the natural distribution's minimum of 58.7%.** The same instrument, one file, one setting, and the two populations do not overlap. Sweeping the identity threshold instead of the e-value says the same thing more sharply: at **≥60% identity exactly one design has any relative at all, against 327 of 330 naturals**; at ≥90% it is 1 against 250. The ordering is invariant at every threshold from 0 to 100.

**37 of the 41 series are entirely zero-hit** — all 11 hallucination series, all 18 run-keyed series, and 8 of the 12 topology series. The hits are confined to `EEHEE` rd3 (7/16), `EEHEE` rd4 (6/13), `HHH` rd4 (2/7) and `HEEH_KT` rd6 (1/9).

**Where the hits come from is identifiable, and it is the mechanism the authorisation anticipated.** All 16 design hits at the gate are to UniParc (`UniRef50_UPI…`) clusters and **not one design hits a named UniProt entry**; the natural control's HSPs are 17.5% UniParc by comparison. Thirteen of the sixteen hit *the same cluster*, `UniRef50_UPI000B803003`, and one of those is `EEHEE_rd3_1049.pdb` at **100.0% identity over all 43 residues** — a design that is verbatim in UniRef50. So the design-side signal is essentially one published design that propagated into UniParc, plus twelve of its own campaign siblings reading against it at 37–56%. That is design-campaign self-homology surfacing through a single deposited member, not natural homology, and it is why the referent survives: **excluding the 16 is a named, auditable exclusion touching 4 series, not a haircut across all 41.**

**The length confound was the one thing that could have made this artefactual, and it runs the other way.** Designs are shorter than naturals (median 43 against 59) and a shorter query is harder to align, so design absence could have been a power effect. In the 40–47 band, where 133 of the 148 designs live, the natural control still hits at **30/31 = 96.77%**. Detection is not failing at design length; the designs are absent. Artefacts under `results/transfer/megascale_disjointness/`.

**4. The k-mer background is wired into `src/transfer/kmer_background.py`, and moving it found a defect worth 3–4.7% of the count.** EXP-R2-189's pass treated the newline as an invalid symbol, which buys the record-boundary property for free — and also silently discards every window spanning the corpus's 60-column FASTA line wrapping. Recounted at record-local semantics: **17,154,643,378 3-mers against the previous 16,640,807,917, and 17,093,475,529 4-mers against 16,324,342,706 — 513,835,461 and 769,132,823 windows recovered, 3.09% and 4.71%.** Line wrapping is a property of the file format, not of the protein, so those are real k-mers of real proteins. Residues (17,277,105,157) and records (60,315,044) reproduce the earlier pass exactly, which is the cross-check that the change is confined to where it was meant to be; DIAMOND's independent `makedb` letter count still agrees to 0.03%, the difference being exactly the non-canonical residues this count excludes. 906 s for the corrected pass.

**How much the correction matters depends on what reads it, and both readings are recorded.** As a *distribution* the old count was nearly right — total-variation distance 0.00028 at k = 3 and 0.00060 at k = 4, because line breaks fall at fixed residue offsets and are uncorrelated with sequence content. Per k-mer it is not: one 4-mer's frequency moves by **42%**. A baseline that scores fragments individually would have read that error, so this is not a cosmetic repair. The superseded counts are retained under `data/kmer_background/uniref50_line_local_superseded_20260812/` rather than deleted.

The tests are what the module is for, and they target the three failures that produce plausible-looking numbers: a fragment that exists only across a record join must be absent, a wrapped record must count identically to the unwrapped one, and the same file counted at nine chunk sizes from one byte upward must give identical counts — a carry bug at a chunk boundary is wrong by parts per million and looks entirely fine. The count remains a count and not a model; the scoring rule is still a design decision for the stage that makes it. CPU suite green at **1186 passed, 8 skipped**, the 18 added tests being the whole difference from the 1168 baseline.

**What this settles.** EXP-R2-189 established that a corpus-disjoint referent is unreachable for natural protein in principle, and that the only class disjoint by construction is non-natural sequence. That class is now staged, and **the construction holds empirically**: 132 designs across 37 fully clean series carry no detectable UniRef50 homologue at a setting where 99.4% of length-matched natural domains from the same file, the same assay and the same experiment do. The referent survives. Objective 3's retrieval question moves from bounded to decidable, and what decides it is a likelihood measurement that has not been run.

**Bounds, one of them load-bearing.** The negative-direction gate (24/24 originals aligned, 0/24 mono-shuffles, 0/24 reversals) fixes the instrument's false-positive floor on sequences with no local order. This run is the first evidence of how a *design* reads, and it reads as absent — but the two remain separate facts and the shuffle bound does not transfer to designs. Absence is certified against the staged UniRef50 snapshot; ProtGPT2's UniRef50 2021_04 is 17% smaller, so absence from the newer implies absence from the older and the bias runs safe — but ProGen2 saw UniRef90 and BFD, which are not searched here, so the certificate is stated for ProtGPT2's corpus exactly as F10's corpus identification already is. Absence of an *alignment* is not absence of *information*: a zero-hit design is still built from corpus fragments, which is what the k-mer background exists to price and what nothing here has priced. The 148/331 label comes from `WT_name` shape corroborated by the dataset README, not from structure. `1A0N.pdb` carries no `wt` row in `dataset2` and was not searched; it is a natural domain and no design is affected. Nothing here was pre-registered, and `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` were not modified.
