## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-191 pre-declared: R2.4's independent dictionaries, the Crosscoder gate fixed as a number, and whether a dictionary that cannot replace a model may still be diffed

Written before any of the four dictionaries exists. Every number below is a re-read of an artefact already on disk; no GPU produced any of it, and three of the measurements are follow-ups this series declared and never ran.

### 1. Does R2.3's negative recovery block a feature comparison? NO — but the reason it does not is narrower than the reason usually offered, and something else does bound the comparison

**The worry.** EXP-R2-182 found NLL recovery negative in all four R2.3 cells: splicing the trained dictionary into every block damages `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` more than deleting every block's contribution and substituting its per-layer mean. Every cell's behavioural verdict is FAIL. If a dictionary cannot stand in for the computation, can a comparison of its features be a comparison of the model's features?

**Why the negative headline is the wrong certificate for this operation.** Sequential replacement composes thirty-two approximations: every block reads a residual stream the replacements above it have already perturbed. A same-input feature diff composes none — each layer's dictionary is applied to that layer's true input on the model's own clean forward pass, which is the teacher-forced convention the dictionaries were *fitted* under and the convention their reconstruction is *scored* under (`condition.reconstruction_measured_under` says so in every stage-15 artefact). The certificate whose operation matches the diff is the shallowest front, and it is positive and high: EXP-R2-186 measured recovery at a one-block front of **0.8875 / 0.8699 / 0.9563 / 0.9593** in the four cells, and EXP-R2-188 reproduced the same statement on four panel arms — 0.9318 to 0.9998 — so "a single replaced block recovers nearly all of the mean-ablation gap, and the damage the headline reports is a property of composition" holds on six cells across three checkpoint families and both modalities.

**Its gap, stated rather than left implicit.** A front is always a prefix, so `k = 1` certifies the *first* block and no other. Nothing on disk certifies a single-block replacement at depth, and the fall from 0.956 to 0.083 between `k = 1` and `k = 2` in text s06 shows the composition penalty arrives immediately. So the argument above licenses "the negative headline is not evidence that each block's dictionary is a bad description of that block", and it does not license "each block's dictionary is a good description of that block".

**Three measurements taken here, at zero cost, that bear on what does.**

**(a) The train/eval population gap is excluded.** This is EXP-R2-186's own declared and un-run follow-up — reconstruction NMSE on the scoring cohort against the held-out figure — and both numbers were already in the artefacts. Summed over 32 layers, cohort against held-out: protein **4.944 / 5.470 = 0.904** (seed 20260806) and **4.980 / 5.476 = 0.909** (seed 20260811); text **6.557 / 6.518 = 1.006** and **6.553 / 6.437 = 1.018**. Both are measured teacher-forced on clean inputs, so this is like against like. The scoring cohort is not a harder population than the held-out draw — on the protein side it is 10% *easier*. Of the three candidates EXP-R2-182 named and EXP-R2-186 left unseparated, this one is now removed.

**(b) Undertraining is excluded for the protein mode and stays weakly live for text.** From the training histories. Protein held-out NMSE sum falls 6.335 → 5.539 by step 12,000 (10.8 M tokens) and then wanders between **5.396 and 5.788** for the remaining 25,000 steps and 23 M tokens, ending at 5.470 — it is flat, not still falling. Dead latents saturate on the same schedule, reaching 201,719 of 262,144 by step 12,000 against 209,256 at the end. Text falls monotonically to 6.518 and is still moving, by −0.059 over its last 4,000 steps. So a larger token budget cannot be expected to buy the protein dictionary anything at this width, and can be expected to buy the text one very little.

**(c) The dictionary's unexplained variance sits where the diffing signal is.** Per layer, the R2.3 held-out reconstruction NMSE and EXP-R2-175's cross-checkpoint true-pairing ridge residual are rank-correlated over the interior layers 2–29 at **Spearman +0.940 to +0.952 on protein and +0.760 to +0.776 on text**, across both dictionary seeds and both diffing skip offsets. In level terms the dictionary's own error is a substantial fraction of the signal it would be used to describe: the ratio (dictionary NMSE) / (cross-checkpoint ridge residual) has median **0.42–0.44 on protein, maximum 0.53–0.55**, and median **0.26 on text, maximum 1.13–1.20**. *This correlation is not an attribution.* Both quantities plausibly rise with how much structured, high-rank computation a layer does, and nothing here separates a shared cause from a causal one. What it establishes is only the thing the design needs: the basis is weakest exactly where the difference is largest, and the size of the resulting bias is not bounded by anything measured.

**The answer, and it is the answer to a narrower question than "is the dictionary good".** A same-input diff asks which features are shared, introduced or removed between two sets of weights. It does not require the dictionary to substitute for the computation, and the negative full-stack recovery — a composition property — is therefore not a reason to refuse it. It does require the dictionary to *describe* each layer's activations well enough that a difference between two dictionaries is a difference between the models rather than between two fits, and on that the evidence is mixed rather than reassuring: the description leaves 17.1% (protein) and 20.4% (text) of per-layer variance unexplained on average, up to 33.6% and 43.1% at the worst layer, concentrated where the signal is, and the protein dictionary's live latents are **1,653 per layer against `d_model` 4,096** — an *under-complete* basis, not the 2x over-complete one it was configured as. The text dictionary's 4,465 live latents per layer clears `d_model` by 9%. **So the comparison is not blocked and it is also not free: it will be read against a declared adequacy gate (§3 below), and where that gate fails the result is a statement about two dictionaries and not about two models.**

### 2. §4c's Crosscoder gate has already fired, and it fires on reading two

`RESEARCH_PLAN.md` §4c is pre-registered and names two deciding measurements, both of which now exist. Taking its three readings in turn:

- **Reading 1 — "both modes reach behavioural faithfulness after layerwise replacement, and simple alignment leaves the cross-stage difference unexplained."** Off. Recovery is negative in all four R2.3 cells and the behavioural verdict is FAIL in every one; the stage's own gate is 0.80.
- **Reading 3 — "linear or orthogonal alignment already accounts for the discrepancy on held-out positions."** Off. EXP-R2-175: mean ridge residual under true pairing 0.400 (protein) and 0.684 (text) against shuffled 1.002 and 1.001, and 0.73 / 0.90 at the layers where the difference is largest. Procrustes is worse (0.670 / 0.852). Nothing is accounted for.
- **Reading 2 — "the protein mode's dictionary remains unfaithful."** On, and a fortiori: both modes are, not only the protein one. Its pre-registered consequence is that **Crosscoder work is postponed and the dictionary's failure mode is diagnosed first.**

**So the Crosscoder gate is decided, and it is decided against training one.** That decision is not this run's to take or to revisit: it was fixed before the evidence existed, the evidence is in, and re-opening it on dictionaries trained after seeing the answer is the move this programme has retracted a dozen findings for.

**This changes what the four cells are for, and the change is recorded before they run.** They remain R2.4's declared independent-dictionary step. They are *not* an instrument for re-deciding the Crosscoder gate. What they add that nothing on disk has is a **base-side dictionary**: every dictionary this programme owns on this lineage is on `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`, so it cannot yet be said whether negative sequential recovery is a property of the adapted checkpoint or of this recipe on a 7B LLaMA backbone. EXP-R2-188 bounds it from one side — the phenomenon does not appear on any panel arm at 12x expansion — and the base checkpoint at the same 2x recipe is the control that separates backbone from adaptation. That is a diagnosis of the failure mode, which is the pre-registered prerequisite, and it is why this run is worth its cards.

### 3. The gate, fixed as a number before the dictionaries exist

Two criteria. The first classifies the alignment result already on disk and is therefore **not** a pre-registration of its own outcome — the numbers it reads existed before the rule did, and this entry says so rather than presenting the rule as blind. The second is a genuine pre-registration: it reads quantities none of which exists yet.

**Criterion A — when is simple alignment insufficient.** The unit was declared inside `25_model_diffing_baselines.py` before it ran: its `verdict.readings` name the adjacent-layer residual at the same layer as "what one layer of the reference model's own ordinary computation costs in the same units", and reading `no_linear_map_explains_it_and_the_gap_exceeds_one_layer` is stated in exactly that unit. What was never fixed is what "exceeds" means. Fix it: per layer, let

> **R(l) = cross-checkpoint true-pairing ridge residual at layer l ÷ adjacent-layer true-pairing ridge residual at layer l**

and read the **median of R over the interior layers 2–29**, with the interquartile range and the fraction of layers above 1 reported beside it. Layers 0, 1, 30 and 31 are excluded in advance and for a stated reason: the top layer has no adjacent successor, and the bottom and top layers carry the degenerate denominators EXP-R2-175 already refused to aggregate over — the text side's layer-1 adjacent identity residual alone reads 6,347.7. **Simple alignment is INSUFFICIENT in a mode when median R > 1**: the residual the best linear map leaves costs more than one layer of the model's own ordinary computation.

Applied, on the artefacts on disk, at both skip offsets:

| mode | median R | IQR | fraction of layers with R > 1 | reading |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| protein, skip 0 | **3.116** | [1.999, 4.264] | 0.821 | INSUFFICIENT |
| protein, skip 40,960 | **3.209** | [2.147, 4.305] | 0.821 | INSUFFICIENT |
| text, skip 0 | **0.956** | [0.904, 1.026] | 0.321 | **UNRESOLVED** |
| text, skip 16,384 | **0.954** | [0.900, 1.024] | 0.321 | **UNRESOLVED** |

**The text mode is recorded as unresolved rather than as sufficient, and that is the honest reading.** Its median sits 4.6% below the cut with an interquartile range straddling it; calling that "alignment accounts for the difference" would be reading a 4.6% margin as a verdict. The protein mode is insufficient robustly — its whole interquartile range is above 1, so even its best quartile of layers costs twice a layer of ordinary computation. **Threshold sweep, as the standing rule asks:** the two modes are separated by every cut in (0.956, 3.116), a factor of 3.26, and the declared cut of 1 is the only one in that range with a stated meaning. Below 0.956 both modes read insufficient; above 3.209 both read sufficient. The ordering — protein above text by 3.3x — is invariant to the cut everywhere. It is also invariant to the corpus draw (third decimal across skip offsets) and does not involve the dictionaries at all.

**Criterion B — when may a feature diff be read as a statement about the models.** Pre-registered; none of these numbers exists yet. Both conditions must hold, in **all four** cells, at the layers a difference is reported on:

- **B1, description adequacy.** D(l) = (that cell's held-out reconstruction NMSE at layer l) ÷ (that mode's cross-checkpoint true-pairing ridge residual at layer l) must satisfy **median D < 0.5 over layers 2–29 and max D < 1**. Above 1 the dictionary's own unexplained variance is as large as the difference it would describe. Orientation from the R2.3 stage-1 dictionaries: protein median 0.42–0.44 / max 0.53–0.55 would pass; text median 0.26 / max **1.13–1.20** would **fail on max**, at layer 2, where the cross-checkpoint residual is small (0.290) and the dictionary's own error is not (0.331).
- **B2, basis adequacy.** Mean live latents per layer must exceed `d_model` = 4,096. A dictionary whose live latents cannot span the space is not decomposing it into more features than dimensions, which is the premise a sparse over-complete dictionary is read under. Orientation: R2.3 text 4,465 would pass by 9%; R2.3 protein **1,653** would fail by 2.5x.

**And the refusal condition on B itself, declared now because it is the shape this programme has breached four times.** B2's cut is cleared by the R2.3 text control by only 9%. If the text cells of *this* run fail B2, the gate is one the control cannot pass, which makes it a specification defect and not a protein result: B2 is then **void as a gate** and its numbers are reported as a descriptive asymmetry only. The same applies to B1 and its max condition. Attainability before application — and the honest position is that B2's attainability is currently demonstrated with a 9% margin, which is thin.

**What each outcome licenses.**

- **A insufficient in a mode and B passing in all four cells.** The feature diff for that mode is reported as a measurement of a difference between two sets of weights, still representational until an intervention shows a behavioural change (§8 of the audit). The Crosscoder stays postponed regardless, because §4c reading 2 is about behavioural faithfulness and no dictionary trained here changes that.
- **A insufficient and B failing.** The diff is reported as a comparison of two fitted bases and not of two models, and the failing quantity is named. This is the expected outcome on the protein side on the R2.3 orientation figures, and saying so in advance is the point of writing it here.
- **A unresolved (the text mode as it stands).** No alignment verdict is issued for that mode in either direction, and it is not converted into a null.

### 4. The four cells, and their matched certificate

`17_train_transcoder.py`, per-layer transcoders, one dictionary per cell, four cards.

| cell | checkpoint | mode | `--steps` |
|---|---|---|---:|
| A | `Llama-2-7b-hf` | text | 26,000 |
| B | `Llama-2-7b-hf` | protein | 56,000 |
| C | `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` | text | 26,000 |
| D | `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` | protein | 56,000 |

Everything else identical across all four: `--architecture plt --rendering prollama --max-tokens 1024 --d-hidden 8192 --k 32 --auxk 192 --train-tokens 34000000 --batch-size 4 --eval-sequences 256 --eval-every 2000 --learning-rate 2e-4 --weight-decay 1e-5 --grad-clip 1.0 --seed 20260812 --corpus-seed 20260812`.

**`--max-tokens` is 1024 in both modes, which R2.3's pair was not.** That pilot ran 512 text against 1024 protein and certified `MATCHED` while `max_tokens_agree` read false — a real unmatched axis carried as a reported field, with the standing recommendation that future joint pairs run equal caps at 1024. Followed. The cost is that these text cells are not comparable with R2.3's text cells, which is accepted: the comparison being made is among these four.

**`--steps` differs by mode and must.** It is deliberately excluded from `MATCHED_TRAINING_FIELDS` because a text record and a protein record carry different numbers of scored positions, so equal steps are equal *schedules* over unequal data; `--train-tokens` is what is held equal. `--steps` bounds the run and sets the held-out offset. A consequence worth stating, because it is what makes this a same-input comparison: within a mode the held-out draw depends only on the corpus, the corpus seed, the step budget and the batch, all of which are matched across the two checkpoints, so cells A and C see the same held-out documents and cells B and D the same held-out proteins.

**The certificate, and one thing it cannot say.** Within each checkpoint the two modes are a pair `compare_matched_training` can certify `MATCHED`, because they share a backbone. **Across checkpoints it cannot, by construction and correctly**: `backbone_sha256` is one of the fifteen matched fields, put there so that two dictionaries from different stages of one lineage cannot be compared under the label of a comparison within one set of weights. For a diffing pair that difference is the contrast, so the honest certificate for the cross-checkpoint pairs A↔C and B↔D is `verdict MISMATCH` with `disagreements` exactly `["backbone_sha256"]`, `max_tokens_agree true`, and every one of the other fourteen fields agreeing. That is reported as such and **no comparator is loosened to make it read `MATCHED`** — a fourth verdict would weaken a guard that has already caught a real failure, and nothing here needs it, because each dictionary is scored against its own mode-partner within its own checkpoint.

**Cell B carries a scope limit that no result relaxes.** The base checkpoint's protein mode is behaviourally unmeasurable on the current estimand. It is a *pre-adaptation representational reference*: its reconstruction, its live-latent count and its features are measurable, its behavioural recovery is not, and no base-side protein claim may be made about behaviour or about knowledge.

**One repair travels with this run, and it is an Objective-2 result rather than housekeeping.** `17_train_transcoder.py` drew its held-out set by skipping past the whole training budget — disjoint as *records*, which L30 established is not a held-out set on a protein corpus. The same defect that blocked R2.4's protein cell reached this stage through a second door and was never checked here. The held-out draw is now oversampled 4x and screened against every training record under the same near-duplicate relation, threshold and calibration (`src/transfer/near_duplicates.py`), and the screen runs on **both** modes because attainability precedes application. Measured on the production draws on the local workstation, at this run's seed and offsets: **protein drops 63 of 1,024 candidates, maximum containment 1.000**; **text drops 0 of 1,024, maximum containment 0.4346**, below the 0.5 threshold. So the record-level draw was genuinely held out on the text corpus and was not on Swiss-Prot — the limitation localises to the evaluation interface on the protein corpus, as L30 does, and the text control demonstrates the gate is attainable rather than being assumed to. The screen costs 56 s (protein, 229,376 records) and 82 s (text, 106,496) of host CPU before the model is touched. R2.3's own held-out figures were drawn unscreened and are optimistic by an unmeasured amount on the protein side; they are not withdrawn, and every use of them in §1 above is a *within-artefact* comparison that the leak affects on both sides. Commit `04fdfa5`; CPU suite green at 1194 passed, 8 skipped.

### 5. Bounds, declared in advance

One draw per cell, one seed per cell — the seed is not replicated here, so nothing in this run prices dictionary-seed variability, and R2.3's two seeds are the only evidence that it is small (their held-out sums differ by 0.006 and 0.081). One expansion factor: 2x, chosen for comparability with the protein half of R2.3 and not because it is adequate — §1(c) and B2 say it may well not be, and a width sweep is the follow-up this run's B2 reading decides on, not one scheduled in advance of it. `d_hidden` 8,192 is what fits: 12x on this backbone needs 206 GB of optimiser state against 143.8 GB per card. The protein corpus is Swiss-Prot and the text corpus OpenWebText, which are two corpora and not one, so a mode difference is never only a mode difference. Cell B's behavioural side does not exist. And the whole comparison is one lineage and one adaptation step; nothing here speaks to stage 1 → stage 2, which `RESEARCH_PLAN.md` already orders behind this one on the evidence that the two adapted stages are indistinguishable on the estimand that qualified them.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-192 pre-registered: the corpus-disjoint referent measurement. Frozen before any score exists

**What has become possible, and why it is worth a pre-registration.** F10 bounds what a protein decoder knows about function *relative to a lookup of its own corpus*, and EXP-R2-189 established that it can never do better than bound it: over 187 ProteinGym wild types the least homologous is still 55.5% identical to a UniRef50 cluster, so retrieval could be estimated and subtracted but never excluded. EXP-R2-190 staged a referent where it is excluded by construction — **132 of 148 de novo designs return no DIAMOND hit** against the 60.3 M-cluster staged UniRef50 at F10's own gate, against a within-cohort natural control from one file, one assay technology and matched length that hits at **328 of 330**. This entry freezes the measurement that referent was staged for, before it is made. Nothing below is a result; every number is a property of the cohort, computable without a model and without a correlation.

**The estimand is F10's, unchanged.** Per wild type, the Spearman correlation between an arm's summed log-likelihood of a variant and that variant's measured folding stability. The phenotype is `ddG_ML`, which is the column ProteinGym itself publishes as `DMS_score` for its 64 Tsuboyama assays — verified here, not assumed: on `ARGR_ECOLI_Tsuboyama_2023_1AOY` the two agree to 8.9e-16 on all 1,287 shared variants. Higher is more stable. This is a **sequence-likelihood** estimand, so L31 does not bind it: a likelihood needs no alignment between the variant and the wild type, and the BPE selection effect that makes a position-level intervention undefined on part of a ProtGPT2 cohort has no purchase here.

**The frozen rule, per arm.** Let (a) be the certified zero-hit designs and (b) the natural-domain control from the same file. For each baseline, the arm *beats* it on a side when the unit-clustered 95% percentile interval on MODEL − BASELINE over that side lies wholly above zero.

- **`positive`** — the arm beats **every** free and fragment-level baseline on (a), **and** the identical conjunction holds on (b).
- **`negative`** — the conjunction fails on (a) while (b) passes. This is a clean negative: the instrument clears its own bar where retrieval is available, and the model does not clear it where retrieval is excluded.
- **`uninterpretable_instrument_bound`** — (b) fails. Nothing is then read from (a) at all, whatever it says, because the gate was never shown attainable. This is recorded as a bound on the instrument, not as a result about the model.

Attainability before application: the gate applied to the corpus-disjoint side is the same gate, computed the same way, on the side where retrieval is available. This rule is executable as `designed_referent.arm_verdict` and its truth table — including the case where (a) passes and (b) fails, which is the one that would otherwise be reported as a discovery — is asserted in `tests/test_designed_referent.py`.

**The baselines, all seven, declared now.** Free: `blosum62` and `profiles.free_baselines`' own family (`position_index`, `wt_hydropathy`, `hydropathy_change`, `background_composition`), imported rather than respelled. Fragment-level: `fragment_markov_k3` and `fragment_markov_k4`, conditional sequence models `log P(x_t | x_{t-k+1..t-1})` built from the **corrected** record-local corpus k-mer background, with the (k−1)-mer denominator taken as the k-mer table's own row sum so the conditional is normalised over exactly the windows counted. All 8,000 3-mers and all 160,000 4-mers are observed, so no smoothing rule is needed and none is invented. The fragment baselines are what replaces F10's profile LOOKUP, which is *empty by construction* on a referent with no homologues: **a homologue-free referent is not an information-free one**, and a decoder does not need to have seen a sequence to score it above chance. The background is verified by total at load — 17,154,643,378 3-mers and 17,093,475,529 4-mers — and the run refuses the superseded line-local counts (16,640,807,917 / 16,324,342,706) by number rather than by path, because both are on disk and a path is not evidence of what a file holds.

**The cohort, a census.** Every wild type EXP-R2-190's certificate searched and every eligible variant of it; nothing is sampled, so rule 1's hazard is absent rather than answered and no skip-offset sensitivity exists. A variant is eligible when every token is a substitution with two *different* residues and `ddG_ML` parses as a number; that rule selects a strict subset of ProteinGym's own variant sets on all 64 Tsuboyama assays (zero variants selected here are absent from ProteinGym) and reproduces them exactly on 27. Measured cohort:

| | designs (a) | natural control (b) |
|---|---|---|
| wild types scored | **130** | **266** |
| units | **40 design series** (36 entirely zero-hit) | **124 `WT_cluster`s** |
| variants | 110,730 | 404,114 |

**The exclusion, and exactly what it costs.** The 16 designs that hit the corpus are excluded from (a); that exclusion touches **4 of the 41 series** (`EEHEE` rd3, `EEHEE` rd4, `HHH` rd4, `HEEH_KT` rd6) and leaves every one of them with zero-hit members, so it is a named, auditable removal rather than a haircut across all 41. Two of the 132 zero-hit designs (`XX|run8_1203_0001.pdb`, `r14_263_TrROS_Hall.pdb`) carry no eligible variant at all, which is why 130 are scored and why the series count is 40 rather than 41 — `TrROS_Hall/r14` had exactly one design.

**Unit of analysis and interval.** The design series — topology × round, run-family × run, or hallucination round, as EXP-R2-190 enumerated them. 40 units against the package's declared 8-unit floor, resampled through `profiles.cluster_bootstrap` at its declared 2,000 replicates under `statistics.bootstrap_unit_floor`; the natural control's unit is the dataset's own `WT_cluster`, which is the analogue of F10's 50%-identity family and is not a threshold invented here. Seed 20260813.

**Two companion readings, pre-registered rather than chosen afterwards.** (i) *Strict*: (a) restricted to the **36 series that are entirely zero-hit**, which drops the campaign siblings of the four series that contain a deposited design. (ii) *Topology*: (a) resampled at the dataset's own `WT_cluster`, which for designs is the topology label and gives **6 units** — below the floor, so it is expected to return a refusal and a point estimate rather than an interval, and it is declared here so that the coarser dependence between series of one topology is visible rather than assumed away. Neither companion can create a positive: the verdict is decided on the headline reading, and a disagreement between them is reported as a disagreement.

**Three specification decisions the design did not fix, declared before they can be tuned.** A variant floor of **30** measurements per wild type, swept over 10/30/50/100 with the cohort required identical at every value (the MegaScale count per wild type is bimodal — a wild type carries either none or more than a hundred). Duplicate measurements of one variant — 4,071 rows over 53 wild types — are **averaged**, and the number averaged into each point is carried into the artefact. And a wild type on which a channel is constant contributes no value for that channel, with the count of such drops reported per contrast rather than absorbed.

**Arms, and the identification that is not shared between them.** `protgpt2`, `progen2-small`, `progen2-base`, `progen2-medium`. **ProtGPT2 is the only arm on which the exclusion is identified**: its declared pretraining corpus *is* the searched database, and UniRef50 2021_04 holds 49.9 M clusters against the searched snapshot's 60.3 M, so absence from the searched one implies absence from the trained-on one and the bias runs safe. Every ProGen2 rung also saw **BFD30, which is not staged and was not searched**, so a design absent from UniRef50 may still be in the corpus those arms read — an asymmetry that runs in the direction that **flatters** the model. A ProGen2 result therefore does not borrow ProtGPT2's certificate and will not be reported as though it does. ZymCTRL is excluded because its rendering is EC-conditioned and a de novo design carries no EC number, so the estimand is undefined for it; ProGen3-112M is excluded because it is not a panel member and its published scoring convention is bidirectional, which is a different estimand from the summed left-to-right log-likelihood every arm here is read under.

**What each outcome licenses, stated now so it cannot be widened later.** A `positive` on ProtGPT2 would be the first evidence in this programme that a protein decoder predicts a measured phenotype on sequences its corpus provably does not contain, above what that corpus's fragment statistics and the free baselines supply. It would still not identify a mechanism, and this entry adjudicates none: the question is whether skill survives when retrieval is excluded, not how. A `negative` — ProtGPT2 predicting designed-protein stability no better than composition or corpus fragments while clearing every baseline on natural domains — is a real result about what protein decoders have learned, and will be reported plainly and without softening. An `uninterpretable_instrument_bound` is a statement about this interface and about nothing else.

**Compute and dispatch.** Cohort, baselines and analysis are CPU-only on B. Scoring is one likelihood pass per arm on the H200, dispatched through `scripts/transfer/run_external_baseline_h200.sh --pin <commit>`, one arm per card on four idle cards; the pod reads the frozen cohort artefact rather than the staged parquet, so no dataset is transferred. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for this work, as it did for EXP-R2-188 and EXP-R2-190; nothing here is dispatched through the registered stage path.

## 2026-08-12 — EXP-R2-192 read: OUTCOME NEGATIVE. On designs with no corpus homologue, ProtGPT2 beats the corpus fragment baselines and loses to hydropathy

**What was run, exactly as pre-registered above.** The frozen cohort (`results/transfer/designed_referent/cohort.json`, sha256 `caaa233d…`): 130 certified zero-hit designs over **40 design series** and 110,730 variants against 266 natural domains over **124 `WT_cluster`s** and 404,114 variants, one file, one assay, `ddG_ML` as phenotype. Baselines computed on B; scoring dispatched through `run_external_baseline_h200.sh --pin 2d8a1f27`, one arm per card on four H200s, 4–9 minutes per arm, all four pulled with digests verified and ADMITTED. The k-mer background loaded and recorded in the artefact is the **corrected** record-local count (17,154,643,378 / 17,093,475,529); the loader refuses the superseded totals by number. `results/transfer/designed_referent/designed_referent.json`.

**The verdict, per arm, with the identification each arm actually has.** The identification column is part of the table and not a note beneath it: the certificate searched UniRef50 and nothing else, so only ProtGPT2's exclusion is identified.

| arm | corpus identification | (a) designs, MODEL | (b) control, MODEL | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **protgpt2** | **exact** — its corpus *is* the searched database | **+0.0837 [+0.0408, +0.1268]** | **+0.3150 [+0.2759, +0.3501]** | **negative** |
| progen2-base | *bounded the model-favouring way* — mixture, unsearched | +0.0456 [+0.0075, +0.0859] | +0.3004 [+0.2590, +0.3414] | negative |
| progen2-medium | *bounded the model-favouring way* — UniRef90 + **BFD30 unsearched** | +0.0280 [−0.0056, +0.0630] | +0.3085 [+0.2703, +0.3454] | negative |
| progen2-small | *bounded the model-favouring way* — UniRef90 + **BFD30 unsearched** | −0.0100 [−0.0523, +0.0355] | +0.2480 [+0.2055, +0.2873] | **uninterpretable_instrument_bound** |

A ProGen2 row is a **bound, not an identified exclusion**: BFD30 was not searched, so a design certified absent from UniRef50 may still be in the corpus those arms read, and that gap runs in the direction that flatters the model. Nothing below lets a ProGen2 number borrow ProtGPT2's certificate.

**The load-bearing result is which baselines the model beats, and it is the opposite of the configuration that was anticipated.** On the corpus-disjoint designs ProtGPT2 **beats both fragment-level retrieval baselines** — MODEL − `fragment_markov_k3` = **+0.1439 [+0.1070, +0.1784]**, MODEL − `fragment_markov_k4` = **+0.1270 [+0.0923, +0.1599]** — and beats corpus composition (+0.1261 [+0.0827, +0.1681]), mutation position (+0.0893 [+0.0226, +0.1595]) and wild-type hydropathy (+0.4541). What defeats it is **free physicochemistry**: `hydropathy_change` alone reads **+0.4385 [+0.4171, +0.4593]** on the designs against the model's +0.0837, and BLOSUM62 reads +0.1616 [+0.1368, +0.1866]. MODEL − `hydropathy_change` = **−0.3548 [−0.4031, −0.3051]** and MODEL − `blosum62` = **−0.0779 [−0.1292, −0.0243]**, both intervals excluding zero *in the wrong direction* over 40 units. So the model's margin over corpus fragment statistics survives the exclusion of retrieval; its margin over a one-parameter hydrophobicity scale does not merely vanish, it reverses.

**Every channel, both sides, at 2,000 series/cluster resamples.**

| channel | (a) designs, 40 series | (b) control, 124 clusters | protgpt2 MODEL − channel on (a) | on (b) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blosum62` | +0.1616 [+0.1368, +0.1866] | +0.1783 [+0.1584, +0.1981] | **−0.0779 [−0.1292, −0.0243]** FAIL | +0.1368 [+0.1007, +0.1700] |

| `fragment_markov_k4` | −0.0432 [−0.0757, −0.0126] | +0.0008 [−0.0252, +0.0265] | +0.1270 [+0.0923, +0.1599] | +0.3142 [+0.2719, +0.3555] |

No wild type was dropped from any contrast for a constant channel, on either side, for any arm. The two ProGen2 rungs that are interpretable fail the same two baselines as ProtGPT2 **plus** `position_index` (+0.0512 [−0.0039, +0.1136] for base, +0.0336 [−0.0235, +0.0946] for medium); their fragment and composition gates pass exactly as ProtGPT2's do.

**The control side is where the gate is shown attainable, and it is — on three arms of four.** ProtGPT2, ProGen2-base and ProGen2-medium clear **all seven** baselines on the natural domains, with `hydropathy_change` the narrowest margin in each case (+0.0975, +0.0828, +0.0909, all excluding zero). **ProGen2-small does not**: MODEL − `hydropathy_change` = +0.0304 [−0.0274, +0.0885] on the control. Under the frozen rule its design-side reading is therefore **uninterpretable and is not read**, whatever it says — the gate was never shown attainable on that arm, and a null behind an unattainable gate is a statement about the instrument.

**This is a null about *ranking against a baseline*, not about the model having no signal.** ProtGPT2's design-side correlation is **positive and excludes zero**, its per-design median is **+0.1078** and **97 of 130** designs read positive. It knows something about designed-protein stability. It simply knows less about it than the sum of Kyte-Doolittle differences does — which reads positive on **129 of 130** designs at a median of +0.4474.

**The two pre-registered companions.** *Strict*, the 36 entirely zero-hit series (101 designs): ProtGPT2 **+0.0792 [+0.0337, +0.1225]** with the **same two** failures, so the verdict is unchanged; ProGen2-base +0.0393 [+0.0008, +0.0785] and ProGen2-medium +0.0211 [−0.0124, +0.0574], same failures; ProGen2-small −0.0181 [−0.0593, +0.0286]. Dropping the campaign siblings of the four series containing a deposited design changes nothing. *Topology*, the dataset's own `WT_cluster` on the design side: **6 units, below the floor, refused exactly as pre-declared**. Its point estimates are +0.1170 (protgpt2), +0.0772, +0.0691, +0.0496. Its gate list reads as seven failures for every arm and **that is the refusal, not seven findings** — at six units no percentile interval is published, so no gate can pass.

**Two controls computed after the reading, labelled `preregistered: false` in the artefact and unable to change the verdict.**

*The instrument is F10's.* Restricted to the 64 ProteinGym Tsuboyama wild types — matched 64 of 64 — this stage reads **+0.3683** for ProtGPT2 and **+0.3620** for ProGen2-medium, against the **+0.367** and **+0.365** EXP-R2-189 section 6 read off F10's own artefacts. A different code path over a different file (MegaScale parquet against ProteinGym CSV) agreeing to 0.002 is what makes the design-side number comparable to F10's at all.

*The design-side reversal is about designed sequence, not about short sequence.* The natural control restricted to the designs' own length quantiles, swept over three bands rather than cut at one. At the full design span **[40, 63] (170 naturals, 79 clusters)** ProtGPT2 reads **+0.3128 [+0.2703, +0.3533]** and clears **every** gate, including MODEL − `hydropathy_change` = **+0.1147 [+0.0446, +0.1862]** and MODEL − `blosum62` = +0.1446 [+0.1083, +0.1805]. At **[40, 47] (30 naturals, 20 clusters)** and **[40, 43] (12 naturals, 11 clusters)** the hydropathy contrast stays positive in point estimate (+0.1422, +0.1899) but its interval widens to cover zero, which is a power statement at 20 and 11 clusters and not a reversal. Set beside the design side's **−0.3548 [−0.4031, −0.3051]** over 40 units, the sign flips between natural and designed sequence at the same length, in the same file, from the same assay.

**What this settles, and what it does not.** It settles that the retrieval question is now *decidable* and has been decided once: with retrieval excluded by construction rather than estimated, ProtGPT2's phenotype prediction **does** exceed what the corpus's own 3-mer and 4-mer statistics supply, and **does not** exceed what a free hydrophobicity scale supplies. F10 bounded the model against a lookup of its corpus; this bounds it against physics that no corpus is needed for, on sequences the corpus does not contain. It does **not** say the model has learned nothing — the design-side correlation excludes zero — and it adjudicates **no mechanism**: the question asked was whether skill survives when retrieval is excluded, not how.

**Bounds.** Absence is certified against the staged UniRef50 snapshot only, so the claim is a ProtGPT2 claim; ProGen2 saw UniRef90 and BFD, neither searched, and their rows are bounds. Alignment-free is not information-free, which is what the fragment baselines priced and passed — but a 3-mer/4-mer conditional model is one fragment-level channel and not every one; a longer-range corpus statistic is unpriced. The phenotype is folding stability from one proteolysis assay, so nothing here speaks to function. `ddG_ML` is the assay's own ML fit and inherits its filters: the 536 variants ProteinGym carries that this cohort does not are exactly those it records as `-`. The design side is 40 units against the control's 124, and the six-unit topology reading is refused rather than reported, so the dependence between series of one topology is bounded only by that refusal. The post-hoc controls were added and run on B *after* the pinned GPU scoring, so they are labelled as post-hoc in the artefact and are not part of the frozen rule. `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` are not modified here; F10's row and the D1.e question both need updating and that is proposed to the coordinator rather than written.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-191 read, PARTIAL: all four cells trained, two were lost in transport, and Criterion B1 is VOID on its own text control

All four cells of the pre-declaration above ran to completion on the pinned snapshot `20260812215507_0f81e190ba55` at commit `04fdfa5`. **Two of the four are not readable on B, and the cause is transport rather than training.** Both protein controllers logged `PRESENT after 18720s` — the launcher's poll saw the artefact in the pod — and then failed the pull with `Chunk size mismatch: expected 268435456, got 0` on a tar of **8,593,715,200 bytes**, whose SHA-256 the pod side computed and recorded (`6f5e33a1…` for the base cell, `235d2776…` for the stage 1 cell). The launcher pulls the whole output directory, and the directory holds an 8.59 GB dictionary beside a 50 KB record. **No training failed and nothing is lost**: the artefacts are on GPFS where `15_replacement_faithfulness.py` reads dictionaries from in any case. Recovery is an extraction of the JSON alone and is not a re-run; it is blocked at the time of writing because the relay refuses at the Windows jump host, on four spaced probes over ten minutes. Per the standing rule a failed probe is not a cluster-health result, so nothing is concluded about the cluster.

**Both text cells were admitted on verified digests** and are the text control the pre-declaration's refusal condition is defined on. They are the same procedure to the token: identical `--steps` realised (11,367), identical scored tokens (34,002,081), identical near-duplicate screen (1,024 of 1,024 kept, maximum containment 0.4346, 106,496 training records screened), identical cap, seed and corpus. So the same-input property the diff rests on holds exactly on this side, verified rather than assumed.

**Criterion A, applied as pre-declared and unchanged by this run** — it reads the R2.4 diffing artefacts, which these dictionaries do not touch. Protein median R **3.116** (skip 0) and **3.209** (skip 40,960), IQR [2.00, 4.31], 82.1% of interior layers above 1: **INSUFFICIENT**. Text median R **0.956** and **0.954**, IQR [0.90, 1.03], 32.1% above 1: **UNRESOLVED**, held there rather than promoted, because a median 4.6% below the cut with an interquartile range straddling it is not a verdict.

**Criterion B, and the declared refusal fires on B1.**

| cell | held-out NMSE sum | median D | max D | B1 | live latents / layer | B2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:--|---:|:--|
| base / text | **16.0838** | 0.730 | 1.460 | **FAIL** | **7,608** | PASS |
| stage 1 / text | **5.7072** | 0.202 | 1.174 | **FAIL** | **4,900** | PASS |

**B1 is VOID as a gate.** The text control fails it — on both clauses in the base cell and on the max clause in the stage 1 cell — so it is a criterion this programme's own control cannot pass, which the pre-declaration named in advance as a specification defect rather than a protein result. Its numbers are descriptive from here and no protein cell may be judged by it. *The void was foreseen and deliberately not tuned away*: the pre-declaration's own orientation figures recorded the R2.3 text dictionary at max D 1.13–1.20 and said in terms that it "would fail on max". Leaving the criterion as written and letting it void is the discipline working; moving the cut after seeing which side it excluded would have been the failure. The mechanism is visible and unremarkable — D divides by the cross-checkpoint residual, which is small at the shallow layers, so the ratio is unstable exactly where neither quantity is large.

**B2 is not void: the text control clears it in both cells**, at 7,608 and 4,900 live latents per layer against `d_model` 4,096. B2 therefore remains the live gate, and **the protein cells' B2 is the number that decides whether a protein feature diff is a statement about two models or about two fitted bases.** That number exists on GPFS and is not yet readable. Nothing is inferred here from R2.3's protein figure.

**The matched certificate reads exactly as predicted.** The cross-checkpoint text pair — the diffing pair — returns `MISMATCH` with `disagreements` exactly `["backbone_sha256"]`, `max_tokens [1024, 1024]`, `max_tokens_agree true`, and the other fourteen matched fields agreeing. The comparator was not loosened and no fourth verdict was added. The two within-checkpoint cross-mode pairs need the protein cells and are pending.

**The base-versus-stage-1 contrast, on the side that is readable, and what it does not answer.** At an identical recipe, identical inputs and an identical held-out draw, the base checkpoint's text-mode block outputs are **2.82x harder to reconstruct sparsely** than the adapted checkpoint's — held-out NMSE sum 16.08 against 5.71, mean per layer 0.503 against 0.178 — and its dictionary keeps **7,608 live latents per layer against 4,900**, with 7.1% dead against 40.2%. Continued protein pretraining left this backbone's *text* representations substantially easier for a 2x k=32 per-layer transcoder to capture. Both curves are still falling slowly at the budget (base 16.172 → 16.084 and stage 1 5.746 → 5.707 over their last 1,367 steps), so both text cells are mildly undertrained, as R2.3's text cell was.

**That contrast is not the control's answer, and must not be read as one.** The question these cells were added for is whether *negative sequential recovery* belongs to the adaptation or to this recipe on a 7B backbone, and recovery is behavioural: it needs `15_replacement_faithfulness.py`, which has not been run on any of these four dictionaries. What this run delivers is the reconstruction and basis half — the prerequisite — and the recovery comparison is a separate scoring pass on dictionaries that already exist. Recorded so the reconstruction contrast is not quietly promoted into the behavioural claim it resembles.

**Bounds.** Two of four cells read; every protein statement in the pre-declaration is still open. One seed and one expansion factor per cell. The base checkpoint's protein mode remains behaviourally unmeasurable and is a pre-adaptation representational reference only. No feature-matching instrument was built, and none is warranted until B2 is read on the protein cells.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-193 pre-registered: is EXP-R2-192's design-versus-natural reversal an interaction, or a length effect? Frozen before any interaction is computed

**What is being tested.** EXP-R2-192 reported two contrasts and never differenced them. On the certified corpus-disjoint designs ProtGPT2's phenotype ranking loses to a one-parameter Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy sum, MODEL − `hydropathy_change` = **−0.3548 [−0.4031, −0.3051]** over 40 series; on the natural domains restricted to the designs' own length span the same arm, the same file and the same assay read **+0.1147 [+0.0446, +0.1862]** over 79 clusters. That length-matched control was computed *after* the pinned scoring, was labelled `preregistered: false` in the artefact, and was deliberately not promoted. It is the most interesting thing in the artefact and it is currently inadmissible. This entry freezes the confirmatory test of it. **The estimand is the interaction — the difference between the two contrasts, with one joint interval — not the two contrasts reported side by side.** The question is whether the model's advantage over free physicochemistry depends on the sequence being *natural* rather than on its being *short*, or on anything else that co-varies with designedness in this cohort. No mechanism is adjudicated: this asks whether the interaction is real, not why.

**What already exists, and is therefore not evidence for anything below.** ProtGPT2's design-side hydropathy contrast and its `[40, 63]` length-band control both exist, in `results/transfer/designed_referent/designed_referent.json` and in the EXP-R2-192 read entry above. Their difference is about **−0.47**, so the pooled ProtGPT2 point estimate of the interaction is essentially already known and is *not* confirmatory. What does not exist anywhere is a joint interval on that difference, any per-family decomposition, and any reading of the other three arms' length-band contrasts. The ProGen2 band contrasts are on disk — `_post_hoc` loops over every scored arm — but they have never been read into any document, and **they were not opened before this entry was written**. The arm axis is therefore *blinded replication*, not out-of-sample replication, and it is reported as the weaker thing it is. Nothing in this entry is a result; every count below is a property of the cohort, computable without a model score and without a correlation, and every one was computed before the rule was written.

**The interaction statistic, exactly.** For an arm, a design subset and a natural subset, take each wild type's contrast `c(w) = ρ_model(w) − ρ_hydropathy_change(w)` from the existing per-wild-type Spearman values in `model_<arm>.json` and `baselines.json`. Average `c` within unit — design series on the design side, the dataset's own `WT_cluster` on the natural side, the units EXP-R2-192 declared — then

> **Δ = (mean over design units of unit-mean c) − (mean over natural units of unit-mean c).**

Δ < 0 is the observed direction: the model's advantage over hydropathy is *lower* on designs than on length-matched naturals. Δ is decomposed in the artefact into its four halves (model and hydropathy, each side) so that which side moves is visible rather than inferred.

**Unit, resampling and floor, all the package's own.** `profiles.cluster_means` for the unit averages and `statistics.bootstrap_unit_floor` at its declared `MINIMUM_BOOTSTRAP_UNITS = 8` on **each side separately**; 2,000 resamples and the 95% percentile rule, the values every clustered interval in this line of work is taken at; seed 20260813, EXP-R2-192's own. The resample is stratified: one draw takes `n_design` design units with replacement and `n_natural` natural units with replacement, and Δ is recomputed inside the draw, because an interval on a difference of two means taken separately is not an interval on the difference. If either side falls below the eight-unit floor the interval is refused and only the point estimate is published, exactly as EXP-R2-192's topology companion was refused.

**Axis 1 — arms.** `protgpt2` is the origin arm and its pooled reading is not confirmatory. `progen2-base`, `progen2-medium` and `progen2-small` are the replication axis. **The corpus-identification asymmetry that bounds the ProGen2 rows in F12 does not apply here and is not inherited.** F12's ProGen2 rows are bounds because BFD30 was not searched, so a design certified absent from UniRef50 may still be in those arms' corpora — that gap matters only for a claim about *retrieval*. Δ is a within-arm difference between two sides of one file under one baseline that no corpus is needed for; whether a design is in BFD30 changes nothing about whether hydropathy beats the model more on designs than on naturals. Saying so explicitly is the point: a caveat carried where it does not bind is as much a defect as one dropped where it does.

**`progen2-small` is admitted, and the reason is that the gate has changed.** In EXP-R2-192 it returned `uninterpretable_instrument_bound` because MODEL − `hydropathy_change` = +0.0304 [−0.0274, +0.0885] on the natural control, so the *conjunction gate* "beats every baseline" was never shown attainable on that arm and its design side could not be read. That rule guarded a threshold against a baseline. Δ is not a threshold against a baseline: it does not require the contrast to be positive on either side, only to differ between them, and both sides are the same arm under the same procedure. What attainability requires here is that a non-zero Δ be detectable at all under this procedure, and that is what the placebo control below tests directly. Admitted, therefore — with the mechanical caveat declared now: this arm's natural-side contrast is the smallest of the four, so its Δ is compressed for a reason that has nothing to do with designedness, and a smaller Δ on `progen2-small` is expected and is **not** independent evidence against the interaction. The overall verdict is constructed so that it does not turn on this arm.

**Axis 2 — design family, and its honest standing.** EXP-R2-190's 40 scored series partition into three families by construction: **topology-prefixed** (`EEHEE`, `EHEE`, `HEEH`, `HEEH_KT`, `HHH`) 12 series over 74 designs; **run-keyed** (`EA`, `GG`, `XX`) 18 series over 37 designs; **hallucination** (`TrROS_Hall`) 10 series over 19 designs. All three clear the eight-unit floor, so none is dropped and the floor is not shrunk to fit one. **This is a generalisation test, not an independent replication**, and the difference is stated rather than blurred: the pooled estimate was taken over all 40 series, so no family is data whose answer has not been seen in aggregate. What a family-held-out reading can establish is that the interaction is reproduced in each family separately rather than carried by one; what it cannot establish is independence. It is reported as the former.

**Length matching, declared with its unit counts before any Δ exists.** The natural side of each axis is the naturals whose length lies in that design subset's own span, padded by `p ∈ {0, 2, 5}` residues. `p = 0` is primary; the sweep is the invariance check that the standing rule requires wherever a threshold is unavoidable. The counts are cohort facts and are frozen here:

| design subset | series | design length span | naturals at p=0 | at p=2 | at p=5 |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| all zero-hit designs | 40 | [40, 63] | 170 / **79 clusters** | 192 / 87 | 226 / 102 |
| topology | 12 | [40, 43] | 12 / **11 clusters** | 28 / 20 | 55 / 29 |
| run-keyed | 18 | [47, 47] | 5 / **4 clusters — below floor** | 19 / 10 | 48 / 27 |
| hallucination | 10 | [46, 63] | 147 / **64 clusters** | 175 / 75 | 208 / 93 |

Every run-keyed design is exactly 47 residues and only five natural domains in the file are, over four clusters, so **run-keyed at `p = 0` is refused by the floor before it is run**, and its primary reading is declared here to be `p = 2` rather than chosen afterwards. The natural length distribution is skewed long (median 58 against the designs' 47), so a band is a restriction and not a match; the residual length imbalance inside each band is reported, and the covariate-adjusted reading below is what answers it.

**The decision rule, per axis.** With both sides above the floor, and writing the 95% interval as [lo, hi]:

- **CONFIRMS** — `hi < 0` and the point estimate ≤ **−0.15**.
- **ATTENUATED** — `hi < 0` and the point estimate > −0.15: a real interaction, smaller than the declared magnitude.
- **REFUTES** — `hi ≥ 0` and `lo > −0.15`: the axis excludes an interaction of the declared magnitude, and this includes an interval lying wholly above zero.
- **UNRESOLVED** — otherwise, i.e. the interval covers both 0 and −0.15, or either side is below the floor. **An unresolved axis is underpower and is reported as underpower, never as absence.**

The **−0.15** magnitude is roughly one third of the −0.47 the two existing ProtGPT2 numbers imply, fixed now so it cannot be moved after the intervals are seen.

**The overall verdict.**

- **CONFIRMED** requires all of: the placebo calibration passes; the pooled ProtGPT2 axis CONFIRMS; at least two of the three families CONFIRM on ProtGPT2 with none REFUTING; at least two of the three ProGen2 arms CONFIRM on the pooled design side with none REFUTING; and the sign of Δ is invariant across `p ∈ {0, 2, 5}` on every confirming axis.
- **REFUTED** if the pooled ProtGPT2 axis REFUTES, or at least two of the three families REFUTE, or at least two of the three ProGen2 arms REFUTE.
- **UNDERPOWERED** otherwise, and stated as that word.

**Controls the design carries.**

1. *Placebo calibration, and the attainability check for this statistic.* The pooled length-matched natural side ([40, 63], 79 clusters) is split at random into two halves **by cluster**, twenty times under seeds 20260813+i, and Δ is computed between the halves. Two sides that differ in nothing should return zero. At 95% about one of twenty intervals should exclude zero; **if more than three of twenty do, the statistic is miscalibrated and every axis in this entry is UNRESOLVED**, whatever it reads.
2. *Length inside natural sequence alone.* Δ between the naturals inside the pooled design band and the 96 naturals outside it, over 57 clusters. This measures how much the contrast moves with length when nothing is designed. Descriptive, not a gate, but a large same-signed value would mean length is not excluded by band matching alone.
3. *Composition — the control that separates naturalness from amino-acid usage.* Designs are not compositionally typical (mean `E` 0.176 against the naturals' 0.088, `S` 0.019 against 0.053, `P` 0.015 against 0.034; mean Kyte-Doolittle −0.865 against −0.544), and `hydropathy_change` is a composition-weighted sum, so this is the confound that matters most after length. An out-of-fold propensity score `P(designed | 20 residue frequencies, length)` is fitted by 5-fold stratified logistic regression (`C = 1`, `max_iter = 5000`, split seed 0) over the 130 zero-hit designs and 266 naturals, and both sides are restricted to the propensity common support; Δ is recomputed on the restricted subcohort under the identical statistic and floor. Restriction windows swept over the common support and over `[0.2, 0.8]` and `[0.3, 0.7]`. Feasibility, measured before this rule was written and using no phenotype: the common support holds **113 designs / 40 series against 117 naturals / 59 clusters**, `[0.3, 0.7]` holds 129 / 40 against 66 / 35, `[0.2, 0.8]` holds 130 / 40 against 165 / 76 — every window clears the floor on both sides. **Balance is not assumed from restriction**: standardised mean differences on length, wild-type mean Kyte-Doolittle and all 20 residue frequencies are reported before and after, and balance counts as achieved only if `max |SMD| ≤ 0.25` afterwards. The composition axis is **not** part of the confirm/refute verdict on the length question; it bounds what that verdict may be read to mean. If it does not confirm, or if balance is not achieved, the plain statement is that this finding cannot distinguish naturalness from amino-acid usage, and it will be made in those words.
4. *Covariate-adjusted interaction, which is what answers residual imbalance inside a band.* At wild-type level, `c(w) = α + γ·designed(w) + β·covariates(w)`, with γ the interaction adjusted for the covariates and resampled under the identical stratified unit bootstrap. Four covariate sets, declared now: **S1** length; **S2** length + wild-type mean Kyte-Doolittle; **S3** S2 + the first five principal components of the 20-dimensional composition; **S4** length + log variant count + phenotype standard deviation. S1 answers length without a band, S2 and S3 answer composition without a restriction, S4 answers the two cohort asymmetries in item 5. Linear adjustment extrapolates where support is thin, which is why it complements the restriction rather than replacing it.
5. *The two cohort asymmetries, reported as numbers rather than acknowledged.* The design side carries **fewer variants per wild type** (median 860, total 110,730) than the length-matched natural side (median 1,128, total 242,948), and a **narrower phenotype range** (median `ddG_ML` span 4.56 against 5.42, median standard deviation 0.73 against 1.03). Both attenuate a Spearman correlation on the design side, but they attenuate *both* channels, so they cannot by themselves produce a differential; they can only do so if the model and the hydropathy sum differ in noise sensitivity. Covariate set S4 prices exactly that, and 81 naturals over 51 clusters fall inside the designs' own variant-count and phenotype-spread ranges within the band, which is above the floor and is reported as a restricted reading beside S4.
6. *Specificity.* Δ is computed for all seven baselines, not only `hydropathy_change`. If every channel shows the same large negative interaction the finding is "the model does relatively worse on designs against everything", which is a different and weaker claim than a hydropathy-specific reversal. Descriptive, declared in advance so that whichever pattern appears cannot be presented as the one that was expected.

**Compute.** **Zero GPU.** Every model likelihood this needs already exists as a per-wild-type Spearman in the four `model_<arm>.json` artefacts from EXP-R2-192's pinned pass at commit `2d8a1f27`, and every baseline in `baselines.json`; the cohort digest is checked against both before anything is read, so a re-analysis cannot silently mix cohorts. This is CPU re-analysis on B, one new `interaction` stage in `scripts/transfer/29_designed_referent.py` writing `results/transfer/designed_referent/interaction.json`. No pod is taken and no dataset moves. `arm_can_run` raises `unknown stage` for this work as it did for EXP-R2-188, EXP-R2-190 and EXP-R2-192; nothing here is dispatched per arm.

**What each outcome licenses.** A **CONFIRMED** verdict makes the sign flip a promotable qualification on F12: the model's deficit against free physicochemistry would be a property of *designed* sequence and not of short sequence, which sharpens F12 from "the model loses to hydropathy" to "the model loses to hydropathy where the sequence is not natural, and beats it where it is". It would still identify no mechanism and would still rest on one file, one assay and one phenotype. A **REFUTED** verdict costs the programme nothing, because the observation is unpromoted: it would say the length-matched control does not survive its own confirmatory test and F12 stands exactly as written, with the post-hoc band control struck rather than promoted. An **UNDERPOWERED** verdict is a statement about 40 design series against a thin short-natural stratum and is not evidence that the interaction is absent. `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` are not modified by this entry or by its reading; any change to F12 or the D1.e row is proposed to the coordinator.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-194 pre-declared: the base-versus-stage-1 recovery comparison, and what would put negative sequential recovery in the adaptation rather than in the recipe

Frozen before any recovery number exists on these four dictionaries. EXP-R2-191 delivered the reconstruction and basis half of the R2.4 cells; recovery is behavioural and reconstruction is not, so the control those cells were added for is not answered until this runs. The reading is fixed here because the answer will be readable either way after the fact.

**The question, stated as an attribution.** EXP-R2-182 found NLL recovery negative in all four R2.3 cells on `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` at 2x expansion, `k` 32. EXP-R2-188 found recovery positive and monotone on all four panel arms at 12x. Two localisations survive and nothing on disk separates them: the failure belongs to the **adaptation** — something continued protein pretraining did to these weights — or to the **recipe on a 7B backbone**, 2x expansion at `k` 32 on 34 M tokens, adaptation or no. The base cells exist to separate exactly this, because they are the same recipe, the same corpus, the same seed and the same held-out draw on the pre-adaptation weights.

**The control exists on one mode only, and that is a bound rather than a choice.** `Llama-2-7b-hf`'s protein mode is behaviourally unmeasurable on the current estimand, so there is no base-side protein recovery number to compare against and **no cross-checkpoint protein recovery contrast exists**. The base protein dictionary is therefore **not scored here at all**: the stage's joint loader gate is structural only and would produce a complete-looking artefact whose behavioural numbers must not be read, and a number that must not be read is a number that eventually gets read. Three cells are scored — `base/text`, `stage1/text`, `stage1/protein` — and the attribution below is a **text-mode** attribution for this lineage.

**Configuration.** `15_replacement_faithfulness.py`, `--replacement-kind local` against each cell's own dictionary in place on GPFS, `--sequences 128`, `--max-tokens 1024`, `--replacement-front 1,2,4,8,16,32`, `--bootstrap 1000`, cohort draw seed 20260728 at skip 0, and every other cohort setting identical to EXP-R2-182's so the two series are one procedure. `--matched-against` is each dictionary's own mode-partner within its own checkpoint, which is the pair that certifies `MATCHED`; the cross-checkpoint pairs are the diffing pairs and are not what this flag is for. Nothing needs to reach B: the dictionaries, their records and the scoring all live in the pod, so the transport failure that stranded the two protein records on GPFS does not block this pass.

**The estimand is the SIGN and the CROSS-CHECKPOINT DIFFERENCE, and explicitly not the stage's 0.80 gate.** That gate is already known to be unattainable on the text control at this dictionary family — EXP-R2-182's text cells FAIL it too — so a FAIL on any cell here carries no information about modality or about adaptation, and none will be read from it. What is read is: per cell, the full-stack recovery with its own 95% paired-per-sequence interval, **and its numerator and denominator in nats**, because a ratio whose denominator differs across checkpoints hides whichever direction a reader does not check.

**Per-cell sign verdict.** NEGATIVE if the cell's 95% interval lies entirely below zero; POSITIVE if entirely above; UNRESOLVED if it covers zero.

**Cross-cell separation, and it is declared conservative.** `base/text` against `stage1/text` separates when their two 95% intervals do not overlap. This is an **unpaired** comparison — the stage scores one arm at a time, and the two cells have different clean and mean-ablated endpoints, so no paired interval across them exists without building one, and none is built. Non-separation is therefore **UNRESOLVED and never "the same"**.

**The four outcomes, and what each licenses.**

- **ADAPTATION.** `stage1/text` NEGATIVE, `base/text` POSITIVE, intervals separated. Then the same recipe on the same backbone and the same inputs yields a dictionary that survives sequential replacement before adaptation and one that does not after, so the failure travels with the adapted weights. Licensed: negative sequential recovery is a property of the adaptation on this lineage, in text mode. Not licensed: any account of *why*, anything about the protein mode, anything about stage 2, and any claim that the adaptation would do this at another expansion factor.
- **RECIPE.** Both NEGATIVE. Then the pre-adaptation checkpoint fails identically and the adaptation cannot be what produces it. Licensed: the failure is a property of this dictionary recipe at this backbone scale, and **EXP-R2-182's result must stop being read as a fact about the joint checkpoint**. This is the outcome that would most change what is already written.
- **NON-REPRODUCTION.** `stage1/text` POSITIVE. Then the phenomenon this comparison exists to localise is absent under the new settings, and the ADAPTATION/RECIPE contrast is void rather than resolved. **Two things moved at once and the reading must say so**: the token cap went 512 → 1024 on the text side and the corpus seed changed, so a non-reproduction is "not reproduced under a changed cap and seed", never "the cap did it". *This is the one comparison in this entry that is confounded, and it is confounded by EXP-R2-191's own equal-cap decision, which was taken for a different and good reason.* The base-versus-stage-1 contrast itself is unaffected: both cells run at 1024 with one seed and one draw, and differ only in the backbone.
- **OTHER.** Anything else, including `base/text` NEGATIVE with `stage1/text` POSITIVE, or either UNRESOLVED. Reported as measured with no attribution recorded, on EXP-R2-186's Branch C convention.

**One secondary reading, free because the front sweep is extra conditions of the same behavioural sweep.** The `k = 1` front gives the per-block certificate on the **base** cell, which does not exist for any pre-adaptation checkpoint in this programme. EXP-R2-186 and EXP-R2-188 put that number at 0.87–0.96 on the joint checkpoint and 0.93–0.9998 on six panel cells; whether the base cell joins that band is a fact about how portable "a single replaced block recovers nearly all of the mean-ablation gap" is. It is reported and nothing is built on it.

**Voiding conditions, declared in advance.** If a cell's attainability ceiling falls below the stage's own threshold, that cell is reported unattainable and enters no comparison. If the `k = 32` front row fails to reproduce that cell's headline recovery bit-exactly, the run is a specification defect and is voided rather than reported, which is the invariant EXP-R2-186 and EXP-R2-188 both turned on.

**Bounds.** Text-only attribution, because the base protein mode is unmeasurable — this is D3.h's standing bound and no result here relaxes it. One seed per cell, so nothing prices dictionary-seed variability; R2.3's two seeds are the only evidence it is small. One cohort at one draw, no skip-offset condition, inherited from EXP-R2-182. One expansion factor, 2x, so nothing here speaks to whether either outcome survives at 12x — which is the axis on which the joint checkpoint and the panel arms already differ. Six fronts on 32 blocks samples the depth curve, and a front is always a prefix. Recovery is behavioural and the reconstruction contrast EXP-R2-191 measured is not, and the two are not to be substituted for one another in either direction.
