## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-193 read: CONFIRMED on length, NOT SEPARATED on composition. The design-versus-natural sign flip is an interaction of −0.47 that survives every axis it was declared on

**What was run, exactly as pre-registered above.** Every model likelihood already existed: the four `model_<arm>.json` artefacts from EXP-R2-192's pinned pass at commit `2d8a1f27`, checked against the cohort digest before anything was read. **Zero GPU, no pod, ten seconds of CPU on B**, one new `interaction` stage writing `results/transfer/designed_referent/interaction.json`. The two resamplers it adds are declared in the package's resampler inventory and exercised against the eight-unit floor by `tests/test_transfer_audit_invariants.py`, so neither arrived without a decision.

**The headline, and it is one number.** On ProtGPT2, over the 40 design series against the 79 natural `WT_cluster`s inside the designs' own length span,

> **Δ = (MODEL − hydropathy) on designs − (MODEL − hydropathy) on length-matched naturals = −0.4695 [−0.5535, −0.3889]**

with the interval taken jointly on the difference rather than assembled from two separate means. **All sixteen arm × design-subset cells confirm, and the sign is invariant across all three length pads in every one of them.**

| axis | units, design vs natural | Δ | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **protgpt2, pooled** (origin, *not confirmatory*) | 40 series / 79 clusters, band [40, 63] | **−0.4695 [−0.5535, −0.3889]** | confirms |
| protgpt2, topology | 12 / 11, band [40, 43] | −0.4503 [−0.6799, −0.2236] | confirms |
| protgpt2, run-keyed | 18 / 10, band [45, 49] at pad 2 | −0.4588 [−0.6300, −0.2912] | confirms |
| protgpt2, hallucination | 10 / 64, band [46, 63] | −0.4854 [−0.5863, −0.3836] | confirms |
| progen2-base, pooled | 40 / 79 | −0.4734 [−0.5606, −0.3901] | confirms |
| progen2-medium, pooled | 40 / 79 | −0.4958 [−0.5781, −0.4168] | confirms |
| progen2-small, pooled | 40 / 79 | −0.4894 [−0.5758, −0.3995] | confirms |

Run-keyed at pad 0 was **refused by the floor exactly as pre-declared** — every run-keyed design is 47 residues and only four natural clusters in the file are — and its primary reading is pad 2, declared before the numbers existed rather than chosen after them. The three families reproduce the pooled value to within 0.04 of each other despite spanning 10, 12 and 18 series and three different length regimes, so the interaction is not carried by one family. The three ProGen2 arms reproduce it to within 0.03 of ProtGPT2.

**Which numbers were already on disk, and therefore are not evidence.** ProtGPT2's pooled design side (−0.3548) and its `[40, 63]` band control (+0.1147) both existed and their difference was already implied, so the pooled row above is a *joint interval on an already-known point estimate* and nothing more. The three ProGen2 arms' band contrasts also existed in `designed_referent.json`, unread in any document; they were not opened before the pre-registration was written, which makes the arm axis **blinded replication and not out-of-sample replication**. The family decomposition and every control below did not exist in any form.

**The corpus-identification caveat that bounds F12's ProGen2 rows does not apply here, and inheriting it would have been wrong.** Those rows are bounds because BFD30 was never searched, which matters only for a claim about retrieval. Δ is a within-arm difference between two sides of one file under a baseline no corpus is needed for; whether a design sits in BFD30 has no bearing on whether hydropathy beats the model more on designs than on naturals. **`progen2-small` was admitted for the same reason** — EXP-R2-192's `uninterpretable_instrument_bound` voided a *conjunction gate against a baseline*, and Δ is not one; it requires the contrast to be positive nowhere, only to differ between sides. Its Δ, −0.4894, is indistinguishable from the other three, so the arm the frozen rule could not read on the earlier question reads normally on this one.

**Length is excluded, and it is excluded by measurement rather than by matching.** The pre-registered placebo splits the length-matched natural side at random by cluster twenty times: **one of twenty intervals excludes zero**, which is exactly nominal at 95%, and the twenty point estimates span −0.133 to +0.122 against the −0.47 being tested. The statistic does not manufacture a difference. The pre-registered length placebo then compares naturals inside the pooled band against those outside it — a median length shift of 56 to 67 — and returns **+0.0403 [−0.0647, +0.1480]** on ProtGPT2, zero and if anything the wrong sign. A sharper split added afterwards and labelled post-hoc, short against long naturals *inside* the band at medians 44 and 57, which is the design-versus-natural length gap of 43 against 56 almost exactly, returns **+0.0450 [−0.0934, +0.1858]** over 24 and 58 clusters. **A length shift of the size that separates designs from their controls moves this contrast by about +0.04 with an interval that excludes any effect of the declared magnitude. It cannot produce −0.47, and it has the wrong sign.** The covariate-adjusted reading agrees without needing a band at all: adjusting for length alone gives **−0.5137 [−0.6013, −0.4211]**.

**The two cohort asymmetries are priced and neither carries it.** The design side has fewer variants per wild type (median 860 against 1,128) and a narrower phenotype range (median `ddG_ML` span 4.56 against 5.42, standard deviation 0.73 against 1.03), both of which attenuate a Spearman correlation — but they attenuate *both* channels, so they can only produce a differential if the two channels differ in noise sensitivity. Adjusting for length, log variant count and phenotype spread gives **−0.3872 [−0.4766, −0.2913]**; restricting to the 81 naturals over 51 clusters whose variant count and phenotype spread both fall inside the designs' own ranges gives **−0.3750 [−0.4659, −0.2820]**. Both attenuate the estimate by about a fifth and neither removes it.

**The composition control could not be built at balance, and that is the honest limit of this result.** The pre-registered propensity restriction fails its own declared balance criterion in every window: `max |SMD|` is **1.775 before** and **1.478, 1.501 and 1.623 after**, against the declared 0.25, and in every case the offending covariate is **glutamate frequency**. Designs carry a median E frequency of 0.186 against the naturals' 0.086, and 73% of designs sit above the naturals' 90th percentile — the two sides are close to *separated* on one residue, and a restriction cannot balance what barely overlaps. This is non-overlap, not underpower: the restricted windows hold 40 design series against 35 to 76 natural clusters, far above the floor. The interaction on them reads −0.4486 to −0.5277 and confirms in all twelve cells, but a confirming number from an unbalanced comparison is not a composition control and is not reported as one.

Two further matched constructions were built afterwards, labelled post-hoc, selected on **covariates alone with no outcome consulted**, and they close the gap without shutting it. Matching explicitly on glutamate (E ∈ [0.11, 0.14] inside the pooled band, 22 designs over 10 series against 31 naturals over 20 clusters) balances glutamate and returns **−0.4533 [−0.6194, −0.3018]** — but it opens a length imbalance of 2.14 SD. The single cell in which glutamate **and** length are both balanced at the 0.25 threshold (E ∈ [0.08, 0.18] ∩ length [40, 47], 53 designs over 24 series against 12 naturals over 10 clusters) returns **−0.4912 [−0.7276, −0.2644]** — and there serine is imbalanced at 1.32 SD. Adjusting linearly for length, mean hydropathy and five composition principal components gives **−0.4034 [−0.5595, −0.2530]**, but that extrapolates across exactly the region where the two sides do not overlap. **No construction in this cohort reaches balance on all twenty-two covariates at once; closing one composition axis opens another.** So: length is excluded, glutamate alone is excluded, mean hydropathy is excluded, and a five-component linear summary of composition is excluded — but **amino-acid usage as a whole is not**, and this result therefore cannot distinguish "the sequence is natural" from "the sequence has the amino-acid composition natural domains have". Stated plainly because it is the one thing the confirmatory design could not deliver.

**The pre-registered specificity control materially qualifies what the reversal is about, and it went the way that was not anticipated.** Δ was computed on all seven baselines, not only hydropathy, and **six of the seven are negative with intervals excluding zero** on ProtGPT2: `hydropathy_change` −0.4695, `background_composition` −0.2514, `position_index` −0.2407, `blosum62` −0.2225, `fragment_markov_k3` −0.1826, `fragment_markov_k4` −0.1755, and `wt_hydropathy` +0.0581 [−0.0247, +0.1445]. **The interaction is not hydropathy-specific.** Its four halves say why: going from length-matched naturals to designs, the **model falls by 0.229** (+0.3128 to +0.0837), which every channel shares because it is the model's own term; and **Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy change rises by 0.241** (+0.1980 to +0.4385), which is specific to that channel. The two are almost exactly equal, they add, and hydropathy is the only channel where they add into a **sign reversal** rather than into a shrunken margin. So the honest description is a *conjunction*: a protein decoder that predicts designed-protein stability markedly worse than it predicts natural-domain stability, and a hydrophobicity scale that predicts designed-protein stability markedly *better*. Reporting only the hydropathy row would have made a general fact about the model look like a specific fact about hydropathy.

**Verdict: CONFIRMED on the question that was asked.** The advantage does not depend on the sequence being short. Every pre-registered condition is met — placebo calibrated at one in twenty, pooled origin axis confirming, three of three families confirming with none refuting, three of three replication arms confirming with none refuting, sign invariant across the pad sweep everywhere. **What it is not confirmed against is composition**, for the reason above, and the pre-registration said in advance that the composition axis bounds the interpretation rather than the verdict.

**Bounds.** The pooled ProtGPT2 point estimate was already implied by two numbers on disk and only its interval is new; the arm axis is blinded rather than out-of-sample; the family axis is a generalisation test over a partition of an estimate already taken over all 40 series, not an independent replication, and it was declared as that in advance. Composition is not separated from naturalness, so "natural" here means "natural or compositionally natural-like" and no narrower reading is licensed. The interaction is not hydropathy-specific; it is a conjunction of a model deficit shared by six channels and a hydropathy gain specific to one. This adjudicates **no mechanism** and was not designed to — it asks whether the interaction is real, not why. One file, one proteolysis assay, one phenotype, and the same 40 design series F12 rests on. `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` are not modified here; F12 now has a confirmed length-matched qualification and a composition bound that the register does not yet carry, and both are proposed to the coordinator rather than written.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-194 PAUSED before dispatch: the cluster errored, and a fail-closed check that tests reachability does not test health

**No scoring run exists and none was dispatched.** EXP-R2-194's three cells were armed on a dispatcher that waited for the relay and refused to launch unless all four cards read under 1000 MiB in-pod. It was disarmed on instruction before the relay returned, and the record is checkable: no `r194` controller log, no `r194` dispatch record, no `r194` results directory, and the dispatcher's own log carries one line — that it was armed and waiting.

**The defect in that fail-closed condition is worth recording, because it is a class of error and not an incident.** The check tested two things, relay reachability and card occupancy, and **neither distinguishes a healthy idle cluster from an errored one**. An errored cluster reports idle cards; a repaired relay in front of a broken cluster satisfies both conditions at once. So the guard would have dispatched a three-cell 7B scoring pass into a cluster that could not complete it, and a campaign that fails halfway is worse than one that never starts — it leaves partial artefacts that a later reader must be told to distrust. The generalisation: **an occupancy check is a courtesy to other campaigns, not a health gate**, and the two must not be conflated because one is cheap to write and the other is not.

**The pre-declaration is untouched and the delay costs the result nothing.** Criteria A and B for the dictionaries, and the four outcomes of the recovery comparison — ADAPTATION, RECIPE, NON-REPRODUCTION, OTHER — are frozen in the commit that precedes any recovery number. When the cluster is repaired the pass runs against exactly those criteria, on the same snapshot pinned at `04fdfa5`, whose stage-15 code was verified byte-identical to the pin that produced EXP-R2-182 and EXP-R2-186 to 188. That is the whole point of committing a rule before the hardware that would test it.

**What is still outstanding, so a later reader does not mistake the pause for a result.** Two of EXP-R2-191's four cells remain unread on B — the protein records were stranded by a transport failure and their **Criterion B2 is the number that decides whether a protein feature diff is a statement about two models or about two fitted bases**. A read-only JSON recovery remains on a five-minute retry; it dispatches nothing and either works or does not. The two within-checkpoint matched certificates and the entire recovery comparison are pending. **Nothing was substituted for them**: reproducing three 7B-backbone scoring passes on a 46 GB card would be a different experiment wearing the same name, and the L20 was not used.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-195 pre-declared: does the SIGN of full-stack replacement recovery depend on dictionary width? A 2x-to-12x expansion sweep on `gpt2`, frozen before any dictionary is trained

Frozen before the first training step. The anchor run described below is a validation of the scoring harness against an artefact that already exists; no dictionary of this sweep exists yet and no width has been scored.

**The question, and the boundary it must not be read past.** EXP-R2-182 found NLL recovery negative in all four R2.3 cells on `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`. EXP-R2-186 excluded single-block reconstruction as the cause and failed to establish compounding; EXP-R2-188 showed the non-monotonicity does not travel to the panel arms; EXP-R2-191 excluded the train/eval population gap and excluded undertraining on the protein side. One mundane candidate has never been tested: those cells ran at **2x expansion** and F11's positive results run at **12x**. If a 2x dictionary produces negative full-stack recovery *on a text control where the same recipe at 12x is strongly positive*, then a negative sign is something the recipe does at a width, and EXP-R2-182's result is a fact about the recipe before it is a fact about the checkpoint or the modality. **This experiment does not settle the joint checkpoint's attribution.** EXP-R2-194 is the frozen comparison that does, on that lineage, and it is paused on the errored cluster. This one asks only whether the recipe's width produces a negative sign **at all**, on an arm where a positive result already exists. Neither result may be read as having settled the other, and EXP-R2-194's own bounds paragraph names this axis as the one it cannot reach: "One expansion factor, 2x, so nothing here speaks to whether either outcome survives at 12x."

**The arm, and why it is this one.** `gpt2` — 124 M parameters, 12 blocks × 768 — because it is a panel arm carrying an F11-era **positive** replacement result at 12x, so the sweep has a known anchor at one end that can be checked rather than assumed, and because 12 blocks and a 768-wide residual make four widths affordable on a single workstation card each. Its existing result is **+0.9091 [+0.9037, +0.9136]** at seed 20260806 and +0.9084 [+0.9028, +0.9128] at seed 20260807 (EXP-R2-141, re-scored unchanged under the front sweep in EXP-R2-188).

**The sweep, and width is the only thing that moves.** Four cells, `17_train_transcoder.py --arm gpt2 --architecture plt`, `--d-hidden` ∈ **1536, 3072, 6144, 9216** = 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x of `d_model` 768. Every other setting is the F11-era `gpt2` dictionary's own, read off that artefact's settings block rather than chosen: `--k 64`, `--auxk 192`, `--steps 20000`, `--batch-size 8`, `--eval-sequences 256`, `--eval-every 2000`, `--learning-rate 2e-4`, `--weight-decay 1e-5`, `--grad-clip 1.0`, `--seed 20260806`, `--corpus-seed 20260806`, `--max-tokens 512`, OpenWebText at the stage's own 800-character floor. **The certificate is `compare_matched_training`'s `disagreements` list, and it must read exactly `["d_hidden"]` for all six pairs.** The verdict itself will read `MISMATCH` in every pair and that is correct rather than a failure: `d_hidden` is a member of `MATCHED_TRAINING_FIELDS`, so a width sweep cannot certify `MATCHED` by construction, and the list of what disagreed is the object that carries the claim. `training_token_budget` is undeclared in all four cells, exactly as in the F11-era run; because the four cells run identical steps, batch size, corpus and corpus seed, and the scored-token count per step depends only on the data, `training_tokens_relative_difference` must read **0.0** across every pair — an equal-data certificate verified after the fact rather than asserted by a flag.

**A confound direction declared now, because it runs the way that makes the interesting outcome harder.** At a fixed token budget a narrower dictionary is **better** trained per latent, not worse: ~72.7 M scored tokens over 12 layers gives **3,944 / 1,972 / 986 / 657** tokens per latent at 2x / 4x / 8x / 12x, against the 132 of F11's passing `gpt2-large` text control and the 154 that saturated ZymCTRL's dictionary in EXP-R2-153. So if 2x is negative it is negative **despite** being six times better trained per latent than the 12x cell that is known to pass, and undertraining is unavailable as an explanation of that cell. Conversely, if 2x is positive, part of the reason may be that it is better trained per latent, and outcome I below is weakened as a statement about width alone by exactly that amount.

**The estimator is the package's own and no second one is built.** Full-stack recovery is `_paired_recovery`: one index set of cohort sequences drawn with replacement per replicate shared by the clean, replacement and mean-ablated conditions, **1000 replicates**, a 2.5/97.5 percentile interval, a replicate discarded when its resampled denominator is not positive, and `bootstrap_unit_floor`'s **eight-unit floor**, which 128 cohort sequences clear, with the interval withheld rather than published if it ever does not. Scoring is `15_replacement_faithfulness.py --replacement-kind local --sequences 128 --batch-size 8 --seed 20260806 --bootstrap 1000 --cohort-draw-seed 20260728 --cohort-skip 0 --max-tokens 512 --replacement-front 1,2,4,8,12`, which is EXP-R2-188's `gpt2` dispatch verbatim.

**Numerator and denominator are reported in nats at every width, per Appendix B rule 27**, because a ratio whose denominator moves hides whichever direction a reader does not check. Here that reporting doubles as a specification check with a prediction: the clean and fully-ablated endpoints do not involve the dictionary, so **all four cells must return the identical clean and fully-ablated cross-entropy and therefore the identical denominator, to every digit**. Four cells that disagree on their denominator are not four widths of one comparison, and the run is void if they do.

**The setup was validated against an existing artefact before anything was trained, and it does not reproduce bit-exactly across platforms.** The F11-era `gpt2` dictionary (`d_hidden` 9216, `k` 64, seed 20260806) was re-scored on one L20 under the dispatch above. The **cohort digest is identical** to EXP-R2-188's H200 artefact (`2c9f8a8e…`), so the same 128 sequences are scored. Recovery reads **+0.9092511668955499** against the H200's **+0.9091401539331156** — an absolute deviation of **1.11e-4**, with clean, replacement and fully-ablated endpoints moving by 7.4e-4, 1.2e-3 and 1.8e-3 nats. That is bfloat16 kernel rounding between two GPU generations and is **not** a defect, but it is a declared bound on this campaign: **a cross-platform recovery difference below ~1e-3 is not resolvable here**, and no reading below that scale will be attempted. Within the L20 run the invariant that actually carries the sweep holds in its strongest form — the `k = 12` front row equals the headline `paired_per_sequence` recovery **and its interval bit-exactly**, point for point and digit for digit.

**What each outcome licenses, fixed now.** Per cell: **NEGATIVE** if the 95% paired interval lies entirely below zero, **POSITIVE** if entirely above, **UNRESOLVED** if it covers zero.

- **W — WIDTH ARTEFACT.** At least one width NEGATIVE while 12x is POSITIVE. Licensed: a negative full-stack recovery is something this dictionary recipe produces at a width, **on the text control**, which by the standing distinction makes it a property of the method rather than of protein models or of any checkpoint. EXP-R2-182's negative sign then stops being evidence about the joint checkpoint until width is controlled on that lineage. **Not licensed**: that width *is* the cause there. That lineage differs in backbone, in depth (32 against 12), in `k` (32 against 64), in tokens per latent, and in being joint at all, and this sweep varies none of them. If the sign is non-monotone in width — negative at some intermediate width and positive at both ends — that is still W and the non-monotonicity is reported as measured, on EXP-R2-186's Branch C convention.
- **I — WIDTH IS IRRELEVANT TO THE SIGN.** All four widths POSITIVE. Licensed: on this arm, at this depth, under this recipe, halving the expansion factor six-fold does not flip the sign, so **the most mundane explanation of EXP-R2-182 is removed as a sufficient one** and the joint result needs something else — backbone, depth, `k`, joint training, or an interaction among them. **This is a useful negative and will be reported as one, not as a failed experiment**: it makes the joint result more interesting, not less. Not licensed: that width is irrelevant *there*, since a sufficient-cause test on one arm cannot exclude width as one term of an interaction on another.
- **V — VOID.** The 12x cell is NEGATIVE, or lands further than **0.02** from the arm's own published +0.9091 in either direction. Then the recipe reproduction has failed and this is **a defect in this setup, reported as such and not as a finding**. 0.02 is deliberately loose against the 0.0007 that separates the arm's two published seeds, so that the condition catches breakage rather than variation.
- **U — UNRESOLVED.** Any width UNRESOLVED with no width NEGATIVE. Then this cohort at this size cannot separate that width's recovery from zero; the sign there is undetermined, no claim about width is licensed in either direction, and the intervals are published so a reader can see how much room is left.

**Cross-width separation is declared conservative in advance.** The four cells are four runs of the stage, so no paired interval across widths exists without building a second estimator, and none is built. Two widths separate only when their own 95% intervals do not overlap; non-separation is **UNRESOLVED and never "the same"**. Recovery at every front is reported too, since the front sweep is extra conditions of the same behavioural pass and costs one sweep each.

**Voiding conditions beyond V.** If any cell's `k = 12` front row fails to reproduce that cell's own headline recovery bit-exactly, the run is a specification defect and is voided — the invariant EXP-R2-186, EXP-R2-187 and EXP-R2-188 all turned on. If the four denominators disagree, the cells are not commensurable and the run is voided. If any `disagreements` list contains anything other than `d_hidden`, the sweep is not a width sweep and is voided.

**Bounds.** One arm, one seed per width, one cohort at one draw and no skip-offset condition, so nothing here prices dictionary-seed or cohort-draw variability; the 0.0007 between the arm's two published seeds is the only evidence it is small. Four widths on a doubling-and-a-half grid brackets any crossing to a factor of two at best. `k` is held at 64 throughout, so the sweep says nothing about the **2x with k 32** combination the R2.3 cells actually ran — width and sparsity are separate axes and only one moves here. 12 blocks, not 32, so depth is not varied and a width effect that only appears deep in a stack would be invisible. Behavioural recovery only: reconstruction NMSE is reported at every width because it comes free in the artefact and a width that moves one without the other is the informative pattern, but no claim rests on it, and the stage's 0.80 gate is not read — it is already known unattainable on text controls at some dictionary families, and no verdict here is a modality or method verdict.

**Compute, and it departs from the standing rule.** All of this runs on the **local L20 workstation**, eight cards at 46068 MiB, of which cards 0 and 2 are held by unrelated vLLM processes and six are free. `AGENTS.md` reserves the L20 for correctness verification and directs full campaigns to the H200; **the user has explicitly authorised lightweight training on the L20 for the time being because the H200 cluster has errored** (the same outage that paused EXP-R2-194). That authorisation is **temporary and specific**, and it is what scopes this experiment to a 124 M-parameter arm with four dictionaries of at most 170 M parameters each; it is not a precedent for running a panel campaign locally. No pod was contacted and none may be. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for both stages used here, as it did for EXP-R2-188, EXP-R2-190, EXP-R2-192 and EXP-R2-194; nothing here is dispatched through the registered stage path. Resolved paths were printed before dispatch, per the standing check that one environment variable once narrowed a campaign's text side to a single model: `TRANSFER_TEXT_MODEL_BASE_DIR=/Data/public` resolves `gpt2` and every GPT-2 rung, and the OpenWebText corpus resolves to its screened local copy. Results land under `results/transfer/width_sweep/`.
## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-196 pre-registered: F12's surviving half against the strongest fragment channel this corpus can support. Frozen before any higher-order count is read

**What is being tested, and why it is the most direct available threat to a claim this programme has just promoted.** F12's verdict is negative, but its surviving half carries real weight in the argument: on a certified corpus-disjoint referent ProtGPT2 **beats** both fragment-level corpus baselines — MODEL − `fragment_markov_k3` = **+0.1439 [+0.1070, +0.1784]** and MODEL − `fragment_markov_k4` = **+0.1270 [+0.0923, +0.1599]** over 40 design series — and beats corpus composition (+0.1261 [+0.0827, +0.1681]), so its margin over corpus statistics survives the exclusion of retrieval. That half rests entirely on two channels, and both are **maximum-likelihood conditionals at k = 3 and k = 4**. A 3-mer or 4-mer Markov model is a weak model of corpus statistics; F12's own bounds say so in terms — *"a 3-mer/4-mer conditional is one fragment-level channel and a longer-range corpus statistic is unpriced"*. This entry freezes the measurement that prices it. If a stronger fragment channel beats the model on the designs, F12's surviving half weakens or fails and has to be re-scoped, and finding that here is a better outcome than someone else finding it later.

**What already exists, and is therefore not evidence for anything below.** The seven contrasts of EXP-R2-192 on both sides for all four arms, in `results/transfer/designed_referent/designed_referent.json`; the per-wild-type Spearman values in `baselines.json` and the four `model_<arm>.json` artefacts from the pinned scoring pass at commit `2d8a1f27`; and the corrected record-local k-mer background at k = 3 and k = 4 (17,154,643,378 and 17,093,475,529 windows over 17,277,105,157 residues and 60,315,044 records). **Nothing at k ≥ 5 exists anywhere**, no held-out estimate of any fragment model exists anywhere, and no contrast below has been computed in any form. One thing has been looked at and is disclosed rather than omitted: a **1 GB prefix** of the corpus was counted to size the compute, and reported 3,196,936 of 3,200,000 5-mers and 54,924,824 of 64,000,000 6-mers observed in it. That is a file-order read of a sorted FASTA, it is the hazard rule 2 exists for, and **nothing in this entry or its reading uses it** — every number below comes from the full-corpus pass and the seeded held-out draws.

**The channel, declared in full before it is built.** For each order k and each declared smoothing scheme s, `fragment_interp_k{k}_{s}` is the conditional sequence model `P(x_t | x_{t-k+1..t-1})` over the **corrected record-local** corpus counts, with three properties fixed now:

1. *Every position is scored.* Position t is scored against the `min(t-1, k-1)` residues before it, so the channel is a proper normalised distribution over whole sequences and no leading residue is dropped. EXP-R2-192's `fragment_markov_k3`/`k4` omit the first k−1 emissions; that convention and the order are two changes, so **both existing channels are recomputed under the new convention and reported beside the old ones**, and a discrepancy there is attributed to the convention rather than to the order.
2. *The counts are verified by total and by digest.* The higher-order pass must reproduce the pinned k = 3 and k = 4 totals exactly, and `require_corrected_background` refuses the superseded line-local totals (16,640,807,917 / 16,324,342,706) by number rather than by path. Beyond that the run refuses to proceed unless the new pass's k = 3 and k = 4 count vectors are **byte-identical** to the pinned ones by SHA-256 — a stronger check than the total, and the one that makes the new orders a strict extension of F12's own background rather than a second opinion about it.
3. *k = 7 is a ceiling, not a preference.* A dense k = 8 count vector is 25.6 G cells, 204 GB, so seven is the highest order this representation holds. If the corpus still supports order 7 the reading says so and stops there.

**Smoothing is a design decision, declared here and not tuned.** A higher-order conditional cannot be maximum-likelihood — an unobserved k-mer is a log-likelihood of minus infinity, and unobserved k-mers exist at k ≥ 5 — so the channel needs interpolation, and the scheme changes its strength. **Two schemes, both parameter-free given the corpus, and both reported at every order; neither is a fallback for the other and the better-performing one is not selected afterwards.**

- **`kneser_ney`** — interpolated Kneser–Ney. Discount `D = n1 / (n1 + 2 n2)` from each table's own count-of-counts (Chen–Goodman), lower orders scored on continuation counts `N1+(. w)` taken from the next-higher order's table.
- **`witten_bell`** — interpolate order j with order j−1 at weight `D(c) / (N(c) + D(c))`, `D(c)` the distinct continuations of the context and `N(c)` its total count.

Both recurse to a unigram and then to uniform, so every conditional is strictly positive; the run raises rather than returning a zero probability, because a channel that can return minus infinity is not usable as a likelihood and would silently rank variants by which of them contains an unseen k-mer.

**How far k may go is measured, not chosen, and the estimator is held out rather than plug-in.** Plug-in perplexity falls with the order by construction and would license any order at all. So: **60,314 records — two disjoint draws of 0.05% each — are marked under a seeded uniform draw consumed in corpus order (seed 20260813) and removed from the counts.** Not a prefix: a FASTA is sorted and its first records are not its typical ones, which is the hazard that has manufactured an effect in this programme three times. Removal is exact rather than approximate: no window spans a record, so counts are additive over records and the training counts are the corpus counts minus the held-out counts, verified non-negative. Held-out records are evaluated as their **canonical-residue runs**, which is exactly the window rule the counter counted under. Then, declared before any curve exists:

> **Order k is SUPPORTED when held-out per-residue cross-entropy at k is strictly below its value at k − 1, on both held-out draws and under both smoothing schemes. The highest supported order is the largest k for which that holds at every step up to k. Admissible scoring orders are 3 through that order.**

This reads a turning point and not a cut, so it introduces no threshold to sweep. **Two draws rather than one** is this entry's sensitivity report on the corpus sample: a cross-entropy that moves between two independent draws of the same corpus is telling the reader the estimate is not settled. Contrasts are computed at **every** order from 3 to 7 regardless, so the admissibility decision cannot be influenced by any contrast; orders past the turn are reported as labelled diagnostics and **cannot change the verdict in either direction**.

**The contrast is EXP-R2-192's, unchanged, so the new channels drop into the existing comparison.** Per wild type, the Spearman correlation between the channel's summed log-likelihood of a variant and that variant's `ddG_ML`; MODEL − CHANNEL over the wild types both channels can be read on; averaged within unit and resampled through `profiles.cluster_bootstrap` at its declared **2,000** replicates under `statistics.bootstrap_unit_floor`'s **8-unit floor**, 95% percentile rule, **seed 20260813**. Unit: the design series on side (a), the dataset's own `WT_cluster` on side (b). The cohort is EXP-R2-192's frozen one, checked by digest before anything is read: **(a) 130 certified zero-hit designs, 40 series, 110,730 variants; (b) 266 natural domains, 124 clusters, 404,114 variants.** Both sides are re-tested, because a fragment channel that beats the model everywhere is a statement about the channel and one that beats it only on designs is a statement about the referent.

**One cohort fact decides how the two sides may be read, and it is recorded now rather than after the numbers.** EXP-R2-190's certificate is asymmetric by construction: **328 of 330 natural domains have a UniRef50 homologue at the gate and 132 of 148 designs have none.** So as the order rises the channel becomes, on side (b), progressively a **lookup of sequences the corpus contains**, and on side (a) it cannot, because the referent is certified disjoint. A high-order channel gaining ground on the natural side is therefore expected and uninformative about corpus *statistics*; **the design side is the only side on which a high-order fragment channel is a fragment channel rather than a retrieval channel**, and it is the side the verdict is taken on.

**The verdict, on ProtGPT2, on side (a), over the admissible orders, under both schemes.**

- **STANDS** — every admissible order under both schemes has its 95% series-clustered interval on MODEL − CHANNEL wholly above zero.
- **WEAKENED** — at some admissible order and scheme the interval covers zero: the margin over the strongest supported fragment channel is no longer demonstrable, though the channel does not beat the model.
- **OVERTURNED** — at some admissible order and scheme the interval lies wholly **below** zero. The reading is then qualified by side (b): if the channel beats the model there too, the finding is a statement about the channel; if it beats the model only on the designs, it is a statement about the referent.
- **UNRESOLVED** — the corpus supports no order beyond the two F12 already used, or a side falls below the eight-unit floor.

**The sparsity diagnostics sit beside every result and gate nothing.** Per order and per side: scored positions, positions at full order, the fraction whose (k−1)-residue context is unseen in the corpus, and the fraction whose full k-mer is unseen; plus corpus coverage at every order. They are how a reader sees whether the channel was still a model at that k — a channel whose contexts are all unseen has backed off and is not the order it is labelled, and a channel whose k-mers are all seen verbatim is a lookup. Making them a gate would require a threshold that the turning-point rule above already makes unnecessary, so they are reported and not applied.

**Arms, and what may be read from each.** All four EXP-R2-192 arms are computed. The **verdict is taken on ProtGPT2 alone**, because F12's surviving half is a claim about corpus statistics and ProtGPT2's declared pretraining corpus *is* the counted database; the ProGen2 rungs saw BFD30, which is neither staged nor counted, so a fragment channel built on UniRef50 alone is an incomplete model of what those arms read and their rows are bounds in the direction that flatters the model, exactly as in F12.

**What this cannot touch, stated now so no reading of it drifts.** Nothing here bears on EXP-R2-193's interaction, on the composition non-overlap that bounds it, on the per-arm corpus identification, or on the hydropathy and BLOSUM62 failures that produce F12's negative verdict — those rest on free baselines that need no corpus. This adjudicates **no mechanism**: it asks whether the model's margin over corpus fragment statistics survives a stronger measurement of those statistics, not why. The corpus is UniRef50 and fragment statistics are one family of corpus statistics; a channel of a different shape — profile, alignment-free embedding, longer-range dependency — remains unpriced whatever this returns. One file, one proteolysis assay, one phenotype, the same 40 design series F12 rests on.

**Compute.** **Zero GPU, no pod, CPU-only on B.** Every model likelihood already exists as a per-wild-type Spearman in the four pinned `model_<arm>.json` artefacts; the only new computation is the corpus pass, the held-out draws and the contrasts. Two new stages in `scripts/transfer/29_designed_referent.py` writing `data/kmer_background/uniref50_high_order/`, `data/kmer_background/uniref50_holdout/` and `results/transfer/designed_referent/fragment_order.json`; the model itself is in `src/transfer/designed_referent.py`. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for this work, as it did for EXP-R2-188, EXP-R2-190, EXP-R2-192 and EXP-R2-193; nothing here is dispatched per arm. The H200 cluster is errored and was not contacted. Resolved paths are printed before every stage, per the standing check that one environment variable once narrowed a campaign's text side to a single model: no `TRANSFER_*` override is set in this environment, so the pinned background resolves to `data/kmer_background/uniref50` and the corpus to `data/uniref50/uniref50.fasta`.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-196 read: F12's surviving half STANDS against every fragment channel this corpus can hold — and the margin it survives by is three times smaller than F12 reports, with no turning point reached

**What was run, exactly as pre-registered above.** The staged UniRef50 recounted at k = 1 through 7 in one record-local pass, **4,879 s of CPU**, reproducing the pinned pass's 17,277,105,157 residues and 60,315,044 records and the corrected totals **17,154,643,378** (k = 3) and **17,093,475,529** (k = 4) exactly; the k = 3 and k = 4 count vectors are **byte-identical by SHA-256** to the pinned EXP-R2-192 background, which the stage refuses to run without, so the new orders are a strict extension of F12's own background rather than a second opinion about it. 60,073 records — two disjoint 0.05% draws under a seeded uniform mark consumed in corpus order, never a prefix — were held out, 8,459,199 and 8,662,306 residues, and the training counts are the corpus counts minus theirs, exactly and checked non-negative. **Zero GPU, no pod**: every model likelihood is the per-wild-type Spearman from EXP-R2-192's pinned pass at commit `2d8a1f27`, checked against the cohort digest before anything was read. The analysis itself is 8.5 minutes of CPU. `results/transfer/designed_referent/fragment_order.json`; counts under `data/kmer_background/uniref50_high_order/` and `data/kmer_background/uniref50_holdout/`.

**Where k turns: it does not, and that is the reading's main limitation rather than a footnote.** Held-out per-residue cross-entropy on natural sequence the counts do not contain falls **monotonically to the end of the range**, on both draws and under both declared schemes:

| nats/residue | k=1 | k=2 | k=3 | k=4 | k=5 | k=6 | k=7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kneser–Ney, draw a | 2.89146 | 2.88486 | 2.87733 | 2.86825 | 2.85491 | 2.83547 | **2.81793** |
| Kneser–Ney, draw b | 2.89012 | 2.88345 | 2.87622 | 2.86768 | 2.85519 | 2.83672 | **2.81816** |

The two independent draws agree to the third decimal at every order, so the estimate is settled and the sensitivity the sampling rule requires is reported rather than assumed. The declared rule therefore returns **`highest_supported_order` = 7 and `turned_at` = null**, and **every order 3 through 7 is admissible**. That is a *ceiling of the representation, not of the corpus*: a dense k = 8 count vector is 25.6 G cells and 204 GB, so the pass could not be run, and this entry cannot say where the fragment channel stops being a model. It can only say it had not stopped by k = 7. **The gains are also still accelerating, not flattening** — the per-order drop is 0.0075, 0.0091, 0.0133, 0.0194, 0.0175 nats — which is the shape of a curve that has not yet turned.

> **Correction, 2026-08-13, to the sentence immediately above — found by the agent placing the F12 amendment and checked against this entry's own table.** "The gains are also still accelerating, not flattening" is contradicted by the numbers printed beside it. The five per-order drops quoted are **Kneser-Ney draw a's**, and its last is *smaller* than its previous — **0.01754 against 0.01944**; draw b's rises by 8 x 10^-5, **0.01855 against 0.01847**, which is flat. Only Witten-Bell accelerates at the final step, 0.02548 against 0.01950 on draw a and 0.02631 against 0.01853 on draw b. So acceleration holds under one declared scheme and not the other, and the sentence asserted it of both. **Corrected statement.** The fall is **monotone through k = 7 on both draws under both schemes**, and the per-order gain at the top of the range is **2.3 to 3.6 times** the gain at k = 3 — 0.01754/0.00753 and 0.01855/0.00723 under Kneser-Ney, 0.02548/0.00753 and 0.02631/0.00723 under Witten-Bell — with **no curve flattening**. The original sentence is left standing above so the error is visible rather than removed. **Nothing this entry concludes changes**: the turning-point rule still never fires, every order 3 through 7 is still admissible, the ceiling is still representational rather than empirical, and the k ~ 8.9 figure was already labelled an extrapolation past the last computable order and is untouched. The defect is in one sentence's reading of the table, not in the measurement — which is the shape this programme has now recorded twice, a summary clause beside a correct table being where an overstatement is hardest to see. The F12 amendment was written from the corrected form and carries no version of the original phrase.

**The channel is still a model at k = 7, by every diagnostic available.** Corpus coverage: all 3,200,000 5-mers observed, **63,951,885 of 64,000,000 6-mers (99.925%)**, and **1,100,135,017 of 1,280,000,000 7-mers (85.95%)** at a mean of 15.4 occurrences per observed 7-mer. On held-out natural sequence at k = 7, **5.4 × 10⁻⁶ of positions have an unseen 6-residue context** and 0.87% an unseen 7-mer, so the model is scoring at full order essentially everywhere rather than silently backing off. On the scored cohorts the same numbers are **0 unseen contexts and 0.431% unseen 7-mers on the designs, 1.9 × 10⁻⁷ and 0.354% on the natural control**. Every wild type was readable on every channel: 130 of 130 designs and 266 of 266 naturals, none dropped for a constant channel, at any order under either scheme.

**That last pair of numbers is the sharpest form of "alignment-free is not information-free" this programme has produced.** The 130 designs are certified to have no detectable UniRef50 homologue — and **99.57% of their scored 7-mers occur in UniRef50**, against 99.65% for natural domains scored identically. Fragment-level, the designs are not strangers to the corpus at all. The exclusion the certificate buys is an exclusion of *sequences*, and it was never an exclusion of *fragments*; this measures how little of the second it buys.

**The declared smoothing turned out not to matter, which is worth recording because it was the decision most open to abuse.** Kneser–Ney and Witten–Bell agree to four decimal places on every contrast at k ≤ 6 and differ in the third decimal at k = 7 (design side +0.0516 against +0.0508). Both were declared before scoring and both are reported; neither was selected. The choice that *would* have mattered had it been tuned is inert here.

**The result, on ProtGPT2, on both sides, at every admissible order.** MODEL − CHANNEL, 40 design series and 124 `WT_cluster`s, `profiles.cluster_bootstrap` at 2,000 replicates under the 8-unit floor, seed 20260813 — EXP-R2-192's procedure, unchanged.

(Kneser–Ney rows; Witten–Bell is identical to four decimals except k = 7, +0.0508 [+0.0208, +0.0796] and +0.1620 [+0.1317, +0.1912].) The two ML rows **reproduce F12's published numbers exactly**, which is what licenses reading the rest of the table against it. The convention change alone — scoring every position instead of dropping the first k−1 emissions — moves the contrast by **+0.015** at fixed k, in the direction that *flatters* the model, while the order moves it by **−0.107**; so the order effect is seven times the convention effect and the two are not confounded.

**Verdict: STANDS, under the rule frozen before any of these numbers existed.** Ten channels — five orders by two schemes — and ProtGPT2's series-clustered interval lies wholly above zero on the corpus-disjoint designs on every one of them. No admissible channel beats the model; none leaves the margin undemonstrated. F12's surviving half is not refuted, and the attempt to refute it was a real one: the channel it now survives is a proper normalised sequence model at more than twice the order, built on counts an order of magnitude sparser, and scored on every residue.

**What the attempt did establish is that the margin is three times smaller than F12 reports and is still falling where the measurement had to stop.** +0.1590 → +0.1453 → +0.1113 → +0.0792 → +0.0516: monotone, with per-order steps of −0.014, −0.034, −0.032, −0.028 that have not begun to flatten. A linear fit over k ∈ [3, 7] reaches zero at **k ≈ 8.9** — an *extrapolation past the last order that could be computed*, offered as the shape of the trend and not as a result, since neither the contrast nor the held-out curve exists at k = 8. **So the honest statement is not "the margin survives corpus statistics" but "the margin survives every fragment channel that fits in memory, by a margin that shrinks by two thirds across the orders that do".** The control side decays too — +0.3435 to +0.1661, by 52% — so part of the decay is the channel simply getting better and not anything about the referent; but the design-side margin decays by 68% and, unlike the control's, is the one approaching zero.

**The three ProGen2 rows are bounds and two of them have already crossed.** Their design-side margins at k = 7: `progen2-base` **+0.0135 [−0.0109, +0.0400]**, `progen2-medium` **−0.0041 [−0.0280, +0.0198]**, `progen2-small` **−0.0421 [−0.0718, −0.0116]**. So on the arm whose corpus is *not* identified and whose F12 design side is *not read at all* under the frozen rule, an order-7 UniRef50 fragment channel beats the model outright; on ProGen2-medium the margin F12 reports has vanished into its interval. **None of this is read as a result about those models**, for two reasons that run in opposite directions and neither of which is resolved here: their corpora include BFD30, which was neither staged nor counted, so a UniRef50 channel is an incomplete model of the statistics they actually saw — which makes it *weaker* than their true corpus channel and their rows correspondingly generous — while the retrieval certificate is likewise unidentified for them, which runs the other way. The verdict is taken on ProtGPT2 alone, as pre-registered, and it is taken there because that arm's declared pretraining corpus *is* the counted database.

**Bounds.** **The turning point was not found**, so nothing here says the k = 7 channel is the strongest fragment channel the corpus supports — only the strongest one a dense count vector can hold, and the held-out curve was still falling at that point. The trend past k = 7 is an extrapolation and is labelled as one. Fragment statistics are one family of corpus statistics: a profile channel, an alignment-free embedding, or any longer-range dependency remains unpriced whatever this returns, and a channel that is not a fixed-order Markov model is not bounded by the order argument at all. The natural control's domains are in the counted corpus by construction — 328 of 330 hit at the certificate's gate — so as k rises that side's channel becomes progressively a lookup and its margin is not comparable with the design side's; the design side is the only one on which a high-order fragment channel is a fragment channel, which is why the verdict is taken there. One corpus, one file, one proteolysis assay, one phenotype, the same 40 design series F12 rests on, and the same four arms. **Nothing here touches F12's other findings**: the hydropathy and BLOSUM62 failures that produce its negative verdict rest on free baselines that need no corpus, EXP-R2-193's interaction is a within-arm difference under one such baseline, the composition non-overlap that bounds it is untouched, and the per-arm corpus identification is unchanged. No mechanism is adjudicated. `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` are not modified here; F12's fragment-baseline clause now has a measured order dependence and a stated ceiling that the register does not carry, and that is proposed to the coordinator rather than written.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-197: EXP-R2-195 read — OUTCOME I. Width does not flip the sign. Recovery is positive at every expansion from 2x to 12x, and the most mundane explanation of the joint checkpoint's negative sign is removed

*Numbered 197 rather than 195 because EXP-R2-196 was appended by another agent while these four dictionaries were training; the pre-declaration this reads against is EXP-R2-195, thirty lines above, and nothing in it was altered after the first training step.*

**The verdict, against the rule frozen before any dictionary existed: OUTCOME I — WIDTH IS IRRELEVANT TO THE SIGN.** All four widths are POSITIVE on the pre-declared criterion, the 95% paired interval lying entirely above zero, and the curve is monotone increasing in width with no reversal anywhere.

| expansion | `d_hidden` | clean | replacement | fully ablated | numerator | denominator | recovery | 95% paired interval | sign |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **2x** | 1536 | 3.116290 | 4.159622 | 9.470033 | 5.310411 | 6.353742 | **+0.835793** | [+0.827111, +0.843057] | POSITIVE |
| **4x** | 3072 | 3.116290 | 3.910098 | 9.470033 | 5.559935 | 6.353742 | **+0.875065** | [+0.868310, +0.880900] | POSITIVE |
| **8x** | 6144 | 3.116290 | 3.753509 | 9.470033 | 5.716524 | 6.353742 | **+0.899710** | [+0.893808, +0.904659] | POSITIVE |
| **12x** | 9216 | 3.116290 | 3.695865 | 9.470033 | 5.774168 | 6.353742 | **+0.908782** | [+0.903320, +0.913146] | POSITIVE |

Numerator is `fully_ablated − replacement` and denominator `fully_ablated − clean`, both in nats per token, so the ratio can be checked rather than trusted. **The denominator does not move at all**: it is the same 6.353742 in all four cells, as the pre-declaration predicted it must, because neither endpoint involves the dictionary.

**Nothing about this is marginal, and the margin is the result.** The narrowest dictionary is the one that would have to go negative for the width hypothesis to survive, and at 2x the replacement sits **5.31 nats below** the mean-ablation endpoint rather than above it. Its interval's lower bound is **104 interval half-widths above zero**. Halving the expansion factor six-fold costs **0.073 in recovery**, about 8% of the 12x value; producing a negative sign would require losing twelve times that much again. The gain per halving also *shrinks* toward the wide end and grows toward the narrow one — −0.0091 from 12x to 8x, −0.0246 from 8x to 4x, −0.0393 from 4x to 2x — so the curve is bending, not diverging; no extrapolation past 2x is offered and none is licensed, because below 1x a dictionary narrower than the residual stream is a different object.

**The matched certificate, all six pairs.** Every pair returns `disagreements` exactly `['d_hidden']`, `training_tokens_relative_difference` exactly **0.000e+00**, and `max_tokens_agree` true. The verdict field reads `MISMATCH` in all six and that is correct rather than a failure: `d_hidden` is itself a member of `MATCHED_TRAINING_FIELDS`, so a width sweep cannot certify `MATCHED` by construction, and the disagreement list is what carries the claim. The four cells consumed **72,971,083 scored tokens each — the identical integer**, which is the equal-data certificate the undeclared token budget could not supply: the trainer's realised count depends only on the corpus, the corpus seed, the step count and the batch size, and all four held those fixed. The certificate was computed outside the stage with `compare_matched_training` itself; `15_replacement_faithfulness.py --matched-against` was deliberately not used, because it records one pair per run rather than six and would have recorded `MISMATCH` without adding anything.

**Every specification check passes, including the two the pre-declaration made voiding conditions.** The clean cross-entropy is `3.116290476173` and the fully-ablated `9.470032915473` in all four cells, identical to twelve decimals, and the cohort digest is identical across all four and equal to the anchor's. In every cell the `k = 12` front row reproduces that cell's own headline recovery **and its interval bit-exactly**. All four cells retained **1000 of 1000** bootstrap replicates, and 128 cohort sequences clear the eight-unit floor, so no interval was withheld.

**The 12x cell reproduces the arm's published result, and by a margin smaller than the arm's own seed spread.** Freshly trained under this recipe it recovers **+0.9087821175** against F11's published **+0.9091401539** — a difference of **0.000358**, against a pre-declared void threshold of 0.02 and against the **0.0007** that separates the arm's two published dictionary seeds. Its training curve tracked the F11-era run throughout: 62,180 dead latents at step 2000 against that run's 62,311, and a final held-out NMSE sum of 2.3322 against 2.3291. So the recipe was reproduced, not approximated, and outcome V does not apply.

**The harness was validated against an existing artefact before any of this was trained, and the one deviation is platform numerics.** Re-scoring the F11-era 12x dictionary itself on an L20 gives **+0.9092511669 [+0.9037723480, +0.9136506006]** against the H200 artefact's **+0.9091401539 [+0.9036567256, +0.9136063982]** — the same cohort by digest, differing by **1.11e-4** in recovery and 7.4e-4 to 1.8e-3 nats in the endpoints. That is bfloat16 kernel rounding between two GPU generations, it is four orders of magnitude below the effect this experiment was built to detect, and it is recorded as a declared resolution bound rather than treated as a finding. Within any single L20 run the deepest-front identity is exact.

**Cross-width separation, on the conservative non-overlap criterion declared in advance.** 2x separates from 4x, 8x and 12x; 4x separates from 8x and 12x; **8x against 12x is UNRESOLVED** at +0.009072, which says this cohort at this size cannot separate them and never that they are equal. So width does move recovery, materially and monotonically, and the sweep resolves that movement everywhere except at its flattest step — but it moves it entirely within the positive regime.

**Two things transfer from the earlier series and both hold at every width.** The depth curve is **monotone falling at every one of the four widths** — all **forty** ordered front pairs across the four cells return DECREASE, none UNRESOLVED and none INCREASE, which is ten per cell, every ordered pair over the five fronts 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12 — so EXP-R2-188's OUTCOME N on this arm is width-invariant and its non-monotonicity remains a property of the joint checkpoint rather than of prefix replacement. And the portable statement survives too: at a one-block front recovery is **0.9949, 0.9966, 0.9977 and 0.9983** at 2x through 12x, so "a single replaced block recovers nearly all of the mean-ablation gap, and the damage is a property of composition" now holds at four expansion factors on this arm as well as across five checkpoints.

**Reconstruction and behaviour move together here, and the sizes differ.** Reconstruction NMSE summed over 12 layers, measured on the scoring cohort, is 3.6035 / 2.9761 / 2.5396 / 2.3537 from 2x to 12x, and the training held-out figures agree at 3.5804 / 2.9534 / 2.5185 / 2.3322. So the 2x dictionary reconstructs **53% worse** than the 12x one and recovers only **8% less** behaviourally. Recovery is far less sensitive to width than reconstruction is — which is the reason the width hypothesis was worth testing and also the reason it failed.

**Undertraining is not available as an alternative reading of the narrow cells, and the direction was declared in advance.** At a fixed 72,971,083-token budget the narrow dictionaries are *better* trained per latent, not worse: **3,959 / 1,979 / 990 / 660** tokens per latent from 2x to 12x, the last of which reproduces F11's published 660 for this arm exactly. Every cell sits above the 132 of F11's passing `gpt2-large` control and above the 154 that saturated ZymCTRL's dictionary in EXP-R2-153. The 2x cell is the best-trained dictionary in the sweep by this measure and still the worst performer, so its lower recovery is a width effect and not a data effect. The converse qualification declared in advance also stands: because narrow cells are better trained per latent, part of why 2x remains positive may be that advantage, which weakens this as a statement about width *alone* by exactly that amount.

**What this settles, and what it explicitly does not.** It settles that **this dictionary recipe does not produce a negative full-stack recovery at any expansion from 2x to 12x on `gpt2`**, and by the standing distinction a limitation demonstrated on the text control would have been a property of the method — so the absence of one is informative in the same register. **The most mundane candidate explanation of EXP-R2-182's four negative cells is therefore removed as a sufficient one**, and this is a useful negative rather than a failed experiment: it makes the joint checkpoint's negative sign harder to explain away, not easier. **It does not settle the joint checkpoint's attribution.** EXP-R2-194 is the frozen comparison that does, on that lineage, and it remains paused on the errored cluster; neither result may be read as having settled the other. Nothing here reaches `ProLLaMA_Stage_1`, whose cells differ in backbone, in depth (32 blocks against 12), in `k` (32 against 64), in tokens per latent, and in being a joint checkpoint at all. What survives on the shortlist after this run is everything except width acting alone.

**One arithmetic point that bounds the transfer of this result more sharply than "different backbone" does.** "2x expansion" is not one recipe across backbones. At `d_model` 4096 with `k` 32 the joint cells' 2x dictionary holds 8,192 latents per layer at an active fraction of **0.391%**; at `d_model` 768 with `k` 64 this sweep's 2x cell holds 1,536 at **4.167%**, and even its widest, the **12x** cell, sits at **0.694%**. **The joint cells' 2x dictionary is therefore sparser in active fraction than every cell in this sweep, including the widest one.** So on the axis that plausibly matters for whether a spliced dictionary can carry a block's computation, the joint cells are outside this sweep's range entirely rather than at its narrow end. This is the single strongest reason not to read outcome I as covering them.

**Bounds.** One arm, one dictionary seed per width, one cohort at one draw and no skip-offset condition, so nothing here prices dictionary-seed or cohort-draw variability; the 0.0007 between this arm's two published seeds is the only evidence it is small. Four widths on a 2/4/8/12 grid, so any crossing is bracketed to a factor of two at best and none was observed. `k` is fixed at 64 throughout, which means expansion and active fraction are inversely coupled by construction — a width sweep at fixed `k` cannot be a sparsity sweep, and the 2x-with-`k`-32 combination the R2.3 cells actually ran is untested here. Twelve blocks, not thirty-two, so a width effect that only appears deep in a stack would be invisible. **Only the text side was swept, so nothing here bears on whether F11's text-versus-protein replacement separation is width-robust**: no protein arm was rebuilt at any other expansion, and reading a width-invariant positive sign on one text arm as evidence for the separation's robustness would be the most likely misuse of this run. Behavioural recovery only; the stage's 0.80 gate was not read and every cell's causal `mlp_block` family FAILs exactly as the F11-era `gpt2` cell does, which is a known property of this arm's artefacts and carries no modality or method verdict. The cross-platform anchor bounds this campaign's resolution at ~1e-3 against any published H200 number, and no reading below that scale was attempted.

**Compute and operational record.** Entirely on the **local L20 workstation** under the user's explicit and **temporary** authorisation of lightweight training there while the H200 cluster is errored — a deliberate departure from the standing rule in `AGENTS.md` that reserves the L20 for correctness verification, and not a precedent for local panel campaigns. Cards 0 and 2 were held throughout by unrelated vLLM processes and were never touched; the four training cells took cards 3 to 6, one each, and each cell was scored on its own card as its checkpoint landed. No pod was contacted. Resolved paths were printed before dispatch per the standing check: `TRANSFER_TEXT_MODEL_BASE_DIR=/Data/public` resolves `gpt2` and every GPT-2 rung — the declared default `~/text_models` does **not** exist on this host and would have failed the loader, which is the narrowing hazard caught before rather than after. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for both stages, as recorded for EXP-R2-188, 190, 192 and 194. Wall clock was about two and a half hours from first training step to last artefact, the 12x cell dominating it. Artefacts under `results/transfer/width_sweep/`: four `s15_gpt2_d*/`, the four dictionaries in `dicts/`, and `anchor_gpt2_d9216_f11/` for the harness validation. `docs/INTERPRETABILITY_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md` and `summary.md` are not modified here; D2.h's shortlist of candidate explanations for EXP-R2-182 now has width removed as a sufficient one, and that change is proposed to the coordinator rather than written.

**Correction, 2026-08-13, made in place and marked because the wrong figure had already been quoted onward.** The front-pair count in the transfer paragraph above originally read **twenty-four** and is **forty**. The fronts are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12, so each cell carries every ordered pair over five rows — C(5, 2) = 10 — and four cells carry 40; the `steps` array in each artefact holds exactly 10 entries, 40 in total, every one DECREASE with none UNRESOLVED and none INCREASE. **The claim is unaffected and rests on more pairs than were stated**, so this is a correction of coverage understated rather than of a result overstated. It is recorded rather than silently amended for one reason beyond the arithmetic: **EXP-R2-188's analogous figure of 73 ordered pairs is correct**, so an undercount here would have read as a genuine difference in coverage between the two entries a reader compares first. The audit narrowing was written from the corrected figure and carries forty.

## 2026-08-13 — EXP-R2-198 pre-declared: does the SIGN of full-stack replacement recovery go negative on a TEXT control at the joint cells' active fraction? A sparsity sweep at fixed width on `gpt2`, frozen before any dictionary is trained

Frozen before the first training step of the six new cells. The seventh cell is reused unchanged from EXP-R2-195 and is named below rather than retrained.

**The question, and it is the axis EXP-R2-197's own bound identified.** EXP-R2-197 excluded dictionary width as a sufficient explanation of EXP-R2-182's four negative cells, and then recorded what that sweep could not reach: **"2x expansion" is not one recipe across backbones.** At `d_model` 4096 with `k` 32 the joint cells run at an active fraction of **0.390625%**, sparser than *every* cell of that sweep including its widest at 0.694%; and because `k` was fixed at 64 there, expansion and sparsity were inversely coupled by construction, so the sparsity axis was never varied at all. This run varies it directly: **`k` moves and width does not**, which isolates sparsity from capacity exactly as the previous sweep could not.

**The arm, and why it is `gpt2` and not the deeper candidate.** `gpt2` at fixed `d_hidden` 9216, because it fits the card and the budget and because at that width the joint checkpoint's active fraction is reached **exactly** at `k` 36 (36/9216 = 32/8192 = 0.390625%), giving an interior operating point rather than an interpolated one, on an arm whose F11-era positive result has already been reproduced twice. Its existing published recovery is **+0.9091401539 [+0.9036567256, +0.9136063982]** (EXP-R2-141 at seed 20260806, re-scored unchanged in EXP-R2-188), and EXP-R2-197's fresh retrain of that exact recipe landed at **+0.9087821175**, 0.000358 away. **`gpt2-large` was the better arm on depth and was rejected on measured cost, not on preference**: 36 blocks against the joint checkpoint's 32 would have varied the one remaining axis, but its F11-era dictionary took **31,749 s on an H200**, and this trainer's measured L20-to-H200 ratio is about 2.9x, so one cell is ~25 h locally and a seven-point sweep is ~50 h on the three free cards. **Depth therefore remains unvaried at 12 blocks and that is this run's principal structural bound**, recorded here rather than discovered later; `gpt2-large` is the natural follow-up when the cluster returns.

**The sweep. Seven active fractions, width fixed, `k` the only thing that moves.**

| `k` | active fraction | position |
|---:|---:|---|
| 384 | 4.166667% | exactly EXP-R2-195's 2x cell's active fraction, at 6x its width |
| 256 | 2.777778% | inside EXP-R2-195's range |
| 128 | 1.388889% | inside EXP-R2-195's range |
| **64** | **0.694444%** | the F11 anchor; **reused from EXP-R2-195, not retrained** |
| **36** | **0.390625%** | **exactly the joint cells' operating point** |
| 16 | 0.173611% | below it |
| 8 | 0.086806% | below it |

Three cells sit above the joint operating point, two below, so it is interior on both sides. Every other setting is the F11-era `gpt2` dictionary's own and identical to EXP-R2-195's: `--d-hidden 9216`, `--auxk 192`, `--steps 20000`, `--batch-size 8`, `--eval-sequences 256`, `--eval-every 2000`, `--learning-rate 2e-4`, `--weight-decay 1e-5`, `--grad-clip 1.0`, `--seed 20260806`, `--corpus-seed 20260806`, `--max-tokens 512`. **The certificate is `compare_matched_training`'s `disagreements` list over all 21 pairs, and it must read exactly `["k"]` every time.** The verdict field will read `MISMATCH` throughout and that is correct rather than a failure, for the same reason it was in EXP-R2-197: `k` is itself a member of `MATCHED_TRAINING_FIELDS`. `training_tokens` must again be the identical integer **72,971,083** in all seven cells — the 300-step probes at `k` 8 and `k` 384 already returned the identical 1,088,901, confirming that `k` does not change which tokens are scored — and `training_tokens_relative_difference` must be **0.000e+00** across every pair.

**A confound direction declared now, and it runs the OPPOSITE way from EXP-R2-197's.** Because width is fixed, the F11-style budget figure is **constant**: 72,971,083 tokens over 110,592 latents is **660 tokens per latent in every cell**, so the sweep cannot be read as a training-budget sweep the way a width sweep can. What does move, and moves 48-fold, is **how often each latent is actually updated**: latent activations per latent per layer run **3,040,462 / 2,026,975 / 1,013,487 / 506,744 / 285,043 / 126,686 / 63,343** from `k` 384 down to `k` 8. So a *low-`k` failure is consistent with sparsity and with per-latent undertraining at once, and this design cannot separate them.* In EXP-R2-197 the confound protected the interesting outcome — narrow cells were better trained per latent and still failed to go negative. **Here it does the reverse: it makes a negative result easier to obtain for an uninteresting reason**, which is precisely why it is written down before the numbers exist. Any NEGATIVE cell will be reported with this collinearity attached and will not be promoted past it. The dead-latent count is reported per cell for the same reason.

**The estimator is the package's own and no second one is built.** `_paired_recovery` — one index set of cohort sequences per replicate shared by the clean, replacement and mean-ablated conditions, **1000 replicates**, a 2.5/97.5 percentile interval, a replicate discarded when its resampled denominator is not positive, and `bootstrap_unit_floor`'s **eight-unit floor**, which 128 cohort sequences clear. Scoring is EXP-R2-188's `gpt2` dispatch verbatim, identical to EXP-R2-195's: `15_replacement_faithfulness.py --replacement-kind local --sequences 128 --batch-size 8 --seed 20260806 --bootstrap 1000 --cohort-draw-seed 20260728 --cohort-skip 0 --max-tokens 512 --replacement-front 1,2,4,8,12`. Numerator and denominator are reported in nats at every cell, and as before the clean and fully-ablated endpoints do not involve the dictionary, so **all seven cells must return the identical clean, fully-ablated and denominator values to every digit** — that is a specification check with a prediction, and cells that disagree on it are not seven sparsities of one comparison.

**What each outcome licenses, fixed now.** Per cell: **NEGATIVE** if the 95% paired interval lies entirely below zero, **POSITIVE** if entirely above, **UNRESOLVED** if it covers zero.

- **S — TEXT-CONTROL REPRODUCTION.** At least one cell at or below `k` 36 is NEGATIVE while the `k` 64 anchor is POSITIVE. Licensed: **a negative full-stack recovery is something this recipe produces on a text control at joint-like sparsity**, and by the standing distinction a limitation demonstrated on the text control is a property of the method rather than of protein models or of any checkpoint. That is a substantially larger finding than the joint cells alone can give and **will be held to a higher standard, not a lower one** — the confound paragraph above travels with it, and so does the fact that it would be a single arm at a single depth. **Not licensed**: that sparsity is the cause on the joint lineage. A sufficient-cause demonstration on one arm cannot settle an interaction on another, and `ProLLaMA_Stage_1` differs in backbone, in depth (32 blocks against 12), in width, in tokens per latent and in being a joint checkpoint at all. The frozen comparison that would settle the joint attribution is EXP-R2-194 and it remains paused.
- **P — SPARSITY IS IRRELEVANT TO THE SIGN.** All seven cells POSITIVE, including both below the joint operating point. Licensed: **sparsity joins width as excluded as a sufficient explanation**, on this arm at this depth, so the joint result becomes harder to explain away rather than easier and the shortlist narrows a second time. Not licensed: that sparsity is irrelevant *there*, for the same asymmetry.
- **V — VOID.** The `k` 64 anchor is NEGATIVE or lands further than **0.02** from the published +0.9091401539; or any cell's `k = 12` front row fails to reproduce that cell's own headline recovery bit-exactly; or the seven cells disagree on their clean, fully-ablated or denominator value; or any pair's `disagreements` list is not exactly `["k"]`. Then this is **a defect in the setup, reported as such and not as a finding**.
- **U — UNRESOLVED.** Any cell UNRESOLVED with none NEGATIVE. Then this cohort at this size cannot separate that cell from zero, the sign there is undetermined, and no claim about sparsity is licensed in either direction.

**One secondary reading, declared as secondary and unable to change the licence.** `k` 384 at `d_hidden` 9216 sits at **4.166667%**, which is exactly EXP-R2-195's 2x cell's active fraction at six times the width. The pair is therefore a free capacity-versus-sparsity contrast on one arm: if the two recover alike, active fraction is what EXP-R2-195 was really measuring; if the wide one recovers markedly better, capacity is. It is reported and nothing is built on it.

**Cross-cell separation is declared conservative in advance**, as before: seven runs of the stage, so no paired interval across cells exists without building a second estimator and none is built. Two cells separate only when their own 95% intervals do not overlap; non-separation is **UNRESOLVED and never "the same"**.

**Bounds.** One arm, one dictionary seed per cell, one cohort at one draw and no skip-offset condition. **Twelve blocks, not thirty-two** — the structural bound named above, and the one a reader should weigh first, since sequential replacement compounds with depth and a sparsity effect that only bites deep would be invisible here. Width is fixed at 9216, so this is not a joint width-and-sparsity map and the 2x-with-`k`-32 combination the R2.3 cells actually ran is still not reproduced — that cell differs from every cell here in width *and* backbone *and* depth. Seven points on a roughly doubling `k` grid brackets any crossing to a factor of about two. `auxk` is held at 192 throughout and exceeds `k` in the three sparsest cells, which is the same configuration the F11-era runs used at `k` 64 but is a larger ratio here; it is held fixed rather than tuned, and it is part of the recipe under test rather than a free parameter. Behavioural recovery only; the stage's 0.80 gate is not read and every cell's causal `mlp_block` family is expected to FAIL exactly as this arm's F11-era cell does, which carries no modality or method verdict. **Only the text side is swept, so nothing here will bear on whether F11's text-versus-protein replacement separation is sparsity-robust**: no protein arm is rebuilt at any active fraction, and that misuse is refused in advance here as it was in EXP-R2-197.

**Compute.** Local **L20** workstation under the user's explicit and **temporary** authorisation of lightweight training there while the H200 cluster is errored — the same departure from `AGENTS.md`'s standing reservation recorded in EXP-R2-195, and still not a precedent. Cards 0 and 2 hold unrelated vLLM processes and cards 3 to 5 are held by another agent's campaign; the six new cells take the three free cards in two rounds of three, and each is scored on its own card as its checkpoint lands. Measured at ~0.3 s/step in a 300-step probe at both `k` extremes, so about 2 h per cell and roughly 5 h for the campaign. No pod is contacted. Resolved paths are printed before dispatch: `TRANSFER_TEXT_MODEL_BASE_DIR=/Data/public` resolves `gpt2`, whose declared default `~/text_models` does not exist on this host. `arm_can_run` was consulted and raises `unknown stage` for both stages, as recorded for EXP-R2-188, 190, 192, 194 and 195. Results under `results/transfer/sparsity_sweep/`.
